Sports.title: Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut
Sports.content:
Sober Glory turned the tables on Supreme Novices’ Hurdle conqueror Old Park Star to make a faultless chasing bow in the Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners’ Chase at Ffos Las.

One of the most eagerly-anticipated showdowns of the early season as the dry spell forced the exciting duo to west Wales, the main protagonists were immediately to the fore with Philip Hobbs and Johnson White's Sober Glory the more sure-footed of the duo in the early exchanges.

There was little to separate the pair as a fine leap four out brought the Nico de Boinville-ridden Old Park Star alongside, but Ben Jones soon reclaimed the advantage in the home straight aboard the 5-4 second favourite.

With the gap growing all the way up the home straight, the Cheltenham Festival runner-up gained revenge over Nicky Henderson's 4-5 favourite, sauntering to an impressive nine-and-a-half length opening victory over fences.

Co-trainer White said: "It was a very pleasing performance jumping wise and there was a few novicey mistakes, but that is understandable for a first run over the bigger obstacles.

"I was delighted with the authority in which he won the race and he had a very good horse a good few lengths behind.

"His schooling has been very good all autumn, but you still have to go out and put that into practice on the course. Ben Jones says he's only going to get better with experience, but that has to be a very nice starting point.

"There is very few parts you could be disappointed with there. He's jumped well, travelled nicely and he's beaten good opposition so it's a very encouraging start to the season."

BOYLE Sports cut Sober Glory to 7-2 joint-favourite for the Arkle alongside Dan Skelton's Kabral du Mathan and while Hobbs and White will work a path back from that Cheltenham Festival event, they could clash early next month at Sandown in the Henry VIII Chase.

White added: "We'll get him home and reassess, but I think you have to aim at the Arkle and work back from there. Sandown would certainly be one of the races on the agenda along the way."

One horse who will not be in Esher on December 5 is Old Park Star after he faded into third, with Henderson left in "shock" after the six-year-old bled as his four-race winning streak came to an end.

"He's broken a blood vessel and bled so that explains it and it's a not just a bit of a shock, but a huge shock," said the Seven Barrows handler. "These things do happen, but we always just pray to God they don't but it has and it is as simple as that.

"It explains things but does create a massive headache. It's a blow when it happens to one like him and at the moment it is just a massive shock really.

"We'll get him back but he obviously won't be going to the Henry VIII which was the race we were trying to get him ready for. We've got the problem and now we have to try and resolve it - we will do our best."

Sports.title: Piastri to serve grid penalty at Las Vegas GP
Sports.content:
McLaren have confirmed that Oscar Piastri will serve a 10-place grid penalty at this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix as he will be forced to exceed his engine allowance for the season.

Following an unspecified reliability issue, Piastri will need to use his fifth Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) of the season, taking him beyond the limit of four that each driver has for the season.

A team statement said: "Oscar will take a new Internal Combustion Engine in Las Vegas after a reliability issue.

"As it is his fifth of the season, he will take a 10-place grid penalty, but he has a good chance to recover positions with overtaking in Saturday's race."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports F1 Show podcast, Zak Brown explains why Lando Norris outperformed Oscar Piastri in the 2026 car.

The Las Vegas Strip Circuit features a 1.2-mile straight that drivers take flat out, which should present a good opportunity for Piastri to surge back through the field.

McLaren also confirmed that both Piastri and his team-mate Lando Norris will have their cars fitted with a new turbo specification, which has been made available by the power unit supplier Mercedes following an engine upgrade.

"Both cars, as with the other HPP-powered cars, will be fitted with a new ADUO-enabled turbo specification," the team added. "The expected performance benefit is relatively small."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the F1 Show podcast, Zak Brown explains the reason why McLaren have 'no plans' to build their own engine in the future.

McLaren to bring new floor to Las Vegas

Despite there being just three rounds remaining of the 2026 season, McLaren will continue to upgrade their car with a new floor arriving in time for Las Vegas.

Having officially been dethroned as constructors' champions by Mercedes last time out in Brazil, McLaren are attempting to close down a 17-point deficit to Red Bull in the battle for third in this year's standings.

A McLaren statement said: "The team will bring further developments to the MCL40 as they continue to push to unlock more performance in the remaining races, primarily a new floor.

"We will also have some solutions to improve drag during the Free Practice sessions, which we will then review before making a decision on whether to run them on Friday.

"With plenty of opportunities to exploit the car's potential, both through evaluating the new upgrades and refining how to operate the package at the maximum potential available, the priority is to turn those learnings into performance on track and valuable points in the immediate term."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris wins the Sao Paulo GP ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

McLaren were the only member of F1's 'big four' teams to bring upgrades to Brazil, where the new parts helped Norris win the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Ross Hood, McLaren executive director of programme delivery, said: "Our programme delivery has evolved throughout this year and continues to do so.

"The new regulations, combined with the volume and pace of performance coming from the tunnel and engineering through to the circuit, have made it an intense year. That galvanises the team and brings us closer together, so we get the right performance to the track while challenging each other and our ideas.

"A new floor is arriving in Las Vegas this week, and it's a great example of our programme delivery. The collaboration between Aerodynamics, Design, Performance, Planning and Manufacturing helped ensure the team could maximise the output of the last tunnel runs for the 40A. It's a big push, but by making decisions closely together, we hit the targets we set ourselves."

Sports.title: South Africa Rugby condemns online abuse of officials after Erasmus ban
Sports.content:
South Africa Rugby has condemned online abuse of World Rugby officials following the decision to hand Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus a six-match ban.

An independent panel imposed the punishment after reviewing comments made by Erasmus at a media conference on Monday ahead of the Nations Championship match against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday.

SA Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing for the 54-year-old, who will not be able to have any matchday involvement in international fixtures during the suspension.

Erasmus delivered an outspoken press conference on Monday, in which he suggested officials had missed 17 illegal tackles against his side during their crunch Nations Championship clash. He went as far as questioning whether "match-fixing" and "manipulation" of the result was behind why those incidents were not picked up.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News reporter James Cole breaks down Erasmus' six-match suspension following his comments on officiating standards

World Rugby confirmed it had reviewed the comments made by Erasmus, and an independent panel had imposed the sanction under World Rugby's Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, a framework that was introduced in July.

Following a social media backlash against the global governing body, SA Rugby has called for calm to allow the proper processes to run their course.

"SA Rugby is aware of the extensive public commentary, analysis and debate surrounding recent matters involving Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus and World Rugby," a statement from the organisation read.

"We are mindful that a significant volume of commentary, opinion and AI-generated content is currently circulating in the public domain, much of which does not necessarily reflect the facts, context or processes involved.

"What is deeply concerning, however, is the reaction of some individuals on social media and other platforms, particularly reports of threats and abusive conduct directed at World Rugby officials and administrators.

"SA Rugby unequivocally condemns any form of intimidation, threats or personal attacks. Such behaviour has no place in rugby and is entirely contrary to the values upon which our game is founded.

Image: South Africa Rugby have requested the opportunity for Erasmus to "contextualise his comments"

"Rugby has long been recognised as a sport built on respect, discipline, integrity and sportsmanship. These values extend beyond the field of play and apply equally to players, coaches, match officials, administrators and supporters. While robust debate and differing opinions are part of sport, they must always be expressed respectfully and responsibly.

"SA Rugby also wishes to assure all stakeholders that rugby possesses the necessary expertise, experience and governance structures to deal with matters of this nature appropriately.

"Any issues that arise will be addressed through the established rugby processes and by the individuals entrusted with these responsibilities, ensuring that due process is followed and that the best interests of the game remain paramount.

"We remain committed to protecting the integrity of rugby, upholding its values and ensuring that all participants in the game are treated with dignity and respect."

Sports.title: Man Utd expected to back Poch in January transfer window
Sports.content:
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as the club aim to address their disappointing start to the season.

A left-back, centre-back and forward are areas the club are looking to potentially strengthen in January with Pochettino expected to have input on targets they will pursue.

Despite the club's hierarchy feeling the team should be further up the table, there is also an acknowledgement that they could have further strengthened the squad in the summer in areas where they lacked depth.

Sky Sports News understands Manchester United already had plans to move in the upcoming window under former head coach Michael Carrick, before he was sacked last month following United's worst start to a league season for 40 years.

However, Pochettino is now expected to be consulted in the coming weeks and will have his say on potential recruits in January.

Watch 'Unfinished Business' Transfer Show special Tune in to Sky Sports News at 4pm and 7pm for our 'Unfinished Business' Transfer Show special for in-depth analysis of Man Utd's plans for the January window.

Centre-back

Image: Fulham want to extend Calvin Bassey's contract

Fulham's Calvin Bassey and Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite are two players United are monitoring as potential options to reinforce their defence in January.

Despite Fulham's struggles this season, Bassey is a player who has impressed and has just six months left on his current deal, though his club have the option to extend that by a further year.

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has described the 26-year-old as one of the best defenders in the world and said the club's aim is to extend Bassey's contract.

Meanwhile, Branthwaite has long been admired by United. In 2024, United had two bids rejected for the centre-back, their second being worth around £50m.

Image: Jarrad Branthwaite is a long-term target for Man Utd

Everton are in a strong negotiating position over the 24-year-old, who has a contract until the summer of 2030.

United are looking at left-footed centre-back options as they consider potential replacements for Lisandro Martinez. His future at Old Trafford looks in doubt come next summer with his current contract expiring.

Despite United having an option for a further 12 months, he is unlikely to be offered fresh terms as Sky Sports News reported last month.

Left-back

Image: Lewis Hall signed a new deal with Newcastle after Manchester United explored a move for him this summer

The club decided not to pursue a left-back in the summer as they focused on their midfield rebuild with the belief their long-term targets would be more attainable next year.

It remains to be seen whether that will be true come the end of the season and where that leaves players such as Newcastle United's Lewis Hall, but with five different players being used in that position with limited success, the club will look at the possibility of cover at left-back in January.

Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson continues to be monitored, as first reported by Sky Sports News in March. Fulham are aware of widespread interest in Robinson but no club has so far made a move for the 29-year-old, who worked under Pochettino with the USA.

Barcelona's Alejandro Balde was a player linked with United in the summer but was never at a stage when the move seemed likely. United were aware of his potential availability and it has not been ruled out that they revisit a deal in January if it works for all parties.

Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri was an option United tentatively explore on Deadline Day but they decided against pursuing him due to City's insistence on an obligation to make the move permanent. Sky Sports News understands he is not considered a target at this stage as United look at other options.

Forward

With United's main No 9 Benjamin Sesko ruled out until at least January, the club will explore potential reinforcements in the upcoming window to re-balance the club's attack.

Although United scored seven goals in their last two games before the break, the club have missed a physical presence in Sesko's absence to lead the line.

Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin was a player of interest but his future looks likely to remain at Elland Road and United are not expected to explore a move for the forward.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored against Man Utd in their match at Leeds - watch the free highlights here

Outgoings

Any outgoings in January could have an impact on how much the club can reinforce Pochettino's squad but numerous first-team departures are not likely with the size of the squad and long-term injuries as well as Pochettino needing time to assess his squad all set to play a factor.

Joshua Zirkzee continues to be a player who attracts interest from Italy and United could entertain a move for the Dutch forward if they receive a suitable offer but would need cover in that position.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On Transfer Talk, Julien Laurens admitted he thought that Lisandro Martinez should never have played again for Manchester United after his comments about the board

Martinez's future will under the spotlight in January. Sky Sports News reported last month United are unlikely to offer him a new contract. His current deal expires next summer although the club hold an option for a further 12 months.

Pochettino will also have to manage other expiring contracts in his squad with Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and captain Bruno Fernandes also in the last six months of their current contracts, although it is worth noting the club have a 12-month option on Fernandes and Maguire.

Sports.title: The wild life of Peter Storey who died aged 81: An Arsenal double-winning legend who was jailed for three years for his role in a criminal counterfeit operation, once ran a brothel and was caught trying to smuggle adult films into the UK
Sports.content:
The wild life of Peter Storey who died aged 81: An Arsenal double-winning legend who was jailed for three years for his role in a criminal counterfeit operation, once ran a brothel and was caught trying to smuggle adult films into the UK

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list

Joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an important part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010)

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

Sports.title: Straight to work! Grinning Mauricio Pochettino delights in starting 'amazing job' at Manchester United after touching down on private jet - and vows that Man City's dominance is 'gonna change'
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino says it is 'an honour and a privilege' to manage Manchester United - after hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss. The new manager landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff. Speaking to the club's media channels, Pochettino said: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.' The club then officially welcomed the new manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian. 'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.' Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening. New Man United manager Mauricio Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati. But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers. 'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.' 'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.' Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge. Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's new-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford. 'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always. 'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved. 'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something important for the future of soccer in this country. The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino) The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United 'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made new friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile. 'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity. 'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy. 'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.' Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford. ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy. ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. ‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward. ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives. ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.' Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break. The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change. An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning. In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick. 'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.' Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to quickly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle. Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone 'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino said after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.' Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield. Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a new contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup. The quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday. Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati. 'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'

Sports.title: Galatasaray forced into emergency pitch repairs to make it playable for Champions League clash with Aston Villa after they had to MOVE OUT, with worrying images emerging
Sports.content:
Galatasaray forced into emergency pitch repairs to make it playable for Champions League clash with Aston Villa after they had to MOVE OUT, with worrying images emerging

Aston Villa have been told their Champions League clash with Galatasaray on Tuesday will still take place at the home of the Turkish champions despite the worrying state of the pitch.

Galatasaray have switched their home league fixture against Samsunspor this weekend to the stadium of top-flight rivals Istanbul Basaksehir to save the playing surface from further punishment.

Images released this week show a pitch that appears to be in alarming condition, with Galatasaray working around the clock to ensure it is playable. The club are in dialogue with UEFA.

At this stage, Daily Mail Sport understands UEFA are satisfied that the pitch will be in suitable condition when the sides take the field, though a pitch inspection will take place at 10am local time as is the case before any European fixture.

UEFA Article 5 states: ‘The field of play must be smooth and level and comply with the IFAB Laws of the Game.’

Villa will look to strengthen their position in the league phase after winning three of their opening four games, though they lost their last fixture, at Barcelona.

Galatasaray are working around the clock to ensure their pitch is up to standard for their Champions League clash against Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom)

Unai Emery’s men have already beaten Turkish opposition this term, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 for their record European win, though that fixture was at Villa Park.

After the chaotic 4-4 draw at Manchester United before the international break, Villa meet Sunderland at home in the Premier League on Saturday.

Emery has doubts over Matty Cash and Johan Manzambi, who picked up injuries while on international duty and may struggle to recover in time.

Sports.title: Full steam ahead for Worcester's top-flight return and expect Welsh clubs to throw their hat into the ring, writes ALEX BYWATER... as PREM Rugby open door for TWO new teams to join competition
Sports.content:
Full steam ahead for Worcester's top-flight return and expect Welsh clubs to throw their hat into the ring, writes ALEX BYWATER... as PREM Rugby open door for TWO new teams to join competition

PREM Rugby – the English game’s top domestic league – has officially confirmed its plans for expansion, opening the door for two new teams to join by the 2029-30 season.

The news will be welcomed by former English top-flight clubs such as current CHAMP side Worcester, as well as London Irish and Wasps, who both have designs on a comeback.

It is also an open invitation for Wales’ struggling domestic game to seek pastures new, even if the PREM wants to target English sides to join it first ahead of those from over the border.

Currently made up of 10 teams, on Wednesday the PREM opened ‘the first stage of its expansion process’ in what they said was ‘a landmark moment’ for the league.

‘The PREM is inviting clubs, investors and their authorised representatives to register their interest in joining the PREM,’ a league statement read.

‘The ambition is to welcome up to two new clubs, growing the league from 10 to 12, with entry targeted for the 2029-30 season, subject to readiness.'

PREM Rugby – the English game’s top domestic league – has officially confirmed its plans for expansion, opening the door for two new teams to join by the 2029-30 season

That is welcome news for ex-English top-flight clubs such as current CHAMP side Worcester

The PREM has become an American-style franchise league, with no promotion and relegation.

The move was unpopular with sporting traditionalists, but was done to try and ensure financial stabilisation and attract fresh investment.

The impact of the Covid-19 pandemic saw Worcester, Wasps and London Irish all disappear following administration.

Since then, the PREM has recovered slowly. Energy drink giants Red Bull have taken over Newcastle, while Sir James Dyson has ploughed money into Bath. Exeter Chiefs have also been taken over by Americans Black Knight Capital.

‘As we celebrate our 30th season, the PREM is in a strong position to grow as we look to write a new chapter with new clubs and new stories,’ said PREM chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor, who is in the USA this week for talks with new potential investors.

‘Expansion is a unique opportunity to welcome new audiences and clubs and we want to hear from anyone who shares our ambition to make the PREM the best league in the world.’

Massie-Taylor has been joined in the PREM’s USA charm offensive by the league’s chief operating officer Charlotte Samuelson.

Existing rugby sides, or investors who may wish to set-up a new one, can now apply to the PREM to express their interest in joining under a ‘request for information’ process.

It will be open until February 1, 2027. No formal bid or commitment to invest is required at this stage.

PREM CEO Simon Massie-Taylor is in the USA this week for talks with new potential investors

Expansion is significantly positive development for English club rugby - here are some potential contenders: Alex Bywater

By officially confirming they were open to receiving expressions of interest from new teams, PREM Rugby’s message on Wednesday was crystal clear.

It essentially amounted to: ‘Come join us! Everything is rosy in the English club rugby garden!’

When Worcester, London Irish and Wasps descended into oblivion, the PREM had to batten down the hatches to survive. So, it is a significantly positive development that it is now in a position to expand.

It will benefit all parties within the English rugby ecosystem, so long as it is done sensibly.

In its current guise as a 10-team league, the PREM doesn’t have enough regular season matches.

The clubs need more power to increase revenue, so moving to 12 suits all parties.

The big question is this: Who will be the two new faces? The Welsh Rugby Union – who centrally fund Wales’ four struggling domestic teams – will certainly apply. It’s a no-brainer for them.

However, as PREM chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor and his RFU counterpart Bill Sweeney have consistently maintained, English expansion is the initial priority.

There is also the added complication of the WRU’s long-term tie to the United Rugby Championship and its ongoing plan to move from four to three teams. Many, however, do support the idea of an Anglo-Welsh league.

The obvious first team to join is Worcester. Their demise only came about thanks to the shocking financial mismanagement enacted by cowboy former owners Jason Whittingham and Colin Goldring.

But they are now back competing in the CHAMP and attracting decent crowds through their loyal following. It would be great to see them back.

Wasps, who have been defunct since 2022, could also return, but that feels a long way off still

While the same is true of London Irish and Wasps, that feels a long way off as right now, neither are in existence.

In an ideal world, a second club would come from areas currently not represented in the PREM – such as Yorkshire, Norfolk or Kent. The north of England, as it stands, only has Sale and Newcastle as PREM representatives.

Doncaster and Rotherham – both currently in the CHAMP – would be good options to join the PREM and help spread the league’s geography, though both would need significant fresh investment.

Massie-Taylor and Co would also, undoubtedly, be open to another global brand coming on board – as Red Bull have done at Newcastle.

In such a scenario, a new team could be started up and quickly too, though they would have to spend at least one season in the CHAMP first before joining the top league.

With a good on-field product and improvement off it, these are exciting times for the PREM. The prospect of two new teams can only be seen as a positive.

Sports.title: Premier League identify FIVE key refereeing errors in one weekend as boss Howard Webb prepares to appear in front of clubs after Arsenal blunder
Sports.content:
Premier League identify FIVE key refereeing errors in one weekend as boss Howard Webb prepares to appear in front of clubs after Arsenal blunder

The Premier League have ruled that referees made five incorrect decisions in the latest round of matches as officials endured their worst weekend of the season so far.

It was unanimously ruled that referee Farai Hallam should have awarded Kai Havertz a penalty after he was tugged in the area during Arsenal's victory over Hull City, despite being in an offside position.

That is because the laws state that if a foul occurs before an offside offence, a penalty should be awarded.

Although Havertz was in an offside position, he had not committed an offence as he had neither played the ball nor interfered with play.

The key match incidents panel (KMI) said: 'Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded.'

Farai Hallam's decision not to award Kai Havertz a penalty was deemed incorrect by the key match incidents panel

Coventry were wrongly denied a spot-kick in their defeat to Everton after James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair

THE 5 WRONG CALLS 1. Everton vs Coventry City: Frank Lampard's side should have been awarded a penalty when James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair. 2. Arsenal vs Hull City: Kai Havertz was denied a penalty after being dragged down. The referee did not award a spot-kick because Havertz in an offside position. However, that decision was incorrect, as he was not committing an offside offence and a spot-kick should therefore have been awarded. 3. Crystal Palace vs Liverpool: Palace were awarded a penalty in the last minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool after Milos Kerkez and Dario Osario clashed heads in the penalty area. The panel saw this as a natural coming together. 4. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: A penalty was given after Abdoul Ouattara tumbled over. The referee gave a foul against Lewis Cook despite Ouattara stepping across him. 5. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: Marcus Tavernier should have seen a second yellow card for time-wasting.

They did, however, praise the VAR for asking the referee to review the incident on the monitor despite Hallam's decision to stick with his on-field call after watching it back.

In the same weekend, Tottenham Hotspur complained to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle's heavy challenge on Mathys Tel's ankle - which forced him off injured.

Spurs felt Bogle should have seen red, particularly after Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for a similar incident in the week prior.

Reviewing the decision, the KMI panel were split but eventually concluded that the foul lacked 'the speed, force or intensity' to be considered serious foul play.

Two of the five panellists, however, felt that the challenge merited a red card.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace's consolation penalty in the 92nd minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool should never have been awarded.

The KMI panel unanimously agreed that the referee was wrong to award a penalty when Milos Kerkez and Dario Osorio clashed heads when contesting the ball, with the contact inevitable given both players were jumping.

However, VAR's decision not to intervene was supported because it was not a 'clear and obvious error'.

It is the second penalty incident in as many weeks that the went against Liverpool after Alexander Isak was wrongfully denied a spot-kick against Arsenal.

On the opposite side of Merseyside, James Tarkowski was fortunate not to concede a penalty for pulling Caleb Yirenkyi's hair during Everton's win over Coventry City, with the score still 0-0 at the time.

The panel found that Coventry should have been awarded a penalty and Tarkowski should have received a yellow card.

Last season, that incident would likely have resulted in a straight red card. However, the guidance changed this term with red cards only brandished if there is excessive force.

There were also two incorrect decisions in Bournemouth's victory over Ipswich Town.

Bournemouth defender Marcus Tavernier should have been sent off for a second yellow card in the 96th minute for delaying the restart during their 2-1 win, the panel found. However, it was a close call as the panel voted 3-2 against the decision.

Ipswich's scored penalty was also deemed to have been wrongly awarded, with Abdoul Ouattara stepping across Lewis Cook to win the spot-kick rather than being fouled by the defender.

The KMI panel consists of a representative from the Premier League and ProRef alongside three former managers or players and meets after every round of Premier League matches to evaluate significant refereeing decisions.

Ref boss Howard Webb will speak to Premier League clubs at a routine meeting on Thursday

While the panel is not new, this is the first season their findings have been publicly released in Pro Ref's drive for greater transparency and accountability.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb is due to appear in front of clubs on Thursday at a routine Premier League meeting.

And in more positive news for Webb, he will be able to share that VAR delays are down this season after increasing the bar for interventions.

Meanwhile, the KMI panel have assessed 296 decisions this season - only six of which have been judged to be wrong post-VAR.

Sports.title: Harry Kane up for ANOTHER prize alongside three England team-mates - as Globe Soccer Awards voting opens ahead of glitzy Dubai ceremony
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is one of the main contenders for the prestigious Best Men's Player prize at the Globe Soccer Awards - and you can vote for the winner.

The Ballon d'Or king is joined by England team-mates Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, and Bukayo Saka in the category.

Meanwhile, Lionesses star Alessia Russo is the sole English representative in contention for the Best Women's Player honour.

Voting is now open across 12 categories, with the awards to be handed out at a glitzy ceremony in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on December 28.

The Globe Soccer Awards began in 2010 and have since became popular among fans worldwide, with more than 100 million votes cast in some years.

Last year's winner Ousmane Dembele is also in the running for Best Men's Player, with Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe joining him in the 26-strong shortlist.

Harry Kane, pictured with the Ballon d'Or, is among the nominees for Best Men's PLayer at the Globe Soccer Awards

Voting is now open across 12 award categories ahead of a ceremony in Dubai in December

Erling Haaland won the Best Men's Player prize for 2023 and is in contention again

Premier League stars Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, William Saliba, and Dominik Szboszlai are also hoping to get their hands on the prize.

Mikel Arteta and Unai Emery are in the running for Best Coach, while Myles Lewis-Skelly and Nico O'Reilly are competing for the Emerging Player gong.

There are 14 categories, with a 'Career and Special Awards' section yet to see its talent announced.

Arsenal are hopefuls in the Best Club category for both men and women, with Aston Villa joining them in the former and Manchester City in the latter.

There will also be prizes for the best forward, midfielder, defender, and goalkeeper, and Fans' Historic Club, Best Sporting Director, and Best Agent.

Ronaldo, a serial winner at the ceremony, is defending his Best Middle East Player crown after winning his first Saudi Pro League title with Al-Nassr. Ivan Toney is among his rivals for that.

Fans are able to cast their votes until November 30, after which a jury including the likes of Antonio Conte and Luis Figo will also have their say.

It is an event of truly global interest, with supporters from more than 225 countries having cast votes in previous editions.

'We are incredibly proud to return for our third consecutive year as title partner of the GLOBE SOCCER Awards,' said Adil Taqi, CEO of title sponsor BEYOND Developments.

'Our continued partnership reflects BEYOND Developments’ commitment to connecting with an international audience through shared passions and experiences.

'Football brings people together across cultures and borders, resonating with our belief in pushing boundaries and aiming higher, a mindset shared by the players, coaches and clubs who will be honoured this December. We are proud to stand alongside an event that unites the global football family.'

Fans are able to vote via the Globe Soccer App.

Sports.title: Brilliant openers, finding a way to knock over old nemesis Travis Head and Sandpapergate blowing up in Australia's face - where it went right for England in ODI series win
Sports.content:
Brilliant openers, finding a way to knock over old nemesis Travis Head and Sandpapergate blowing up in Australia's face - where it went right for England in ODI series win

England’s comprehensive 97-run win in the deciding ODI against Australia in Hobart gave Harry Brook’s 50-over team their greatest moment yet.

Daily Mail Sport looks at where it went right Down Under.

Opening up

In five of England’s last eight ODIs, one of their openers – Ben Duckett and Tom Banton – has scored a century, regularly providing a cushion for those below. And Duckett’s 133 off 115 balls in Hobart was among the best.

After falling for just nine at both Perth and Adelaide, he seemed to have confirmed the prejudice that Australian conditions are not for him. After all, it’s not yet a year since he averaged just 20 in the Ashes.

But he bided his time while Banton crashed nine fours in powerful 35-ball 44, then opened up with strokes all round the wicket. In 2026, only India's Shubman Gill has more than Duckett’s 888 runs. Banton, meanwhile, finished the series with 190 runs, more than anyone on either side. There will be no immediate way back for Jacob Bethell.

Tom Banton (left) and Ben Duckett (right) provided a cushion for those below them

Utility man

Top of the batting averages, though, was Will Jacks, who in the last month alone has walked out in every position from No 4 to 7, and developed a priceless knack for playing the right shot at the right moment.

At Adelaide, he gave England’s innings late impetus with an unbeaten 54 off 40 balls. At Hobart, he managed an industrious 59 off 48, preventing a lower-order collapse and helping the total to 328.

Jacks, who was also trusted to come on as first change with his off-breaks, has turned into a significant white-ball cricketer – and has out-performed his Surrey colleague Sam Curran.

Knocking the head off

During the Ashes, England looked clueless against Travis Head, who scored centuries in Australia’s wins at Perth, Adelaide and Sydney. In this series, he has been dismissed three times by Gus Atkinson for 0, 7 and 4 – bowled once off the edge, and caught twice in the slips.

In the opener at Perth, it didn’t matter, since Australia were chasing only 132. But when they needed well over 300 at both Adelaide and Hobart, Atkinson’s early strikes drained the hosts of confidence.

He has been the attack leader out here, and would have taken more than six wickets at 17 had England held all their catches. He even forced Cameron Green to retire hurt, blood coming out of his mouth, after he misjudged a slippery bouncer. Atkinson looked chillingly unconcerned.

Travis Head was dismissed for 0, 7 and 4 in the three-match ODI series

Exuberance of youth

Sonny Baker got his chance in the second game only because of a thigh injury to Jamie Overton, but he made an instant impact with the wicket of Mitchell Marsh as Australia crashed to 13 for three.

Overton was available for selection in Hobart, but England’s selectors stuck with Baker. He dismissed Marsh cheaply once more, and cleverly worked over Josh Inglis, sending down two inswingers before taking the outside edge with a wider one that held its line.

Still only 23, he finished with an ODI-best four for 45, and celebrated each wicket as if he had just won the lottery. After a shaky start to his international career in 2025, he is showing why England didn’t lose hope.

Dawson’s sleek

England’s continued omission of Adil Rashid has invited scrutiny, but Liam Dawson justified his role as frontline spinner in their two wins, taking combined figures of five for 83 from 19 combative overs – and twice removing the adhesive Matthew Renshaw.

Brook enjoys the 36-year-old Dawson’s on-field nous and competitive edge, and the only question now is whether both he and Rashid can be squeezed into the same World Cup side.

Liam Dawson justified his role as frontline spinner for England in their victories

It’s catching

At both Adelaide and Hobart, Joe Root and Brook caught superbly in the slips to help reduce Australia to 13 for three, then five for two. Root’s diving grab to see off Marsh in the second game was the catch of the series.

It was strange, then, that England dropped easier outfield catches in both games, but they had such a buffer that it didn’t matter.

Forward planning

England were not afraid to get funky as they worked out what everyone’s capable of less than a year before the World Cup. Tom Banton bowled some rarely seen off-breaks, and Brook himself took the last wicket of the series with some off-spin of his own.

Then there was the promotion to No 6 of Jofra Archer in Hobart, in a bid to knock Australia’s spinners off their rhythm. He made only seven, but it was the move of a side growing in confidence.

Mitchell Marsh dodged the press conference and avoided more Sandpapergate questions

Role reversal

During the Ashes, all the mockery was directed at England. But Sandpapergate has blown up in Australia’s face, with Cameron Bancroft’s claim that everyone knew about the plot in South Africa eight years ago just the latest explosive device.

White-ball captain Mitchell Marsh, the only member of this team to have played in that series, skipped the post-match press conference, sending the fresh-faced all-rounder Jack Edwards to speak instead.

Asked whether it was frustrating that off-field headlines had dominated, he said with a nervous chuckle: ‘It takes the heat off us, to be honest.’

Sports.title: How England cracked down on being 'the world's least-disciplined team': Why they brought a Test referee into training, players' ratings for penalty probability and what they've changed since summer sin-bin woes
Sports.content:
How England cracked down on being 'the world's least-disciplined team': Why they brought a Test referee into training, players' ratings for penalty probability and what they've changed since summer sin-bin woes

The referee’s whistle has been one of England’s most valuable weapons this autumn. On the evidence of the opening two rounds of the November Tests, Steve Borthwick’s side seem to have finally tightened up their discipline.

Since the summer, their penalty count has dropped from 11.25 per game – the highest in the world in 2026 – to seven. And bar Luke Cowan-Dickie’s late yellow card against Japan, they have managed to keep 15 players on the pitch, having conceded six yellows in their three Nations Championship matches during the summer. Only Argentina (nine) have more over the first five rounds of the tournament.

So, what is the secret? This autumn, PREM Rugby and international referee Christophe Ridley has spent more time in camp with the team on an unpaid arrangement. Almost every live training session has been officiated to Test match standards.

Players focus on tackle height, the offside line and rolling out of the tackle before being given a percentage score at the end of each session.

‘We would break up into small groups and had good conversations in and around that,’ said hooker Jamie George. ‘They were very open. There was one coach per group. For example Henry Pollock was in my group – when does he feel like he gives away penalties? Why does he feel that way? It’s about stressing the importance of what we can do around him to make sure he's not put into those positions.’

Daily Mail Sport understands there would be appetite for England to bring in a full-time refereeing coach at some point in the future, similar to the French and South African arrangements with Jerome Garces and Jaco Peyper. Wales have done similar with Ben Whitehouse.

Henry Arundell received two yellow cards in quick succession against Scotland in the Six Nations, first for sealing off a ruck (left), then for tackling Kyle Steyn in the air (right)

PREM and international referee Christophe Ridley (right) has been invited into England camp to officiate training matches

‘I think a referee going in can definitely help you and get you into good habits,’ legendary Welsh referee Nigel Owens, who took charge of 100 Tests before retiring in 2020, told Daily Mail Sport.

‘A couple of players would come to me and say, “I’m struggling with referees at the moment" or "I’m finding it difficult to communicate with them in the heat of the moment". I’d ask them to send me a couple of clips or examples.

‘I’d tell them to approach it in a different way, or little things like that. Sometimes (former Wales captains) Alun Wyn Jones or Sam Warburton would ask me a couple of things. Personally, I don’t think a referee in camp needs to be a full-time role but South Africa and France are doing it and now so are Wales.’

One of the biggest things England learned from the summer was that their discipline was at its worst when the opposition had possession. More than 60 per cent of their penalties were conceded when they did not have the ball.

Subsequently, there has been more focus on getting the ball back quickly. The selection of turnover specialist Ben Curry at flanker has been central to their thought process. Limiting the opposition ruck count is a key target and Curry’s jackals killed Australian and Japanese attacks.

‘The biggest change is probably the defensive sets being a bit shorter,’ said England defence coach Richard Wigglesworth. ‘Inevitably, with the way the game's refereed, the longer those sets go on, the more likely they're going to pick something up.

‘With good players, you give them a few things to go after and they do it. Every defensive team probably wants the ball back. There are not too many teams that just want to contain. We certainly don't want to be that defensive team. We want to put a team under pressure without the ball.’

England’s defensive system has evolved under Wigglesworth. They now apply more pressure around the ruck, with the likes of Ellis Genge and Maro Itoje flying up to disrupt the pass. Previously, the emphasis was on line speed being generated by the outside backs.

Nigel Owens, who became the first man to referee 100 Tests before retiring in 2020, is a fan of England bringing in a referee to consult

Maro Itoje (left) and Sam Underhill (centre) were both shown yellow cards in Rome in the Six Nations, costing England dear as they slipped to a first-ever defeat by Italy

Ben Curry (centre) has been crucial to England's improved discipline as a fierce jackler

‘Change is not always as quick as you like,’ added Wigglesworth. ‘If the opposition have 100 rucks in their own half, you'd be pretty happy. If they have 100 rucks in your 22, you're not going to be on the right end of it.

'If they have multiple possessions over seven or eight-plus phases, you know they've gone back-to-back sets and they're putting you under pressure. It’s different if it's spread out between penalties and turnovers and our possessions.

‘It’s a different challenge against the All Blacks this week. We could talk about getting the ball back and the All Blacks could end up with 120 or 130 rucks.’

After four straight victories, the pressure has eased on Borthwick’s England. For now, they have shaken off their status as the world’s least-disciplined team.

Bigger Tests lie ahead, however, and Borthwick’s old mentor Eddie Jones, now Japan head coach, fired a sharp message: ‘When you’re on the front foot, you shouldn’t have discipline issues. Your discipline gets tested when you’re under the pump.’

Sports.title: Ivan Toney fails in bid to avoid court case clashing with Euro 2028
Sports.content:
Ivan Toney fails in bid to avoid court case clashing with Euro 2028

England and Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney will go on trial during Euro 2028 after failing in a bid to get his court case moved to August

View 2 Images Ivan Toney's bid to move an assault trial next year has failed (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

A bid to move the date of England striker Ivan Toney’s assault trial to avoid a clash with Euro 2028 in case he is selected to play has been refused.

The 30-year-old footballer is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6.

Toney denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a three to four-day trial was fixed for June 12 2028, which is three days into Euro 2028.

At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, which Toney did not attend, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: “It came to our attention that…there may be potentially a football match called the European Championship in 2028 between June 9 and July 9.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Mr Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: “We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.

“My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup.”

Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a “speculative” application. He refused the request, saying: “It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed.”

The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.

View 2 Images Toney was part of the England team at the World Cup (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Mr Da Silva. It was heard the two men “squared up to each other”, before Toney allegedly “lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches”.

The Metropolitan Police investigated and the footballer was charged in late July.

Toney represented England at this summer’s World Cup and has made 10 international appearances and scored one goal. He missed out on the latest squad for the country’s Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton and played for teams including Wigan and Peterborough before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

Sports.title: The true cost of being a football fan revealed as supporters fork out eye-watering costs
Sports.content:
The true cost of being a football fan revealed as supporters fork out eye-watering costs

A study of 2,000 football fans who attend away matches, alongside analysis of this season’s league fixtures, reveals the financial and travel commitment involved in following a club around the country

View 2 Images Manchester United fans make their feelings felt against Aston Villa recently (Image: 2026 Catherine Ivill - AMA)

Fans of England’s top-flight football teams spend an average of £3,564 each season on travel, tickets, accommodation and food and drink while following their team to away games.

‌



‌



A study of 2,000 football fans who attend away matches, commissioned by budget hotel chain Travelodge, alongside analysis of this season’s league fixtures, reveals the financial and travel commitment involved in following a club around the country.

‌



With the average supporter attending six away games a season, costs quickly add up. Fans spend on average £594 per match, including £217 on accommodation, £195 on travel, £152 on food and drink and £30 on their match ticket.

‌



That means supporters shell out an average of £3,564 across the season, with travel alone accounting for £1,170. This includes getting to and from fixtures by train, bus or car, including petrol and EV charging.

View 2 Images Costs can vary considerably between stadiums, with the most expensive pint found at Arsenal’s stadium costing £6.80 compared to just £3.50 at Ipswich Town, the cheapest in the league

Despite the mounting costs, more than half (55%) of fans say they wouldn’t miss a chance to support their team at a match, regardless of the expense.

‌



Costs can vary considerably between stadiums, with the most expensive pint found at Arsenal’s stadium costing £6.80 compared to just £3.50 at Ipswich Town, the cheapest in the league.

Analysis of this season’s fixtures shows the distances supporters face travelling when following their club away from home. Fans will travel an average of 4,864 miles following their club across the season, with Sunderland supporters facing the greatest overall distance at 7,547 miles due to fewer direct rail connections.

‌



Newcastle United supporters follow closely behind at 7,425 miles, while Bournemouth fans face the third-highest total at 6,229 miles.

Fans of Aston Villa are due to cover the least ground, needing to travel only 3,849 miles to get to all away matches this season.

‌



The fans set to travel furthest during the 2026/27 football season:

Sunderland (7,547 miles) Newcastle United (7,425 miles) Bournemouth (6,229 miles) Ipswich Town (5,922 miles) Brighton & Hove Albion (5,488 miles) Hull City (5,307 miles) Everton (5,212 miles) Liverpool (4,799 miles) Leeds United (4,557 miles) Manchester United (4,442 miles)

For supporters already travelling significant distances, fixture changes can make getting home even harder. More than two-thirds (68%) of matches were rescheduled last season, while 61% of fans say altered kick-off times or stoppage time can make their journey home difficult.

Nearly eight in ten (79%) say they have missed the last train home following an away fixture, while 88% have faced a lengthy journey home after a game.

‌



To avoid the challenges of getting home after a game, 82% of supporters say they would consider staying in a hotel following an away match. Avoiding a long journey home is the biggest reason (58%), followed by having more time to explore the city (35%), and avoiding crowds (34%).

With Newcastle United fans facing one of the longest journeys of the season when their side travels to play Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday 29th November, Travelodge is stepping in to give five fans a free overnight stay at Travelodge Brighton, helping supporters make the most of their trip to the south coast.

‌



Fans travelling to the match and staying the night can email gamedaystay@travelodge.co.uk to be in the running for a free room.

Expert statistician, Ed Jefferson, who oversaw the study for Travelodge, said: “Supporting a football team has always involved a significant commitment of both time and money, but our analysis shows just how much that investment can be during a season.

"While ticket prices are an obvious cost, travel, food, accommodation and other matchday expenses are all contributing to the overall cost of supporting a top-flight team.”

Sports.title: Man Utd 'ready to take legal action' after JJ Gabriel's two bombshell announcements
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'ready to take legal action' after JJ Gabriel's two bombshell announcements

Manchester United are concerned by the latest developments regarding JJ Gabriel - and legal action isn't off the table

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel announced his Manchester United exit this week (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are poised to pursue legal action over JJ Gabriel's move to Real Madrid should proof of inducement come to light. Agency Epic Sports officially confirmed on Monday evening that they are Gabriel's new representatives in the first of two announcements this week.

‌



‌



The following day, the youngster released a farewell video expressing his gratitude to United for their role in his development. The club were left frustrated that the farewell video was published without any prior communication from Gabriel's camp.

‌



They've made numerous attempts to check on the teenager's welfare since receiving a request for him to leave in September, yet have been unable to establish contact with his family.

‌



United are now primed to pursue legal action should evidence of inducement from Madrid surface, according to the Manchester Evening News. Strict regulations exist surrounding the signing of Under-18 players, and United are prepared to fight their corner using every legal avenue available.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

United have received no communication from any governing bodies regarding the de-registration of Gabriel, who remains registered with the club. Concerns have grown over the guidance he has been given.

‌



The 16-year-old had been on track to become the club's youngest ever debutant, but was advised to leave after failing to report for training. United are keen to ensure that Gabriel has had a genuine say in what is a life-changing decision, with growing concerns that he has been poorly guided by his father throughout the entire process.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel was on course to be United's next big thing (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

In Gabriel's farewell video, he said: "Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams. Here I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

‌



"You gave me moments I will always treasure. To every coach and every member of staff, to my teammates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

"As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ."

‌



Michael Carrick handed Gabriel his pre-season senior debut against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, yet the youngster failed to feature for a single minute in any other friendly throughout the rest of the summer.

United had intended to hand Gabriel his competitive debut against Brighton in the Carabao Cup in September, but his camp pushed for a transfer ahead of that fixture.

‌



Following his request to leave, Gabriel initially trained in Castelldefels, Barcelona, under a personal coach, but has since relocated to Madrid in anticipation of his widely expected move to the Bernabeu.

If Gabriel's impending move to Madrid goes through, United would be due just £300,000 in FIFA training compensation, though potential legal action could be taken to seek a higher fee.

Article continues below

Reports indicate that the 16-year-old England youth international will be given a three-year contract at Real Madrid worth around £8.5million.

Sports.title: Incredible abandoned stadium being brought back as football giants expect £415m Christmas gift
Sports.content:
Incredible abandoned stadium being brought back as football giants expect £415m Christmas gift

The sporting and concert venue is a sorry sight, but is set to be transformed as part of an ambitious project

View 3 Images The Stadio Flaminio has become an abandoned wasteland since it last hosted sport (Image: Marck/Youtube)

Lazio are on the verge of getting the green light to bring an historic stadium back to life and move out of the Stadio Olimpico. The Stadio Flaminio has sat abandoned in northern Rome for 15 years, but is set to become the new home of the Italian giants.

‌



‌



Built for the 1960 Summer Olympics, the ground had a capacity of around 32,000 when it hosted Six Nations rugby between 2000 and 2011 before being left to decay. Now, the Serie A giants are spearheading an ambitious £415million project to resurrect the venue as their exclusive new home, having ground-shared with Roma since the Stadio Olimpico opened in 1953.

‌



Lazio aim to have the ground rebuilt and operational by 2031, making it a potential venue for the Euro 2032, which Italy will co-host with Turkey.

‌



The club is confident that formal approval will be granted before Christmas, following submission of the requested additions to the Superintendency. If the project receives the council's green light, building work will commence next year. It will have a capacity of around 47,000.

Abandoned Six Nations stadium with huge capacity could be set to come back to life READ MORE :

Abandoned Champions League stadium now overgrown mess with explosives warning signs READ MORE :

Alessandro Onorato, Rome's councillor for major events, sport, tourism and fashion, told Radiosei: "We're confident that approval on the grounds of public interest will arrive by Christmas. We're halfway there.

"The money? I'd wait before saying it's not there. It would be foolish to invest money only in the planning phase."

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources .

The plans involve restoring its listed concrete structure while building a dramatic, suspended second tier and a full-stadium roof over the existing bowl.

‌



Following months of negotiations with cultural heritage authorities, Lazio recently submitted revised plans that lower the stadium's overall height to match neighbouring landmarks and scale back the proposed capacity from over 50,000, ensuring the original iconic canopy remains visible.

View 3 Images Must-needed building work should start next year (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The stadium opened in 1959. After being used for the Olympics the following year, it became a concert venue, with acts including Bruce Springsteen, U2, Michael Jackson, David Bowie and Pink Floyd performing there.

Lazio and Roma played a handful of games there during the 1989/90 season while Stadio Olimpico was being spruced up for the 1990 World Cup. Italy's rugby team called it when the Five Nations Championship expanded to six.

‌



View 3 Images The Stadio Flaminio in 2000 during a Six Nations game (Image: Keith Beckley/Getty Images)

However, the growth of rugby in the country saw them outgrow it and move to the Stadio Olimpico, which holds around 70,000. It is possible the national team could return to the revamped stadium in the 2030s.

Article continues below

Lazio, managed by Gennaro Gattuso, look to be a club on the up on and off the pitch as they currently top the Serie A table following an unbeaten start to the season.

Sports.title: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus slapped with six-match ban over 'match-fixing' allegations
Sports.content:
South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus slapped with six-match ban over 'match-fixing' allegations

Rassie Erasmus has received his punishment after claiming officials were guilty of “match-fixing” or “manipulation of the game or result” over on-field decisions

View 2 Images Rassie Erasmus has been banned (Image: David Rogers/Getty Images)

South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been handed a six-match ban after questioning whether officiating during his side’s defeat by France amounted to match-fixing.

‌



‌



The sanction takes immediate effect and prevents Erasmus from having any matchday involvement in international fixtures during the suspension. SA Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing for the 54-year-old.

‌



The Springboks are scheduled to complete the group stage of the Nations Championship against Ireland in Dublin on Saturday before finals weekend at Twickenham.

‌



An independent panel imposed the punishment after reviewing comments made by Erasmus at a media conference on Monday ahead of the match at the Aviva Stadium.

Referring to South Africa’s 21-19 defeat in Paris on Friday, Erasmus claimed France had committed 17 illegal hip-drop tackles which went unnoticed by the on-field officials and television match official (TMO). He questioned whether the failure to intervene could amount to “match-fixing” or “manipulation of the game or result”.

Boxer Lee Reeves dies aged 31 after brutal knockout in Dublin READ MORE :

“The TMO doesn’t come in once,” Erasmus said. “I’m not saying he’s wrong. I’m saying if he didn’t see it it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and he decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing? Is that not interfering with the outcome of a game if you see this injury that happens there?”

‌



Andrea Piardi was the referee for the Stade de France fixture, while fellow Italian Matteo Liperini was the TMO.

Erasmus later added: “If the TMO didn’t see it maybe then technology must be better. If he saw it and he ignored it, what does that boil down to? Manipulation of the game or the result.”

‌



Erasmus also predicted Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast would avoid a suspension and be free to play against the Springboks this weekend. The 23-year-old was cited for a hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato following Saturday’s match in Dublin.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Rassie Erasmus made eye-catching allegations (Image: Getty Images)

The panel ruled Erasmus’ comments crossed the threshold for serious misconduct under World Rugby’s match official abuse sanction process. It concluded the remarks suggested match officials had acted “with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match”.

‌



The panel also determined that his conduct constituted “an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of the match officials”.

Explaining the punishment, a World Rugby statement read: “The panel determined that the conduct clearly amounts to disrespecting the authority of the match officials by impugning their integrity.

‌



“Therefore, the panel reviewed a number of elements of the commentary including the timing and reach of the statements, combined with the allegations of bias or bad faith, and found that the comments attracted a six-match automatic suspension.”

The ban prevents Erasmus from coaching or having any contact with players and team management on international matchdays. He is also barred from entering stadiums and technical areas and cannot approach match officials or carry out media duties during the suspension.

‌



Erasmus has previously been suspended twice by World Rugby over comments about match officials. The governing body stressed the importance of protecting officials from abuse. “Respect is fundamental to rugby, and match officials are central to the sport,” their statement added.

“Protecting their wellbeing and integrity, and their right to perform without abuse or intimidation, is a responsibility World Rugby and unions take seriously. Coaches, players, unions and everyone in the game must uphold these standards.

Article continues below

“Robust, respectful debate is natural, but teams have access to well-established and supported channels and protocols for raising officiating matters before and after matches. Challenging a decision is not the same as questioning an official’s integrity or making comments that expose them to personal abuse.”

Sports.title: Second Man Utd rule change as Mauricio Pochettino makes offer to players ahead of Liverpool
Sports.content:
Second Man Utd rule change as Mauricio Pochettino makes offer to players ahead of Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino has already laid down two rules and introduced a new dressing room tradition for his Manchester United stars

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino looks set to make his mark at Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Mauricio Pochettino's spell at Manchester United is already looking set to be markedly different from Michael Carrick's tenure. The Argentine manager hasn't even arrived at Carrington yet and he's already implemented two fresh regulations.

‌



‌



After a dreadful opening to the season - during which United have secured just a solitary Premier League victory from 10 matches and find themselves languishing in the drop zone - the club parted company with Carrick last week.

‌



There was no hanging about when it came to appointing his successor, with former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino lured away from the United States men's national team.

‌



During Carrick's time in charge, United's players were typically granted a day off following fixtures. But under Pochettino's stewardship, they will be required to attend the training ground for recovery work after matches.

Mauricio Pochettino drops Man Utd transfer hint after January plan emerges READ MORE :

This represents one of two regulations brought in. According to The Independent, routine body-fat assessments will also be rolled out and as part of an additional tradition, the manager will host his squad for a team meal.

View 2 Images Pochettino asks a lot from his squad (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

As for new boss Pochettino's regulations, The Sun suggests they form part of a wider ambition to enhance the United squad's general conditioning.

‌



Throughout his stints with Spurs and Chelsea, Pochettino prioritised physical conditioning and earned a reputation for his demanding training methods.

United's squad will need to adjust to these changes, but Pochettino is taking steps to lift spirits within the group. Before his first match in charge against Liverpool on November 22, he'll treat all the players and staff to a meal out.

‌



This is a ritual Pochettino has typically observed on the eve of every campaign since his time as Southampton boss, though he'll tweak the arrangement and stage the meal ahead of the journey to Anfield.
