World.title: ADC faults APC over claims of sponsored rally violence
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has rejected allegations by the All Progressives Congress (APC) that it is sponsoring hoodlums to disrupt campaign rallies, insisting that Nigerians do not need opposition parties to express dissatisfaction with the economic situation in the country.

The party said public anger over the policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration should not be attributed to opposition-sponsored activities.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of attempting to portray public discontent with the government as a political plot.

Shaibu said the policies of the Tinubu administration over the past three and a half years had increased the cost of food, fuel and other basic necessities, adding that Nigerians were entitled to assess the government’s performance based on their daily experiences.

The ADC was reacting to an earlier statement by Dele Alake, spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, who accused the ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) of sponsoring hoodlums to disrupt campaign events and endanger young Nigerians.

Alake had also alleged that opposition parties were using artificial intelligence-generated images, deepfakes, fake news and sponsored protests to create tension ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He further accused the parties of mobilising young people with cudgels and directing them to chant “Bamaiyi” at APC campaign rallies.

However, the ADC questioned the allegations, particularly the circumstances surrounding the reported release of individuals arrested in connection with the incident.

The party asked the APC to provide evidence linking it to the alleged sponsorship of violence rather than making accusations against opposition groups.

“The Presidency earlier denied that the President’s motorcade had been pelted. Now the APC campaign council says people were detained for pelting the convoy with stones and that President Tinubu directed their release. Which account should Nigerians believe?” the statement asked.

It added: “If the APC has evidence that the ADC armed or sponsored those people, why were those detained released? Why have the alleged sponsors not been identified and prosecuted? A government with evidence of such a serious offence should hand it to investigators, not fling accusations at its opponents.”

The ADC denied sponsoring violence or recruiting young people to confront political opponents, saying it condemned attacks on campaigners, supporters, places of worship and public property, irrespective of political affiliation.

The party also urged the ruling APC to account for its own campaign activities, arguing that reports and images purportedly showing money being distributed at political events should also be scrutinised.

It maintained that public criticism of the government should not automatically be characterised as opposition-sponsored activity.

“Nigerians are entitled to judge this government by the cost of living and by their own daily experience. Calling their anger an opposition plot will not make it disappear,” the statement added.

World.title: Senate passes bills establishing research fund, granting medical college PhD powers
World.content:
Senate

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate has passed two bills seeking to provide a framework for research funding and expand postgraduate medical education in Nigeria.

The bills are the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill, 2026, and the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, 2026.

Both bills were passed on Wednesday after consideration of their provisions, clause by clause, at the Committee of the Whole and subsequent third reading.

Their passage followed the presentation and consideration of reports by the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, chaired by Senator Mohammed Dandutse (APC, Katsina South).

Presenting the reports, Dandutse said the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill sought to establish a sustainable funding mechanism for research, development and innovation across the country.

He said the proposed legislation also provided for the establishment of the National Council on Research and Innovation, which would provide strategic direction, policy oversight and supervision for Nigeria’s research agenda.

According to him, the proposed fund would support research institutions and provide a dedicated funding framework for addressing the country’s development challenges.

He added that the fund and the council would work together to strengthen Nigeria’s research, scientific, technological and innovation capabilities.

On the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, Dandutse said the proposed amendment sought to expand the academic and institutional functions of the college.

He explained that the amendment would empower the college to establish academic programmes and award Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in specialised medical disciplines.

The areas include clinical medicine, dentistry, basic medical sciences, pharmacology and other related fields.

Dandutse further explained that the amendment would empower the college’s Senate to develop, administer and supervise the proposed doctoral programmes.

He said the programmes would be subject to accreditation and regulation by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to ensure compliance with prescribed academic standards.

According to him, the proposed changes are intended to provide a framework for advanced medical education, clinical research and specialised medical training in the country.

World.title: World Bank threatened to cut Nigeria’s financing over subsidy — Fashola
World.content:
Fashola

Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said the World Bank warned Nigeria that it would stop financing the country unless the Federal Government removed petrol subsidy.

Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, made the disclosure on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

He said the decision to remove the subsidy was not merely a policy choice, but was also influenced by legal provisions and Nigeria’s financial position at the time.

Fashola urged Nigerians to revisit President Bola Tinubu’s inaugural address, arguing that public attention had focused largely on the declaration that “subsidy is gone” without sufficient consideration of other parts of the speech.

He also cited the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), which he said provided for petroleum products to be sold at competitive market rates, arguing that the provision had implications for any move to reinstate subsidy.

“The World Bank simply said, ‘We won’t finance your country again unless you remove subsidy.’ It was that simple,” he said.

Fashola said the issue had been discussed during the previous administration, when he was a member of the Federal Executive Council, adding that Nigeria was spending close to 90 per cent of its revenue on debt servicing.

He argued that the country could not afford to sustain the subsidy regime and challenged those advocating its restoration to explain how they intended to fund it.

The former minister also asked political opponents of the Tinubu administration to explain how they would implement an alternative policy if elected, saying some politicians who had previously supported subsidy removal had changed their positions after it became unpopular.

He said the Tinubu administration deserved commendation for maintaining the policy despite the economic difficulties it had imposed on Nigerians.

“What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on its word and saying, ‘Because the people like it, let’s bring it back.’ It was a road to perdition,” he said.

Fashola, however, acknowledged that subsidy removal had affected household livelihoods and increased the cost of living, but said the government was introducing other measures to cushion the impact.

He listed tax reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), salary adjustments and compressed natural gas (CNG) initiatives among the measures being deployed to address the economic pressures.

He also cited a decline in inflation from above 30 per cent to about 14 per cent, arguing that reversing the subsidy policy midway could disrupt the progress recorded.

The former governor recalled the Subsidy Reinvestment and Empowerment Programme (SURE-P), introduced under former President Goodluck Jonathan, as an earlier attempt to manage the proceeds from subsidy removal.

He said the programme’s chairman resigned after developing concerns about the management of its funds.

In August, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, said he would restore petrol subsidy if elected president in the 2027 general election.

World.title: DSS challenges Atiku to prove it recruited protesters in Sokoto
World.content:
…Says preliminary investigation found no evidence against operatives

…Recalls rescuing ADC governorship candidate from attack

The Department of State Services (DSS) has challenged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to provide concrete evidence to support his allegation that the agency recruited protesters to disrupt the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign rally in Sokoto State.

The secret police said its preliminary investigation into the allegation failed to establish any evidence linking its operatives to the organisation or sponsorship of protests against the ADC’s campaign activities in the state.

Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, had earlier accused the Sokoto State Government of obstructing his party’s campaign activities ahead of its rally in the state.

Addressing journalists in Abuja, the former Vice-President also alleged that the DSS recruited protesters to cause unrest and create grounds for imposing a curfew that could prevent the opposition party from holding its rally as scheduled.

However, in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Deputy Director of Public Relations and Strategic Communications of the DSS, Favour Dozie, said the agency activated its internal investigation procedures following the public allegation.

Dozie said the investigation was conducted on the directive of the Director-General of the DSS, Adeola Ajayi, and involved interviews with ADC leaders in Sokoto, party members and other relevant stakeholders.

According to the spokesperson, Atiku had specifically alleged that the ADC knew where some of the protesters were assembled and how they were allegedly deployed to strategic locations.

Quoting the former Vice-President, Dozie said: “Where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road. Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout.”

The DSS spokesperson, however, said the agency’s preliminary findings did not substantiate the allegation.

“Outcome of the preliminary investigation did not confirm the allegation, as there was no evidence to establish such,” the statement said.

In presenting its account of its activities in Sokoto, the agency recalled that on October 31, its operatives rescued Mannir Daniya, the ADC governorship candidate in the state, from an attack and evacuated him to safety.

It said two of its operatives were assaulted during the rescue operation and were receiving medical attention at the time of its earlier statement.

The agency further disclosed that Daniya subsequently contacted the State Director of the DSS to express appreciation for the intervention and request additional security reinforcement.

It also said it received letters of appreciation from the ADC state chairman and the governorship candidate, describing the correspondence as evidence of its efforts to protect political actors irrespective of their party affiliations.

Against this background, the DSS said it expected Atiku to publicly clarify his allegation or provide supporting evidence to enable further investigation.

“While the Service acknowledges the Letters of Appreciation from the ADC chairman and governorship candidate in Sokoto State, the DSS still requests that, in view of the fact that the allegation was made in public, His Excellency should set the records straight publicly or provide concrete evidence (if any) to enable further investigation,” Dozie said.

The agency added that it was open to an independent investigation into the matter.

“The Service welcomes any fair and independent enquiry into the issue,” the statement added.

The DSS said its appeal was made out of respect for the former Vice-President and in the interest of truth, fairness and the morale of its personnel, who it said risk their lives in the service of the country.

It reaffirmed its commitment to its constitutional responsibilities and the principles of professionalism and political neutrality.

World.title: Atiku questions Tinubu’s Villa interview over $4.5m US lobbying deal
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has questioned whether President Bola Tinubu’s recently recorded interview at the Presidential Villa was connected to a $4.5 million lobbying contract involving the Nigerian government in the United States.

Atiku demanded that the Presidency disclose the terms of the contract, explain the purpose of the payment and release the full, unedited interview to establish whether the recording was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement.

In a statement on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified Diana London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged to work for the Nigerian government through Aster Legal.

He said the filings showed that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but did not establish whether the presidential interview was covered by the contract.

Atiku also criticised the Presidency for presenting the recorded encounter as an interview while promoting it with photographs and a ‘coming soon’ announcement.

“When Tinubu is ready for an interview, he should let Nigerians know. He cannot invite a strategist registered to work for his government, record a publicity production and advertise Sitting on a Flat Mandate as ‘coming soon’, like a trailer from 51 Iweka Road, Onitsha.

“Hungry Nigerians are not here to market his failed movie. They have suffered through Part One of Tinubu’s government, and they will not sit through a sequel,” he said.

The former vice president also questioned London’s professional relationship with the lobbying firm and her decision to delete social media posts in which she had praised Tinubu’s administration and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States.

“After praising Tinubu’s government and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States on her social media accounts, Diana London deleted the posts. She has not explained why. Nigerians are entitled to ask what changed between the glowing praise and its disappearance,” Atiku said.

He argued that the deleted posts and questions surrounding London’s professional engagements reinforced the need for the Presidency to release the complete recording.

“Someone who could delete her own public praise of this government without an explanation has given Nigerians reason to wonder what will survive the editing of her interview. Will difficult questions and awkward answers remain in the final cut? Or will Nigerians be served a carefully redacted, defensive account that mutilates the facts? The Presidency can put those doubts to rest by releasing the full, unedited recording,” he said.

Atiku also questioned the presence of a large screen positioned within Tinubu’s line of sight during the recording, suggesting it might have been used to display prepared prompts.

“The Presidency staged a recorded publicity production, advertised it like a home video and called it an interview. It has offered no reason to believe the questions were spontaneous or that Tinubu answered without prepared prompts. If it was a genuine interview, let the Presidency release the full, unedited recording, including what appeared on that screen,” he said.

He maintained that Nigerian journalists were capable of subjecting the President to rigorous questioning, naming Rufai Oseni, Ojy Okpe, Seun Okinbaloye and Reuben Abati as potential interviewers.

“Let him sit with them live. Let him explain why food costs so much, why wages no longer cover transport, and when families can expect relief. A flattering interview cannot wipe away poverty and hunger,” Atiku said.

The former vice president further demanded to know who authorised the $4.5 million payment, where the money came from and whether public funds were used for the lobbying arrangement.

“Who authorised the $4.5 million payment, and from which public account did it come? At a time when Nigerians are told to endure the pain of fuel subsidy removal, they deserve to know whether the money saved is being spent on foreign publicity.

“My Affordable Life campaign is about making food, fuel and transport affordable again. Tinubu cannot ask families to suffer in silence while millions of dollars are committed to polishing his image. Publish the contract. Show the invoices. Release the unedited interview. Then face Nigerian journalists and answer the people,” Atiku said.

World.title: NELFUND: I dare opposition to promise scrapping scheme — Fashola
World.content:
…Says students, beneficiaries would revolt against such proposal

Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged opposition politicians to campaign on a promise to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying beneficiaries and their families would resist such a move.

Fashola, who spoke on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, described the student loan scheme introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration as one of the reforms that had eased the financial burden on families across the country.

NELFUND was established in April 2024 after Tinubu signed the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act into law to provide interest-free loans to eligible students in tertiary institutions.

As of October 3, 2026, the fund said it had disbursed more than ₦372 billion to 1,635,676 beneficiaries across 312 tertiary institutions nationwide.

Speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jigawa on November 10, Tinubu had described NELFUND as a weapon deployed by his administration to tackle poverty, insisting that the scheme would not be discontinued.

Supporting the President’s position, Fashola said the initiative was introduced to help Nigerian families cope with financial obligations, particularly rent, transportation, healthcare and education.

“This led to the creation of NELFUND to help families pay school fees and provide student allowances,” he said.

He noted that more than one million Nigerians were already benefiting from the scheme, adding that the number was increasing.

Fashola challenged opposition candidates to make the discontinuation of the programme part of their campaign promises, saying such a position would attract resistance from beneficiaries and their families.

“I challenge the opponents to promise to scrap NELFUND and see how beneficiaries and their families react. They won’t dare,” he said.

The former Minister of Works and Housing also addressed the rising cost of living, describing it as a global challenge whose effects were being felt in Nigeria.

He called for a broader understanding of the factors contributing to the economic hardship, pointing to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent global developments.

According to him, the pandemic disrupted economic activities worldwide, forcing governments to inject money into their economies to support businesses.

He said China, which he described as the world’s biggest production centre, took about two to three years to resume normal operations, contributing to supply shortages and rising prices.

Fashola also identified the Russia-Ukraine war as another factor that worsened the situation, citing disruptions to the supply of energy products, including diesel, and food commodities such as wheat.

He said increased shipping costs and war-related insurance premiums further contributed to rising prices, although the impact differed among countries depending on their locations and levels of development.

“Thirdly, there was the unexpected war in the Middle East, which further worsened the situation,” he said.

Fashola added that the conflict had brought renewed attention to the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz, with developments around the waterway influencing the cost of goods.

“Everybody now knows the Strait of Hormuz… even the tomato seller, and prices goods based on replacement costs,” he said.

World.title: Atiku’s subsidy restoration plan is ‘abracadabra’ — Fashola
World.content:
File: Babatunde Fashola

…Demands figures, details on funding, crude oil supply

Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has described former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore petrol subsidy as “abracadabra without proof”, challenging him to provide details of how he intends to implement the policy if elected president in 2027.

Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, had in August said he would restore petrol subsidy if elected in the 2027 general elections.

Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under former President Muhammadu Buhari, stated this on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

He recalled that major presidential candidates in the 2023 general elections had supported the removal of petrol subsidy, questioning what had changed to warrant a reversal of that position.

“For credibility’s sake, all major candidates, at least as at the last election, promised to remove this fuel subsidy. So what has changed?” he asked.

Fashola said politicians advocating a different approach should explain the reasons for changing their positions and provide concrete details of how they intended to sustain the proposed arrangement.

He questioned the source of funding for the subsidy, warning that its restoration could reduce allocations to state governments and undermine their ability to meet financial obligations.

“I was in a government that was paying subsidy. And the states were not getting money. So we are going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries. Is that where you want us to go?” he asked.

He urged voters to consider the financial implications of the proposal and use their votes to prevent a return to the revenue challenges experienced by state governments during the subsidy regime.

Asked whether Atiku’s proposal was unrealistic, the former minister said he wanted detailed explanations and supporting figures before reaching a conclusion.

“With the sketchy pronouncements that come with it, I want to see rigour, I want to see detail; I want to see numbers,” he said.

Fashola also questioned Atiku’s argument that increased local refining would promote competition and reduce petrol prices, asking where the crude oil required to supply domestic refineries would come from.

He explained that Nigeria’s crude oil production involved joint ventures and production-sharing contracts with international oil companies, meaning the country did not own all the crude produced.

According to him, the assumption that Nigeria could simply supply local refineries with cheap crude overlooked the fact that crude oil was traded internationally at benchmark prices.

Fashola further questioned Nigeria’s capacity to supply sufficient crude to domestic refineries, noting that the country had yet to fully optimise its production quota.

He attributed the production challenges to legacy issues, insecurity and vandalism.

“If we have refineries working, what is our current oil production quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because there are legacy issues; there are challenges with security, vandalism, and so on and so forth, so where is this magic crude oil going to come from?” he asked.

He said Atiku needed to provide evidence and demonstrate how his proposal would address the country’s crude oil supply constraints to avoid disappointing Nigerians.

“Let people choose. But without proof, it’s like abracadabra,” Fashola said.

World.title: Obi never sought US endorsement for 2027 bid — Media office
World.content:
…Says meetings with US lawmakers focused on Nigeria’s development

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA—The Media Office of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified that his recent meetings with some members of the United States Congress were not intended to secure an endorsement of his 2027 presidential ambition by the American government.

The office said Obi neither claimed to have received an endorsement from any US lawmaker, the US Congress as an institution, nor the American government.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, the spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Reach (POMR), Idris Zekeri, said the former Anambra State governor’s visit to the United States was not undertaken to seek political backing for his presidential ambition.

Zekeri described reports and interpretations suggesting that Obi had secured American political endorsement as inaccurate, stressing that such claims did not emanate from his party or campaign organisation.

According to him, Obi’s discussions with some congressional leaders and other prominent American figures centred on Nigeria’s development, the welfare of its citizens, democratic governance and the country’s strategic role in the international community.

He said the engagements also addressed the future of relations between Nigeria and the United States.

While acknowledging favourable comments made by some American lawmakers about Obi’s leadership record, POMR cautioned against presenting such remarks as an official political endorsement.

“It is essential to distinguish between meeting with individual members of Congress and engaging officially with the United States Congress as an institution. These are separate circumstances,” the statement said.

The organisation maintained that Obi believed Nigeria’s challenges required constructive engagement with international partners, mutual respect and candid dialogue with stakeholders across the world.

It said his meetings in Washington reflected this conviction rather than an attempt to secure foreign support for his political ambition.

POMR welcomed the positive reception and supportive remarks from American lawmakers but urged the media and political commentators to report the engagements accurately.

It also cautioned against embellishment, sensationalism and attributing statements to Obi that he did not make.

“The objective of the meetings with his interlocutors was to promote dialogue about Nigeria, not to obtain foreign backing for a Nigerian presidential bid,” the statement added.

World.title: Senate Sends State Police Bill to Tinubu, Demands Operational Guidelines
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Oshiomhole, others warn against political abuse

* insists on safeguards as Akpabio says new policing structure could tackle 70% of insecurity

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate on Wednesday approved the transmission of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for the establishment of State Police Services, to President Bola Tinubu for assent, following its approval by the required number of State Houses of Assembly.

However, the upper legislative chamber urged the president to expeditiously forward the proposed National Policing Bill to the National Assembly to establish operational guidelines, define the relationship between federal and state police authorities and provide safeguards against possible abuses.

The Senate’s resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, directing the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, to transmit the constitutional amendment to the president in accordance with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004.

The development marks a major milestone in Nigeria’s efforts to decentralise its policing architecture amid persistent security challenges, including terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflicts and other violent crimes.

Leading the debate, Bamidele recalled that the Senate approved the constitutional amendment on June 24, 2026, while the House of Representatives passed it on July 23, 2026, with both chambers securing the constitutionally required two-thirds majority.

He informed his colleagues that the 36 State Houses of Assembly had also transmitted their resolutions approving the amendment to the National Assembly, thereby satisfying the requirements of Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution.

Under the amendment process, the National Assembly is required to secure the support of at least two-thirds of the State Houses of Assembly before forwarding a constitutional alteration to the president for assent.

Bamidele said the Senate should recognise the completion of the constitutional requirements and proceed with the transmission of the bill.

He also commended Tinubu for providing the political leadership and support that facilitated the initiative, urging him to forward the National Policing Bill to the legislature for scrutiny and expeditious passage.

Seconding the motion, the Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, said the establishment of State Police had become necessary given the country’s worsening security situation.

He maintained that the proposed arrangement would complement the existing security architecture and strengthen the capacity of governments to respond to threats within their jurisdictions.

In his contribution, Deputy Senate President and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Constitution Review, Senator Barau Jibrin, described the development as a historic achievement for the Tinubu administration and the 10th National Assembly.

Barau said successive administrations had considered introducing State Police but failed to translate the proposal into reality.

He attributed the progress to Tinubu’s commitment, describing the proposed arrangement as a collaborative policing structure designed to strengthen the Nigeria Police Force rather than undermine it.

“This is a wonderful achievement for the present administration and the current National Assembly. As we know, this matter has been under discussion for a long time. Successive governments have considered how to introduce State Police into the country’s policing system.

“However, no administration was able to achieve this until the present government came into office. Credit must go to the president for his commitment to ensuring that this bill is passed to allow the establishment of State Police in our policing system,” he said.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio also described the constitutional amendment as one of the major accomplishments of the 10th National Assembly, expressing optimism that the new policing structure would significantly reduce insecurity.

He projected that the establishment of State Police could address as much as 70 per cent of the country’s security challenges.

“This is a legislation that will not be forgotten. It is a major achievement of the 10th National Assembly,” Akpabio said.

He, however, stressed that the next phase would be to address the operationalisation of the system and prevent conflicts between state and federal police authorities.

The most pointed intervention came from former Edo State Governor, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, who warned that the proposed State Police system must not become an instrument of political oppression in the hands of state governors.

While congratulating the Senate leadership and the president, Oshiomhole said concerns about possible abuses should not prevent Nigeria from adopting a policing structure capable of responding more effectively to local security threats.

He recalled that as governor, he had expressed reservations about the possibility of future administrations using State Police against political opponents.

Oshiomhole therefore called for comprehensive operational guidelines with the force of law to regulate the activities of the proposed security institutions.

“We can foresee the possibility of some people misusing the police, but that should not be enough reason to abandon the idea,” he said.

He added: “While we pass the bill and transmit it for presidential assent, we should also encourage the executive to send a bill addressing the operational guidelines and how State Police will function alongside the federal police.”

The former governor further warned that disagreements could arise between federal and state authorities over security responsibilities, insisting that clear legal provisions were necessary to prevent institutional conflicts.

He said the guidelines should establish limits on the use of State Police, particularly in political matters, and ensure that the initiative achieved its primary objective of making Nigeria safer.

Similarly, former Senate Leader, Senator Adamu Aliero, supported the amendment, arguing that Nigeria’s existing security architecture required an overhaul to accommodate multiple policing structures.

He said the country could eventually consider local government policing, alongside federal and state police, to address its diverse security challenges.

Also contributing, Senator Ekon Sampson said the judiciary must play a critical role in checking possible abuses through effective oversight and accountability mechanisms.

He argued that concerns about misuse should not overshadow the urgent need to strengthen Nigeria’s security institutions.

The Senate subsequently adopted all three prayers of the motion, directing the Clerk to transmit the constitutional amendment to Tinubu, commending the president for supporting the initiative and requesting the National Policing Bill.

Akpabio, in further clarification, said the executive was expected to forward the implementation framework to the National Assembly without unnecessary delay.

He, however, indicated that the legislature could initiate the necessary legislation if the executive failed to act within a reasonable period.

The Senate’s resolution has therefore shifted attention to presidential assent and the subsequent legislative framework that will determine the structure, powers, funding, accountability and operational relationship between the proposed State Police Services and the Nigeria Police Force.

World.title: Tinubu Receives State Police Constitution Alteration Bill From N’Assembly Wednesday
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which provides for the establishment of State Police in Nigeria.

All 36 State Houses of Assembly approved the Bill, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 states, as stipulated in Section 9(2) of the Constitution.

The Bill, according to a release issued by the Chief of Staff to the President, Hon Femi Gbajabiamila, was formally transmitted by the National Assembly to the president on Wednesday via his two Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and Dr. Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart respectively.

Tinubu will review the Constitution Alteration Bill in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) after which he will assent to the Bill at a formal signing ceremony.

The president expressed his appreciation to the President of the Senate, Speaker of the House of Representatives, members of the National Assembly, Clerk to the National Assembly, 36 state governors, State Houses of Assembly, and all Nigerians who have demonstrated a shared commitment to addressing the nation’s security challenges.

Gbajabiamila also disclosed that the

Presidential Working Group on State Police, which he chairs, with the support of the Policy Advisory Committee, has undertaken extensive stakeholder engagement and nationwide consultations towards developing a draft National Policing Bill.

The draft bill, he explained, has been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation.

“Upon receipt of the validated version, the Working Group will review it and present it, alongside its report, to Mr President for consideration,” the Chief of Staff further stated.

World.title: Covenant University Leads Africa, As Nigeria Records Highest Number of Varsities in THE Rankings
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

Covenant University, Ota, Ogun State, has retained its position as Africa’s top-ranked institution in the 2027 Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings, as Nigeria recorded its highest-ever number of universities in the global ranking.

The 2027 edition, released on Wednesday, November 18, featured 27 Nigerian universities, representing a 50 per cent increase from the 18 institutions ranked in 2026.

Covenant University was placed joint 49th globally, retaining its position as the only African university among the world’s top 50 for the second consecutive year.

The private university ranked ahead of Egypt’s Cairo University, which placed joint 52nd globally.

Chairman of the Nigerian Tertiary Education Ranking Advisory Committee (NiTERAC), Professor Emeritus Peter Okebukola, disclosed this in a statement issued on Wednesday in Abuja.

He said Nigeria’s performance represented an improvement from the 19 universities ranked in the maiden 2025 edition, while another seven institutions were given Reporter status after submitting data.

This brings the total number of Nigerian universities participating in the 2027 exercise to 34, compared with 30 in 2026 and 27 in 2025.

Okebukola , a former Executive Secretary of the National Universities Commission (NUC), said that Nigeria had moved from 16th to 11th position globally in terms of the number of ranked universities, maintaining its second position in Africa behind Egypt, which has 37 institutions.

The ranking, produced by THE in partnership with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 universities across 102 countries and territories.

It evaluates universities’ capacity to fund, support and deliver research cutting across scientific disciplines, using 11 performance indicators grouped into inputs, processes and outputs.

While inputs account for 19 per cent of the assessment, processes account for 16 per cent and outputs 65 per cent.

The Massachusetts Institute of Technology retained the global first position for the third consecutive year.

In Nigeria, Landmark University, Omu-Aran, emerged second, placing in the 251–300 band, while Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and the University of Ilorin occupied the 351–400 band.

The University of Calabar, University of Lagos and University of Nigeria, Nsukka, were placed in the 401–500 band. Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Obafemi Awolowo University and the University of Benin completed Nigeria’s top 10, placing in the 501–600 band.

Okebukola a former Chairman, Governing Board of the National Open University of Nigeria (NOUN), particularly commended Ahmadu Bello University and the University of Calabar for their significant improvements in the latest edition.

According to him, ABU moved from the 601–800 band in 2026 to the 351–400 band, while the University of Calabar improved from the 601–800 band to the 401–500 category.

Eight universities made their debut in the ranking. They are the Federal University of Technology, Minna; Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike; Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University, Makurdi; University of Jos; Rivers State University; Babcock University; Bells University of Technology; and Nile University of Nigeria.

Osun State University also returned to the ranking after a year’s absence.

Of the 27 Nigerian universities ranked, 14 are federal institutions, seven are state-owned, while six are privately owned.

Reacting to the performance, Okebukola said the growing number of Nigerian universities participating in the exercise was encouraging, particularly with Covenant University retaining its continental leadership.

He, however, cautioned that increased participation must be matched with improved performance, noting that Nigeria had two universities in the global top 300 in 2027, compared with five in the previous edition.

Similarly, seven Nigerian universities featured in the top 500, against eight in 2026.

The former NUC boss identified inadequate funding for interdisciplinary science research, limited dedicated research facilities, administrative support and institutional policies as some of the areas requiring urgent attention.

According to him, many Nigerian universities recorded low scores in the inputs and processes pillars, which assess funding for interdisciplinary research and institutional structures supporting collaboration across scientific disciplines.

He said universities could improve their rankings through proper reporting of research grants, income from industry partnerships and the adoption of clear institutional policies that encourage interdisciplinary research.

Okebukola commended the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, for prioritising the global competitiveness of Nigerian tertiary institutions and establishing NiTERAC to drive the agenda.

He disclosed that the committee had submitted a comprehensive report on the latest ranking, alongside recommendations, to the minister.

He added that NiTERAC, working through the League of Directors of Academic Planning and the Virtual Institute for Capacity Building in Higher Education, would support participating universities and prospective entrants in preparing stronger submissions for the 2028 edition.

The chairman also urged research-intensive Nigerian universities yet to participate in the exercise to take advantage of the opportunity.

He further disclosed that the 2026 national ranking of universities, polytechnics and colleges of education was nearing completion, with the results scheduled for unveiling at a national conference on December 15, 2026.

He expressed optimism that the national ranking exercise would strengthen institutional data management and healthy competition, ultimately improving the performance of Nigerian institutions in international rankings.

World.title: Ajakaye Vows to Push Security Reforms, Skills-Based Education if Elected
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The All Progressives Congress (APC) House of Representatives candidate for Offa/Oyun/Ifelodun Federal Constituency in Kwara State, Dr. Rafiu Ajakaye, has pledged to prioritise security, education, youth empowerment and inclusive governance through people-oriented legislation if elected in the 2027 general election.

Ajakaye, a former Chief Press Secretary to Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, said effective legislative representation must go beyond attracting constituency projects to include advocacy, accountability, problem-solving and ensuring that the voices of constituents are heard in national decision-making.

He stated this on Tuesday while featuring on the News Keg programme organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Kwara State Council, at the chapel’s secretariat in Ilorin.

The APC candidate said his decision to contest was informed by his experience in public service and conviction that political leadership should be driven by the desire to improve people’s lives rather than personal ambition.

“My aspiration is driven not by personal ambition, but by a conviction that public service offers an opportunity to create meaningful impact in society,” he said.

Reflecting on his experience in the AbdulRazaq administration, Ajakaye cited the recruitment of more than 4,700 teachers in 2021 as an example of how transparent governance could expand opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government.

He said the exercise was conducted through an open and competitive process involving online applications, examinations and interviews, insisting that employment opportunities should be based on merit rather than political connections.

“We ensured that people were employed based on their competence and qualifications, not because they knew anybody in government or had political connections,” he said.

On security, Ajakaye described insecurity as a major threat to national development, particularly in communities affected by kidnapping, banditry and other criminal activities.

He advocated stronger legislative oversight of security agencies, improved welfare and equipment for security personnel, increased recruitment and better collaboration between federal and state governments.

He also called for security policies that take into consideration the geographical realities of different communities, including forests, difficult terrain and poorly monitored rural settlements exploited by criminal elements.

“Security remains the foundation upon which every society develops,” he said, stressing that the National Assembly must ensure that security agencies receive adequate resources and are held accountable for their responsibilities.

On education, the former governor’s spokesman called for increased investment in science, technology, technical and vocational education, as well as digital learning to prepare young Nigerians for emerging opportunities in the labour market.

He argued that the education system must evolve with changing economic and technological realities, noting that many traditional occupations had been displaced by technological advancement.

“Our schools should produce innovators, entrepreneurs, professionals, artisans, researchers and responsible citizens capable of competing in an increasingly dynamic world,” he said.

Ajakaye also identified youth empowerment as a major component of his proposed legislative agenda, advocating policies that would expand access to finance, digital entrepreneurship, professional training and agricultural opportunities.

He urged young Nigerians to embrace agriculture as a viable business, rather than regarding it as an occupation of last resort.

On women’s participation in governance, he maintained that inclusive decision-making was essential to developing policies that adequately addressed the needs of different segments of society.

Citing the debate surrounding the proposed six-month maternity leave policy in Kwara State, he recalled how a female participant at a policy discussion advised that the arrangement should be optional rather than compulsory to accommodate the different circumstances of working mothers.

According to him, the experience reinforced the importance of involving women in decisions affecting their welfare.

“That is the advantage of having women at the table where decisions affecting their lives are being made, rather than men sitting down and assuming that what they consider good for women must automatically become policy,” he said.

He further argued that responsible leadership required distinguishing between what people wanted and what they genuinely needed, noting that some decisions might be difficult but necessary for the long-term interest of society.

Ajakaye promised that his approach to legislative representation would be guided by humility, fairness, accessibility, empathy and intellectual rigour, irrespective of the social status, gender, religion or political affiliation of constituents.

“My approach to legislative service will be guided by humility, fairness, intellectual rigour, accessibility and empathy,” he said.

Earlier, Chairman of the News Keg Committee, Ibrahim Alege, commended Ajakaye for his contributions to media development and support for the Correspondents’ Chapel during his tenure as the governor’s spokesman.

Alege described the APC candidate as an experienced media professional whose years in government had equipped him with valuable knowledge of political communication, media relations and public service.

He particularly acknowledged Ajakaye’s support for the chapel’s annual Press Week, acquisition of its bus, end-of-year gifts and financial assistance on different occasions.

“Indeed, there is a popular saying that once a CPS, always a CPS. We believe that experience and those professional instincts remain part of him, even outside the corridors of government,” Alege said.

He, however, stressed that the engagement was not merely an opportunity to celebrate the former CPS but a platform to examine his political ambition, legislative priorities and proposed programmes for the constituency.

Alege urged journalists to ask critical questions and demand clarity to enable the electorate make informed decisions ahead of the 2027 elections.

In his remarks, Chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel, Alhaji Biola Azeez, appreciated Ajakaye for his support and goodwill towards the chapel, expressing the union’s commitment to sustaining its cordial relationship with him.

World.title: The Salvation Army Demands Credible 2027 Polls, Urges Nigerians to Reject Electoral Violence
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Mmachi Okafor

The Salvation Army, Nigeria Territory, has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), political stakeholders, the media and the electorate to prioritise peace, transparency and national unity ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Speaking at a press parley at the church’s headquarters in Lagos, the Territorial Commander, Commissioner Friday Ayanam, described the forthcoming elections as more than a routine political exercise, saying they presented a critical opportunity for citizens to determine the country’s direction.

He outlined a five-point appeal centred on rejecting political violence, ensuring transparent electoral processes, encouraging responsible voter participation, promoting ethical journalism and sustaining prayers for the nation. He urged political leaders and party supporters to shun hate speech, intimidation, vote-buying and electoral malpractice, stressing that no political ambition justified the loss of Nigerian lives.

“Nigeria is bigger than any political party, candidate or election. Our love for this country must always be greater than our political differences,” he said. “This is a call for all of us to become agents of peace, not only in our words but also in our actions. At the end of the elections, we will still have to live together as one people and build our nation together.”

He also urged INEC and relevant government institutions to ensure free, fair, and credible elections that reflect the will of the people, noting that public confidence in the electoral process depends on ensuring every eligible vote counts.

Turning to the electorate, particularly young people and first-time voters, Ayanam urged citizens to register, obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and vote according to their conscience rather than succumb to pressure, financial inducement or intimidation.

On concerns about unemployed youths being recruited for vote-buying and electoral violence, he identified youth empowerment as a central pillar of the church’s strategic plan. He disclosed that various departments run skills acquisition and empowerment programmes to help young people become self-reliant. The church also conducts grassroots sensitisation campaigns nationwide and plans to hold a stakeholders’ seminar ahead of the elections.

Ayanam clarified that The Salvation Army is a non-partisan Christian church and international charitable organisation that neither endorses political parties or candidates nor has any partisan interest in the outcome of the 2027 elections. He said its primary concern was the wellbeing of Nigerians and the promotion of honesty, integrity, justice and service.

The engagement, themed “The 2027 General Elections: A Call for Peace, Credibility and Responsible Citizenship,” brought together senior church leaders, including the Territorial President of Women’s Ministries, Commissioner Glory Ayanam, and the Chief Secretary.

A major highlight of the parley was the unveiling of the organisation’s broadcast advocacy campaign, featuring audio-visual jingles scheduled to air on radio and television stations nationwide. The campaign reinforces the message that “election is not war”, urging Nigerians to reject fighting, ballot snatching and vote-buying while turning out peacefully to exercise their franchise.

World.title: Dayo Adedayo: Building a Destination for Nigerian History
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

He has spent decades capturing Nigeria’s defining moments through his lens. Now, Dayo Adedayo, founder of Dayo Adedayo Photography, is building a unique destination where Nigerians can learn about and rediscover their country through photography. Vanessa Obioha writes.

On his way from Lagos to London on June 19, 2003, at about 11:15 am, Dayo Adedayo had a vision. He wanted to build a structure with 37 rooms, each representing one of Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. The idea was that visitors entering each room would be able to identify the state through photographs. At the time, digital photography was not yet in practice. He, however, recorded the idea in his diary.

More than two decades later, that dream is taking shape, even though it doesn’t have 37 rooms as initially planned.

Along T.F. Kuboye Road in Lekki stands a striking structure that immediately catches the eye. Called the DAP Experience Centre, its geometric façade, composed of angular panels, intersecting lines and narrow window openings, gives it a distinctly futuristic appearance. The prominent ‘I Love Lagos’ sign in front offers an early indication of the building’s purpose.

Inside, the experience becomes more revealing. The glass doors on the ground floor are illuminated with LED lighting, a feature Adedayo expects to create a Times Square-like spectacle in New York when night falls.

Visitors are welcomed by screens suspended from the ceiling, designed to display images of Nigeria’s different states and the FCT. At one end is a café, already taken up by Sterling Bank.

There is a philosophy behind almost every architectural detail. Its three ground-floor pillars represent Nigeria’s Northern, Western and Eastern regions at independence, while its seven sides correspond to the six geopolitical zones and the FCT. There is also a garden outside that showcases indigenous Nigerian plants, while the lift features space-inspired wall tiles, an idea Adedayo says came from his son’s fascination with space. Even the slanted windows carry a message. According to him, it conveys that nothing is straight in life. The windows, 154 openings in total, he adds, represent places worth visiting across Nigeria, with QR codes allowing visitors to read about each destination.

“The whole idea is to start a conversation. Let the visitors talk about the places they have been or not been to. By the time we start doing that, people will start noticing and telling our stories,” he explains.

The narrow openings are not designed to open, but the building’s central air-conditioning system, supported by an inverter and generator, is intended to ensure adequate ventilation even during power interruptions. The building also incorporates soundproofing and cladding to create a quieter environment.

Even the staircase has a story. There are 98 steps in the building: 54 from the entrance and 44 from the exit. According to Adedayo, they represent the 98 interesting places one must visit before leaving Lagos. He gives the word ‘exit’ a double meaning: leaving the city or dying in it. A QR code beside the staircase will allow visitors to scan and read about the featured locations, while the staircase itself will be fitted with digital LED displays.

As one progresses, the more captivating the building becomes. For instance, the first level houses the digital floor, featuring 54 projectors and a massive 360-degree immersive experience designed to accommodate up to 75 people. Its walls, he says, will display photographic works that transport visitors to different parts of the country.

Also located on this floor is the documentary room. Fitted with seating resembling church pews, it will feature short documentaries about Nigerian states. The intention is for visitors to experience the stories being exhibited across the centre in a more immersive format.

Another interesting feature on the digital floor is the boat room. Here, Adedayo has created a stationary boat installation with water and turbulence effects, using mapped waterways to give visitors the sensation of travelling through Nigeria’s riverine landscapes.

“You will take the boat from Marina to the Atlantic, from the Atlantic into the Niger Delta; from the Niger Delta creeks you go straight to Onitsha where you see the Niger Bridge…”

The uppermost level is the analogue floor, where Adedayo’s office is located. Here, the hallway is transformed into a gallery of some sort, with walls displaying photographs, including one dedicated to the evolution of photography, tracing the journey from the pinhole camera to modern cameras.

A particularly distinctive feature is the darkroom, where visitors will witness how photographs are produced through the analogue process.

“Before you come into the building, you are going to take your pictures with two cameras: one analogue, one digital. For the digital, you will collect the pictures immediately before you exit our building with a fee. Then the analogue one will be processed in your presence. So you see how films are turned into negatives.”

The floor also houses a library containing his publications and other books on photography and videography. Adedayo, who has written 19 books, is preparing to publish his 20th. For him, the educational component is central to the project, particularly its potential to introduce younger Nigerians to photography.

“What I want to do is to impart knowledge to the younger generation,” he says, particularly those who may not have had the opportunity to learn photography formally.

He hopes the centre will attract school trips from different parts of the country, giving students an opportunity to understand how photography was practised in earlier times and, more importantly, to appreciate Nigeria’s history.

“But most importantly is to tell our stories,” he says. “What is left is for us to inspire, because without inspiration, nobody will aspire to be anything, and that is what I’m trying to do.”

Beyond serving as a repository of Nigerian history and culture, the DAP Experience Centre will also provide a platform for emerging photographers to exhibit and sell their works. Adedayo hopes to create a viable market that allows photographers to earn a decent living from their craft.

“The first N1 billion naira image to be sold may come from this building. It may not necessarily be my own work.”

The prospect also goes beyond the commercial value of photography. It is also an opportunity to encourage photographers to venture out and document the country’s civilisation, creating visual records for future generations.

The centre will operate largely on a digital model, with transactions handled electronically. Visitors will be required to pay before entry, with a surcharge for those who fail to comply. Each session is expected to last approximately 90 minutes. The facility is also designed with accessibility in mind, with ramps provided for visitors living with disabilities.

For Adedayo, establishing the centre as a foundation was deliberate, allowing it to attract international funding for educational and cultural initiatives.

The project is deeply personal for Adedayo. He sees it as a way of preserving his life’s work and ensuring that his extensive photographic archive survives beyond him.

“I wanted to start a foundation where all my works would be domiciled.”

With the opening scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, Adedayo says he has secured partnerships with airlines. Revenue will come from digital payments and the sale of more than 500 types of merchandise. He is confident the investment will be recouped within a year of operation. He also hopes to replicate the project in other parts of the country.

Having visited all 36 states and the FCT and photographed all 774 local government areas, Adedayo has amassed an extensive visual record of Nigeria, totalling four million. The experience centre is an attempt to bring that archive to life and, potentially, give the country’s tourism industry a new attraction.

World.title: APC Kwara South Senatorial Candidate, Adewoye, Seeks Policies to Protect Indigenous Investors
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

All Progressives Congress(APC) Kwara South Senatorial Candidate in Kwara state for 2027 election, Prince Olalekan Adewoye, has said Nigeria’s industrial development would remain constrained without deliberate policies to protect and expand the participation of indigenous investors in key economic sectors.

Adewoye, an industrialist in the steel sector stated this in Ilorin on Tuesday while speaking with newsmen on his economic development agenda for the people of the senatorial district ahead of 2027 election in the state.

He however said his proposed legislative iinterventions if elected into the senate would seek to strengthen Nigerian-owned businesses while creating opportunities for small enterprises and young entrepreneurs in the senatorial district.

Reflecting on his experience in the manufacturing industry, the APC candidate said the ownership structure of some sectors had changed significantly over the years, with Nigerian participation declining in favour of foreign interests.

“In the 1980s, ownership in some sectors was largely dominated by Nigerians, with a smaller share belonging to foreign interests.

“Today, the situation has been reversed in some of those sectors, with Nigerian participation falling below 20 per cent,” he said.

Although he did not identify the specific industries or provide supporting data for the comparison, Adewoye maintained that the trend highlighted the urgency of policies that would improve the competitiveness of local enterprises.

He said his advocacy for local content was informed by his involvement in industry associations and engagements with government institutions, including the National Assembly and relevant ministries.

According to him, industry stakeholders repeatedly sought government intervention to encourage domestic production and reduce unnecessary imports of products that Nigerian companies had the capacity to manufacture.

“More than 70 per cent of the time, we did not receive the kind of support we needed,” he said, describing the experience as one of the factors that influenced his decision to seek elective office.

Adewoye said his proposed role in the Senate would include supporting laws and policies that improve the operating environment for indigenous businesses, attract investment and encourage employment-generating enterprises.

He added that his economic agenda would also focus on the grassroots, particularly small businesses that often lack access to equipment, capital and institutional support.

The candidate disclosed that he was considering the establishment of a trust fund that would bring together individuals and organisations willing to invest in the economic development of Kwara South.

Under the proposed arrangement, he said, financial or material assistance would be provided to qualified beneficiaries based on clearly defined criteria.

“I believe the office of a senator provides an opportunity to attract development partners and bring together individuals and organisations interested in supporting the district,” he said.

He added that the proposed fund would be designed to support people with viable business ideas, with the broader objective of helping beneficiaries become economically independent and create employment for others.

Adewoye said he had commenced a needs assessment to identify the most pressing development concerns in the district, noting that the exercise would guide his legislative priorities if elected.

Beyond enterprise development, he identified healthcare and education as areas requiring sustained intervention.

He cited the activities of his foundation, which he said had supported disadvantaged children, elderly people, artisans, traders and small business operators.

The industrialist argued that public representation should not be limited to lawmaking but should also involve building partnerships capable of attracting development opportunities to constituents.

He said effective collaboration among federal, state and local governments would be important in translating policies into tangible improvements in people’s lives.

On the political implications of his candidacy, Adewoye expressed confidence that the APC would perform strongly in the 2027 elections, citing the party’s record in government and its candidate-selection process.

He maintained that his business background and community interventions would provide a basis for engaging voters, despite his lack of previous experience in elective office.

“I am convinced of my capacity and believe I have what it takes to represent the people effectively,” he said, adding that compassion and commitment to service would guide his approach to public office.

He also urged voters to compare the country’s economic and infrastructure conditions under previous administrations with the current situation before making their choices in 2027.

Adewoye called for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the continuation of APC-led governments, arguing that continuity would provide an opportunity to consolidate existing development programmes.

World.title: KWASUTH, EU Sign MoU on Quality Healthcare Delivery in Kwara
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The Management of the Kwara State University Teaching Hospital (KWASUTH) Ilorin has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the European Union- Sharah on quality healthcare delivery for the people of the state.

Already, the officials of the EU- Sharah has visited the hospital so as to ensure the successful implementation of the MoU.

The Chief Medical Director of Kwara State University Teaching Hospital (KWASUTH), Ilorin, Dr Ahmed Abdulkadir made the disclosure in Ilorin while speaking with newsmen on the sidelines of the recent false comment on the hospital.

He said the new initiative would go a long way in boosting health care delivery of the people of the state.

Dr. Abdulkadir who said the hospital has recorded over 3,000 deliveries of new born babies every month added that the development at times makes finding space difficult at the antenatal section of the women wing and this called for collaboration from the European Union to step up move to build more accommodation that would take care of the people.

He said that, the Mou would cover the infrastructure development of the hospital so as to assist the hospital to have enough accommodation that would help healthcare delivery in the state.

Dr. Abdulkadir who used the interactive session with newsmen to dismiss allegations of poor service delivery and professional misconduct levelled against the hospital by an individual on social media.

He said the hospital management constituted an investigative panel, comprising internal and external experts, to examine the allegations and establish the facts surrounding the claims.

He explained that the panel reviewed each of the issues raised and made recommendations on areas requiring improvement but could not establish evidence to substantiate some of the allegations, particularly claims relating to poor patient care.

The CMD said the hospital had established several channels through which patients could lodge complaints and seek redress, including its SERVICOM unit, customer service department and social media platforms.

According to him, a review of the available records and complaint channels did not reveal any formal complaint relating to the issues raised on social media.

He urged patients and members of the public to utilise the available complaint mechanisms whenever they experience unsatisfactory services.

Dr Abdulkadir also stressed that the hospital operated a strict financial policy which prohibited staff from collecting cash payments directly from patients, noting that payments were made through approved electronic channels.

He disclosed that the management had previously taken administrative and disciplinary measures against some personnel over issues relating to service delivery, including the transfer of staff from the pharmacy and laboratory departments.

He added that the hospital had also secured full accreditation to train specialist paediatricians for five years, describing the development as an indication of the institution’s capacity to meet the required professional and training standards.

Dr Abdulkadir maintained that the hospital remained committed to improving healthcare delivery, accountability and professional standards.

World.title: Unemployed graduate reveals the one thing stopping her SASSA SRD grant
World.content:
A North West mother holds a degree but cannot find work, and she says she cannot get the SASSA Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant either.

The woman, who is in her late thirties to early forties, has received the Child Support Grant for more than five years. She shared her experience with The South African through its SASSA grant survey.

She lives in a shared family home, where two people depend on her.



Child maintenance blocks sassa SRD grant

The mother said she tried to apply for additional government support beyond her Child Support Grant, but she was declined or gave up.

She believes child maintenance paid into her bank account is what stands between her and the SRD grant.

“What am I supposed to do if I’m not working and can’t even get SRD because I have the child’s maintenance coming through my bank account, that money is not for me, SASSA needs a better governing strategy to deal with it’s issues, their system and policies are no longer working,” she said.

Her frustration points to a problem that many caregivers face: money meant for a child passes through the parent’s account.

Degree but no job

The mother is unemployed and actively looking for work. She has a degree and says she is willing to relocate for a job.

She named unemployment as her biggest financial concern.



Her Child Support Grant does not stretch far enough. She said she regularly struggles to make ends meet and runs out of money before the month ends.

‘Their system and policies are no longer working’

The mother said her grant payments have been straightforward, with the money deposited directly into her bank account. She rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as adequate.

However, she wants change. If she could change one thing about SASSA, she would increase the grant amount.

Her story reflects the reality for many qualified South Africans who remain unemployed and depend on grants that do not cover their household’s basic needs.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: A popular Durban street was just named one of the coolest in the world
World.content:
Durban's restaurant and nightlife scene is making waves internationally, with one famous street landing a spot on a global list. Image: supplied

Durban’s Florida Road has been named one of the coolest streets in the world, putting the city’s food and nightlife scene on the international map.

The popular Morningside strip secured 20th place on Time Out‘s list of the 28 Coolest Streets in the World for 2026, published on 17 November.

The list celebrates streets around the world known for their character, architecture, food, nightlife and local culture.



Why Durban’s Florida Road made the list

Florida Road is known for its historic Victorian and Edwardian buildings, many of which now house restaurants, cafés and bars.

The street’s wide verandas reflect Durban’s warm climate, while its history dates back to when it was an affluent residential area and trams brought more people to the Berea area.

Today, it is one of Durban’s most popular entertainment strips, offering everything from Durban curries and Indian street food to halaal restaurants and cocktail lounges.

Visitors can also stop at Florida Fields for daytime café visits or explore the street’s restaurants and bars after dark.

Where to eat and drink

According to Time Out‘s write up, Florida Road has plenty to offer visitors looking to experience Durban’s food and nightlife.

Eat : Doppio Zero for spicy corn riblets and butter steak, or House of Curries for a bunny chow.

: Doppio Zero for spicy corn riblets and butter steak, or House of Curries for a bunny chow. Drink : Dukkah’s upstairs Level Up lounge for cocktails, wine and champagne.

: Dukkah’s upstairs Level Up lounge for cocktails, wine and champagne. Shop: Ike’s Books and Collectables at 48A Florida Road for second-hand books and Africana.

The recognition comes after Durban was also ranked 14th on Time Out‘s list of the Best Places to Travel in 2026.



EThekwini Municipality welcomed the latest accolade, saying Florida Road captured Durban’s multicultural identity through its food, architecture and hospitality.

The City credited local businesses, residents as well as visitors for helping make the street one of Durban’s most recognisable lifestyle destinations.
