World.title: Katotobwe pushes for quality export products
World.content:
Minister of Trade and Export Development Caroline Katotobwe has urged Zambian manufacturers to prioritise product quality, timely delivery and understanding international market requirements to build sustainable export businesses.

Ms Katotobwe said securing consistent export orders is critical to strengthening Zambia’s competitiveness and growing the country’s export earnings.

Speaking during the commissioning of British American Tobacco (BAT) Zambia Plc’s first export shipment, Ms Katotobwe urged manufacturers to look beyond the domestic market and pursue opportunities across regional and continental markets.

Ms Katotobwe also called on manufacturing companies to invest in skills development, particularly among young people and women, to broaden their participation in industrial growth.

She noted that the expansion of manufacturing activities should translate into meaningful opportunities for local businesses and the wider population.

The Minister said BAT Zambia’s entry into export markets was an important step in advancing the Grow Zambia Agenda, which prioritises industrialisation, export growth and economic diversification.

“A shipment is an achievement, but sustained orders are what establish a reliable export business,” she said.

And The Tobacco Board of Zambia Executive Director, Robert Mwale said the first export of locally manufactured products by British American Tobacco (BAT) Zambia demonstrates the country’s potential to strengthen local manufacturing and expand its participation in international trade.

Mr Mwale said the development would contribute to value addition, job creation, skills and technology transfer, as well as increased foreign exchange earnings.

“Today’s milestone demonstrates what can be achieved when investment, manufacturing capacity, regulatory coordination and access to markets come together,” he said.

Mr Mwale further called on manufacturers and investors to explore Zambia’s export opportunities while ensuring compliance with national laws and international standards.

“We must continue to uphold national laws and international standards as we pursue export opportunities,” he said.

Meanwhile, BAT Zambia Managing Director Mukubesa Maliande said the development was expected to contribute to national export earnings, attract additional investment and create direct and indirect employment opportunities.

Mr Maliande said the company was committed to making exports a regular activity rather than a one-off achievement, with ambitions to increase export volumes year on year.

He added that BAT Zambia would continue working with the Zambia Development Agency (ZDA), Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) and the Lusaka South Multi-Facility Economic Zone to ensure efficient movement of future export consignments.

“We are committed to making exports a regular activity and growing our export volumes year on year,” he said.

The Zambia Association of Manufacturers (ZAM) Vice President South, Eugene Chungu urged local manufacturers to expand into regional and international markets to strengthen export earnings and diversify the economy.

Mr Chungu said increased participation in export markets would broaden Zambia’s productive base, create employment and reduce dependence on a limited range of exports.

He said the first export consignment by British American Tobacco (BAT) Zambia was a positive development for the manufacturing sector and the country’s export diversification agenda.

“Export growth is essential to strengthening our manufacturing sector and diversifying the economy,” he said.

World.title: Kasempa Council gives vendors ultimatum
World.content:
Kasempa Town Council has given street vendors and motorbike operators in the Central Business District (CBD) up to November 24, 2026, to vacate undesignated trading places.

Council Public Relations Officer, Mukosela Kasalwe, disclosed that all affected traders must remove their goods, merchandise and confine their businesses to designated markets and trading areas.

Mr Kasalwe said this in an interview with Zambia News and Information Services (ZANIS) in Kasempa today.

“All street vendors operating within the Kasempa Central Business District and persons conducting trade and business within verandas are required to vacate and remove all goods, merchandise and personal belongings from the said areas by November 24,” he added.

Mr Kasalwe said street vendors have been advised to contact the Market Master for allocation of trading stands, while motorbike operators have been directed to relocate to an area near the main market.

He further warned that anyone found trading in undesignated areas after the deadline will face enforcement action.

“Any person found vending or remaining in the undesignated areas shall be removed and prosecuted in accordance with the law,” he added.

Mr Kasalwe urged all affected traders and motorbike operators to comply with the notice and move to their designated areas.

World.title: Kamboni challenges Universities to improve curriculum
World.content:
Minister of Education Harry Kamboni has challenged universities and professors to re-examine the curriculum, arguing that historically, Africans were only taught to read and write and not to be innovative and creative.

He said Zambia must add value to its raw materials instead of exporting raw, saying that adding value creates jobs and improves lives.

Mr Kamboni said education must produce a learner who can use his environment to earn a living, and not one who after 12 years of school and four years of tertiary education is still looking for employment.

The Minister was speaking when he received a donation of food and essential items from the University of Lusaka to support 20 schools in Lusaka.

The donated hampers include 800 trays of eggs, 100 bags of 25 kilogramme breakfast meal, tea bags, a 101-kilogram bale of white sugar, 100 bales of tissue among several essential items.

The Minister applauded the university and its partners, saying the gesture shows the important role institutions of higher learning can play in complementing the government’s efforts.

” As a University we saw from inception to date, you are doing a commendable job by partnering with the Government on policy actualisation” he said.

The Minister further urged the government to continue expanding the school feeding programme and called on corporate bodies, faith-based organisations, non-governmental organisations, institutions of higher learning and well-meaning citizens to emulate the gesture by UNILUS.

And Deputy Vice Chancellor Academics, Bryson Mumba, speaking on behalf of UNILUS Vice Chancellor, Pinnalow Chifwanakeni said the donation of assorted items has reaffirmed the institution’s social corporate responsibilities.

“We are donating assorted items to 20 schools in Lusaka and we hope the gesture will be of significant help to the schools and government” he said.

He emphasised the need for the corporate world to support government policies if the country is to achieve set goals for the grow Zambia Agenda.

Kelly Hikalunga, a Head teacher at Prince Takamado has assured of accountability of the items received.

Meanwhile, grade 11 pupil Faides Moyo at Chaisa secondary school has appreciated the gesture saying the feeding program and free education policy is playing a major role in pupils performance in school.

World.title: Burundi dents Chipolopolo AFCON qualification hopes
World.content:
Chipolopolo’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) have suffered a setback following a 1-1 draw against Burundi away in Bujumbura on match-day four.

Zambia have now collected five points from a possible 12, after two draws, one win and one defeat.

With two matches remaining – at home against Algeria and away to Togo between 22 and 30 March 2027 – Zambia have complicated their chances of reaching the tournament.

At Stade Intwari, Zambia needed a late equaliser to force a draw after Burundi had taken a second-half lead through a controversial goal.

Chipolopolo protested the goal scored by Bonfilscaleb Bimenyimana after 78 minutes, alleging it was scored from an offside position.

Zambia equalised through Red Arrows defender Zephania Phiri five minutes before full time to earn a point.

Phiri was introduced in the 73rd minute to replace fellow full-back Mathews Banda.

The result has seen Chipolopolo drop from second to third place in Group I after Togo beat Algeria 3-0 later on Tuesday night.

Algeria top Group I with seven points, followed by Togo on six, Zambia on five and Burundi on three.

The top two teams in the group will qualify for the 2027 AFCON to be hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

Meanwhile, football writer Kenney Mbewe said Chipolopolo’s performance in Tuesday’s match was better than what was witnessed at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium last Friday, where Burundi also held Zambia to a 1-1 draw in the first leg.

“The performance by Chipolopolo in Tuesday’s match against Burundi was better compared to what we witnessed at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium last Friday. The team was able to string some decent passes; the only challenge was finding the back of the net,” Mbewe said.

“Kings Kangwa stood out for me. Albert Kangwanda should be blamed for the draw. Chanka Zimba is not good enough and I wonder why they even call him to the national team,” he said.

“Kennedy Musonda is better than Zimba. Fashion Sakala has been failing to show leadership. He has been below average, maybe the armband should be transferred to another player. We cried for Joshua Mutale, chance was given but failed to impress apart from falling.”

Mbewe, however, hailed the backline anchored by Power Dynamos central defender Dominic Chanda.

“David Hamansenya, Mathews Banda, Ricky Chanda, Miguel Chaiwa, Dominic Chanda and keeper Willard Mwanza were impressive,” he said.

World.title: Malawian national dies under unclear circumstances
World.content:
A 50-year-old Malawian national has died under unclear circumstances in Chama District of Eastern Province.

Eastern Province Police Commissioner, Robertson Mweemba, has confirmed the incident that occurred on November 15, 2026 around 07:00 hours at Kunke Village in Chief Kambombo’s Chiefdom.

He says the deceased has been identified as Phiri Silika, 50, a Malawian national who had illegally entered Zambia in search of manual labour, together with his wife Joyce Remison, 43.

Mr Mweemba explains that on 24th October, 2026, Mr Silika was employed to do tobacco farming by Aaron Mtonga, a Headteacher at Bambanda Primary School.

“On 14th November 2026, Mr Mtonga gave the deceased K50 to buy soap, but Silika went to Kamfutu market square for a drinking spree and did not return home that day. The following day, Silika was found by Chisomo Banda at the tobacco field in a drunken state and could not stand,” he narrates.

Mr Mweemba added that a few minutes later, Silika suddenly stopped talking and became unconscious.

“His co-worker checked on him and discovered that he was not breathing. He rushed to inform their employer, who informed the village headman,” Mr Mweemba stated.

He said the deceased’s relatives from Mbalachanda in Malawi were also notified.

“Community police from Malawi inspected the body and the family authorised the village headman to bury the body on the Zambian side at Katabazika burial site as no foul play was suspected.

Mr Mweemba said an inquiry file has since been opened.

World.title: Zimbabwe pushes AU for continental recognition of TVET qualifications by 2030
World.content:
Local

Valentine Maya · November 18, 2026

ORAN, Algeria. Zimbabwe has called on the African Union Commission to deliver a continental system for mutual recognition of technical and vocational qualifications by 2030 and it has been included in the four proposals written into the Oran Declaration on the Future of Skills in Africa.

Higher and Tertiary Education minister Frederick Shava tabled the proposals on Tuesday at the Ministerial Roundtable of the African Skills Policy Forum. The forum hosted by Algeria’s Ministry of Vocational Training and Professional Education and the AU Commission runs from 16 to 18 November

“The African Union Commission should accelerate a continental mechanism for mutual recognition of TVET qualifications, building on existing national, regional and continental qualifications frameworks. This would strengthen skills portability, labour mobility and regional economic integration,” said Shava

He also urged the development of an African Qualifications Passport.



“We encourage the development of an African Qualifications Passport, building on national and continental qualifications frameworks, to facilitate recognition of TVET qualifications and the movement of skilled professionals across borders,” he said.

The draft Oran Declaration is due to be presented to delegations for possible adoption before the forum ends.

Zimbabwe’s other proposals are a biennial African Skills Competition Calendar, a Continental TVET Trainer Mobility Programme and a regular reporting mechanism for the declaration.

On the calendar, minister Shava said a predictable biennial calendar, aligned with WorldSkills Africa and WorldSkills International cycles, would enable countries to plan, mobilise resources and prepare competitors systematically.

The trainer programme would offer funded short-term exchanges and placements for instructors, assessors and institutional managers, including industrial attachments and exposure to modern production technologies, with priority given to emerging and under-resourced TVET systems.

Zimbabwe also wants the declaration to become what minister Shava called a living implementation mechanism, with regular progress reporting against measurable indicators, including apprenticeships created, trainers exchanged, qualifications recognized, industry partnerships established, competitors prepared and youth employment outcomes achieved.

Minister Shava said Zimbabwe is preparing for its first WorldSkills International competition in 2028 and said it welcomes trainer exchanges, technical expert placements and joint preparation with African partners.

He also acknowledged shortages at home, citing the 2018 National Critical Skills Audit, which reported a national critical skills level of 38.25 percent, with significant deficits in engineering, technology, and natural and applied sciences.

“Critical skills shortages continue to constrain productivity and industrial growth, however industry participation must move from consultation to investment and ownership,”he said

He said access and financing remain uneven, particularly for the informal economy and underserved communities.

Shava continued saying Zimbabwe’s Integrated Skills Expansion Outreach Programme (ISEOP) has certified 15,338 artisans through industrial trade testing and deployed 12,819 trainees into local infrastructure projects. Its apprenticeship programme splits training into 20 percent institutional theory and 80 percent supervised workplace learning.

Training is financed through the Zimbabwe Manpower Development Fund (ZIMDEF), supported by a one per cent training levy on registered employers. He said ZIMDEF spent about US$187.5 million during the 2021 to 2025 National Development Strategy 1 period.

Addressing the roundtable’s second session on artificial intelligence and the future of work, he said TVET must move beyond preparing people to occupy existing jobs.



“It must equip them to create enterprises, operate modern industries, adapt to technological change and contribute directly to national development,” said Shava

Minister Shava closed by urging delegates to act rather than only declare saying Zimbabwe has not come to Oran with a finished blueprint but have come with an evolving system, a willingness to share our experience and a strong commitment to learning from our African partners.

“Let us move beyond declarations to implementation, beyond training for qualifications to training for productivity,” he said.

World.title: Kenya: Kenya's 'World-Class' Stadium Gears Up for Historic Inauguration
World.content:
interview

Kenya is undertaking massive preparations as it gears up to co-host the 36th edition of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON 2027) alongside Uganda and Tanzania. This will mark the first time the tournament takes place in East Africa since Ethiopia hosted the 10th edition in 1976. Construction work is nearing completion on the 60,000-capacity Raila Odinga International Stadium (formerly known as Talanta Stadium). Ahead of its historic January 5 inauguration, the CEO of the AFCON 2027 Local Organising Committee, Tony Lungaho, told AllAfrica's Boakai Fofana that the occasion will bring two of Europe's most celebrated football clubs - FC Bayern Munich and Ajax Amsterdam - to Nairobi for a landmark clash.



Please give us an overview of what is expected to happen in January.

To understand January, it helps to look at how this idea started. After Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda won the bid to host AFCON 2027 - and with the African Nations Championship (CHAN) coming first - I went on benchmarking trips to the CAF Champions League final and the AFCON final.

When I returned, I realized the capacity gap was too wide. It is unfair to ask a Local Organizing Committee (LOC) of nearly 400 people to execute a major tournament without prior hands-on experience. Since it is too expensive to fly 400 people abroad to observe major finals, we decided to bring that caliber of event home.



Second, we have built the most technically advanced stadium in Africa - the only venue on the continent combining a virtual offside line, a native VAR system, and goal-line technology. A stadium of that standard deserved an equally historic inauguration.

In January, for the first time in history, two UEFA Champions League-winning sides will clash on African soil. At first, clubs were hesitant because it had never been done in Africa before. By pulling this off, we are opening the door for the continent to experience top-tier global football right at its doorstep.

The first phase of tickets has already sold out. What does that say about anticipation in Kenya and the wider region?

It is complete vindication. People initially questioned our choice of teams, but African fans are discerning - when you deliver a superior product, they show up.

Selling out in eight minutes is practically unheard of. It proves our new ticketing system - which allows fans to select exact seats, understand their matchday experience, and pay across multiple financial platforms - works seamlessly. We have even sold tickets to fans in Colombia, Kazakhstan, Turkey, and Armenia. If we make it possible, the world will come to Africa.

Have you factored in affordability for ordinary fans in Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania?

Absolutely. Tickets start at €15 to keep them as accessible as possible, while ensuring the event sustains itself through ticket sales and sponsorships without relying on government money.

To lower the barrier further, we introduced mobile-money installment plans, allowing fans to pay off a €15 ticket in €2 increments over seven months. Cost is usually the biggest obstacle keeping Africans from top-tier sports; this is a model that can be replicated across all 54 countries.

So you are using this match as a live test case for AFCON 2027?

Exactly. While we have partnered with international experts to ensure world-class execution, our own LOC staff are embedded directly into functional roles. All 400 committee members will gain real-time operational experience that we can refine ahead of 2027.

Beyond the match, building a stadium is one thing; making it financially viable is the true legacy. This venue will double as a premier concert and entertainment hub for our creative economy.

As head of the LOC, how are broader infrastructure preparations shaping up for AFCON?

Hosting AFCON relies on four pillars: competition venues, hospitality and healthcare, transport infrastructure, and the fans.

Kenya already has strong roads, airports, and hospitals. The missing piece was sports infrastructure. Talanta Stadium is 96% to 98% complete ahead of our November 30 handover. Meanwhile, Kasarani - which stood for 40 years and successfully hosted CHAN - now features an advanced Monaco-Bermudagrass hybrid pitch. Launching Talanta signals that Kenya is 100% ready to host the biggest football party Africa has ever seen.

What were your biggest takeaways from hosting CHAN, and what will you improve for AFCON?

Our biggest lesson was underestimating Kenyan enthusiasm. Even matches not featuring Kenya drew massive crowds; during the Morocco vs. Madagascar final, fans packed the stadium to capacity and even sang the Moroccan national anthem.

Close 

Going forward, we need tighter stadium crowd-flow controls, alongside more public fan zones and free-to-air broadcasts to absorb overflow demand. Aside from crowd management, CAF rated CHAN the most successful edition ever held.

What about the national team's readiness on the pitch?

As our Minister often says, we cannot build world-class stadiums just for other nations to shine in. We have heavily resourced the Harambee Stars, with a rigorous preparation program running through June next year. Any team facing Kenya won't just play 11 men—they will the millions of fans.

Finally, how are you leveraging this moment for grassroots football?

Kenya last hosted a multi-sport event of this scale 40 years ago during the 1987 All-Africa Games. Beyond upgrading six major stadiums to AFCON standards, we are building 29 community grounds - without using taxpayer money - to nurture young talent. Giving kids the chance to watch Africa's best players in accessible hometown venues will be the defining legacy of 2027.

With Kenya now visa-free for fellow Africans, we are inviting the continent and the world to join us for a once-in-a-generation experience.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 18, 2026
World.content:
press review

South Africa Reprimands Nigerian Envoy Femi Fani-Kayode Over Broadcast Dispute

South Africa has formally reprimanded Nigeria's new High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, following a public dispute with the Presidency over the broadcasting of his credentials ceremony. The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) summoned him, with Director-General Zane Dangor reminding him to raise diplomatic concerns through the relevant foreign ministries rather than directly with the president. Fani-Kayode had accused the Presidency of deliberately excluding his introduction and speech from an SABC livestream, a claim disputed by President Cyril Ramaphosa's spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya. The Presidency maintained that Ramaphosa had simply directed the commissioner to raise his concerns with the appropriate SABC official. DIRCO said diplomats are required under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations to conduct official business through foreign ministries. The incident comes amid already strained relations between the two countries over allegations of xenophobic attacks and deaths of Nigerian nationals in South Africa.

Ugandan Politician Besigye's Wife Renews Calls for His Release Over Health Fears

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The wife of detained Ugandan opposition leader Kizza Besigye, Winnie Byanyima, has renewed calls for his release, citing serious concerns about his deteriorating health and need for specialised medical treatment. Besigye was arrested in Kenya's capital, Nairobi. He was abducted and taken to Uganda, where he was first charged with treason before his case was transferred to the civilian justice system. Byanyima said that he is experiencing difficulties walking, speaking, and using his hands. His family remains concerned about inadequate medical care under military surveillance. She said that soldiers remain stationed inside and around the hospital room where he is being held, raising further concerns about his welfare. His defence team has also questioned his fitness to stand trial. They argued that his communication difficulties prevent him from properly participating in his defence. Four bail applications have reportedly been rejected, while another is awaiting a hearing date. His next court hearing is scheduled for 25 November.

UN Says Over 2,230 Civilians Killed in Sudan Conflict Since January

At least 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan between January and October 2026, including more than 1,630 in drone strikes, according to the UN Human Rights Office. Its latest report highlights the growing use of drones by warring parties, with attacks targeting markets, hospitals, schools, fuel facilities and other essential infrastructure. The Kordofan region recorded more than two-thirds of verified civilian deaths. Attacks on electricity and fuel infrastructure have disrupted healthcare, water supplies and food production. During the first half of the year, the UN documented at least 39 drone strikes on markets, 20 attacks on civilian vehicles and 16 strikes on healthcare facilities. It warned that the actual death toll is likely considerably higher because its figures include only verified cases. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said the violations could amount to war crimes and called for accountability and greater protection of civilians.

Guinea Jails 224 Over Illegal Gold Mining

A court in Guinea has sentenced 224 people, including 22 former regional administrators and 202 alleged illegal gold miners, over unauthorised mining activities in the northeastern Siguiri region. The former officials received two-year prison sentences. The miners were sentenced to three years for offences including environmental destruction, water pollution and illegal mining. Foreign nationals among those convicted were also banned from Guinea for 10 years. The sentences form part of a wider government crackdown aimed at protecting farmland, rivers and the environment from damage caused by illegal mining. The operation has triggered violent clashes between protesters and security forces, leaving 10 people dead and 13 injured. More than 1,200 artisanal miners have been arrested in November. Thousands have fled across the border into Mali, with many awaiting transportation back to their home countries, including Burkina Faso.

Ethiopia-Eritrea Fighting Reignites, Raising Fears of Wider War

Fighting has resumed along the Ethiopia-Eritrea border, raising fears of a wider conflict in the Horn of Africa as relations between the neighbours continue to deteriorate. Ethiopian government forces have pushed Tigrayan fighters to the Eritrean border, with reports of skirmishes and artillery fire near the contested town of Badme. Tensions have also been heightened by Ethiopia's repeated demands for access to the Red Sea, including references to Eritrea's Assab port. The town of Badme remains a sensitive territorial issue between the two countries, even with a peace agreement that awarded the town to Eritrea after their war from 1998-2000. Relations between Ethiopia and Sudan have deteriorated at the same time amid accusations of interference in each other's conflicts, including claims by Sudan that Ethiopia is backing Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, which Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates deny. Analysts warn that proxy involvement could intensify, although direct military confrontation between Ethiopia and Sudan is considered less likely for now.

Close 

Mozambican Opposition Leader Venâncio Mondlane Goes on Trial Over Post-Election Unrest

Mozambican opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane has gone on trial at the Supreme Court over charges including terrorism-related offences, incitement and civil disobedience linked to deadly protests following the disputed 2024 elections. Mondlane, who denies wrongdoing, maintains that his calls for demonstrations were aimed at demanding electoral transparency after he challenged the victory of ruling Frelimo party candidate Daniel Chapo. Prosecutors accuse him of encouraging unrest that resulted in deaths, property damage and disruption of public services. He faces up to 24 years in prison if convicted of the most serious charge. The trial has prompted tight security in Maputo, with police urging citizens to remain calm and avoid actions that could threaten public order. Access to the proceedings has been restricted to selected media organisations, while live broadcasts have been banned over concerns about possible unrest. The case is widely viewed as a major test of Mozambique's political stability, nearly two years after the disputed elections triggered one of the country's deadliest post-election crises.

World.title: South Africa: ANC Postpones Media Briefing on Coalition Talks - South African News Briefs - November 18, 2026
World.content:
press review

ANC Postpones Media Briefing on Coalition Talks

The African National Congress (ANC) has postponed its scheduled media briefing on coalition negotiations, citing ongoing and extensive discussions, reports EWN. Party Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula is set to brief the media on progress at a revised date. The postponement comes after the ANC suffered major losses in the recent municipal elections. It lost its position as the largest party in Gauteng's three metros to the Democratic Alliance (DA).

Two Killed in Suspected Gang Shooting on Cape Flats

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Two people have been killed and three others wounded in a suspected gang-related shooting in Seawinds, Lavender Hill, on Cape Town's Cape Flats, reports SABC News. The victims, two men in their thirties, were declared dead at the scene. A 53-year-old woman was among those injured. Police said that occupants of a vehicle drove up to the group and opened fire before fleeing. Police visibility has been increased in the area. Operation Prosper deployments are conducting crime prevention operations to restore calm.

Sport Minister Urges Athletes to Secure Own Sponsorships

Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture Gayton McKenzie has urged athletes to secure individual sponsorships, reports EWN. He said that the government cannot afford to fully fund all sporting federations and their athletes. His comments follow Olympic swimmer Tatjana Smith's decision to withdraw from representing South Africa amid a sponsorship dispute with Swimming South Africa (SSA) over competing in national team sponsor Arena's apparel despite her personal Speedo sponsorship. McKenzie said federations should support athletes in securing individual deals rather than penalising them. He has demanded clarity on the sponsorship agreement while apologising to Arena for being caught up in the controversy.

World.title: Egypt: CPJ Urges Congress to Raise Press Freedom Violations With Egypt Foreign Minister
World.content:
On Tuesday, the Committee to Protect Journalists sent a letter to members of the U.S. Congress, urging lawmakers to raise Egypt's unprecedented decline in press freedom during Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty's visit to Washington, D.C. this week. The letter called on Congress to use all available diplomatic tools, including U.S. Foreign Military Financing (FMF), to press Egypt to end its criminalization of independent journalism.

In less than two months, Egyptian authorities arrested six journalists from the investigative platform Matsadaash -- who remain in detention on terrorism and false news charges -- and convicted Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah of running the outlet without a license, fining her nearly US$54,000 and ordering the closure of the outlet. Attalah also faces a separate case stemming from Mada Masr's coverage of the war on Gaza, in which she was secretly sentenced in absentia to one year in prison. A hearing in that case is set for Wednesday, November 18, and her appeal in the closure case is set for November 25.

The crackdown coincided with the decision on October 1 by President Donald Trump to waive human rights conditions on $320 million in FMF for Egypt. Asked on November 10 about the crackdown, Secretary of State Marco Rubio described Egypt as a "reliable and good defense partner of the United States."



CPJ called on Congress to make clear that continued U.S. military aid is dependent on Egypt releasing the six Matsadaash journalists, reversing the closure of Mada Masr, ending the legal intimidation of Attalah, granting licenses to independent outlets and unblocking news websites, and amending Article 6 of Media Law No. 180 of 2018 so outlets can be established by notification rather than prior authorization.

Egypt remains one of the world's leading jailers of journalists, with 25 currently behind bars.

Read the full letter here.

World.title: Africa: World Governments Summit Sets Agenda for Latin America and Caribbean Talks
World.content:
press release

Mohammad Al Gergawi

Expanding cooperation, aligning visions and building global partnerships are essential to creating major opportunities and a more prosperous future

Víctor Bisonó

Hosting the Dialogue opens new opportunities for the Dominican Republic to strengthen international relations

Dialogue at a glance

10 heads of state and prime ministers to participate in the Dialogue

UAE government delegation led by Sheikh Shakhboot bin Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan to participate in the Dialogue

More than 70 speakers and representatives from more than 30 countries

35 sessions and 15 high-level meetings and engagements to explore the future of government, the economy, investment and regional and international cooperation

More than 120 leading private-sector companies and institutions

Under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, the World Governments Summit Organization has announced the agenda for its Latin America and the Caribbean Dialogue. Organised in partnership with the Government of the Dominican Republic and the Center for Analysis for Public Policies (CAPP), the Dialogue will take place in Cap Cana on 20 and 21 November under the patronage and in the presence of His Excellency Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic.

The agenda features 35 sessions and 15 high-level meetings and engagements, with more than 70 speakers, representatives from more than 30 countries, and more than 120 private-sector companies and institutions. Sessions will focus on six themes: geoeconomics and strategic investment, tourism, culture and experience economies, international cooperation and regional integration, the future of government, logistics and global connectivity, and human capital and the future of work.

The Dialogue will bring together heads of state and government, ministers, leaders of international organisations and economic institutions, and representatives of major global companies. It will provide a platform to expand cooperation among governments, explore development and investment opportunities, and build partnerships that connect regional potential with global opportunities. The Dialogue will also help shape shared priorities for the future of the economy, development and government. Participants include H.E. Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic, H.E. José Raúl Mulino, President of the Republic of Panama, H.E. Rodrigo Paz Pereira, President of the Plurinational State of Bolivia, H.E. Nasry Asfura, President of the Republic of Honduras, the Hon. Philip Davis, Prime Minister of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas, the Hon. Dr. Natalio Wheatley, Premier of the British Virgin Islands, the Hon. Brigadier (Ret'd) Mark Phillips, Prime Minister of the Co-operative Republic of Guyana H.E. María José Pinto, Vice President of the Republic of Ecuador, and H.E. Félix Ulloa, Vice President of the Republic of El Salvador. They will be joined by H.E. Albert Ramdin, Secretary General of the Organization of American States (OAS), H.E. Shaikha Al Nuwais, Secretary General of UN Tourism, and H.E. Noemí Espinoza Madrid, Secretary General of the Association of Caribbean States (ACS).

The UAE ' s official delegation will be led by H.E. Sheikh Shakhboot bin Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, Minister of State. It will include H.E. Noura AlKaabi, Minister of State at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Mohammad Alhawi, Undersecretary at the Ministry of Investment, H.E. Dr. Alsaghira Alahbabi, Head of Mission, UAE Ambassador to the Republic of Paraguay and Director of the American Affairs Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mohamed Yousef Al Sharhan, Managing Director of the World Governments Summit Organization, and other government officials.

The Dialogue's 35 sessions and 15 high-level meetings and engagements will bring together more than 70 speakers, representatives from more than 30 countries, and more than 120 private-sector companies and institutions. Its six themes cover geoeconomics and strategic investment, tourism, culture and experience economies, international cooperation and regional integration, the future of government, logistics and global connectivity, and human capital and the future of work.

The Dialogue builds on the World Governments Summit's role in convening governments, decision-makers, institutional leaders and experts. It connects expertise with policymaking and creates opportunities to share experience and develop partnerships. The initiative strengthens ties between the UAE and Latin America and the Caribbean and supports cooperation that can deliver lasting economic and development benefits.

Mohammad Al Gergawi highlights the Summit's role in helping governments respond to global change

H.E. Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs and Chairman of the World Governments Summit Organization, said strengthening dialogue and cooperation among governments was a strategic priority as countries respond to global shifts and work towards a more prosperous future. He added that shared priorities and effective cross-border partnerships were essential to seizing opportunities, addressing challenges and turning ambitions into tangible development outcomes that improve people's lives.

He said Latin America and the Caribbean had considerable economic, human and strategic potential, as well as promising opportunities to strengthen their role in the global economy. Dialogue with governments across the region would expand opportunities to share expertise, develop partnerships and identify new areas for integration and investment, supporting sustainable growth and prosperity.

He added that the World Governments Summit had established itself as a global platform that connects knowledge with decision-making and gives governments access to experience and expertise from around the world. This enables them to anticipate change, develop more innovative and efficient ways of working, and find practical solutions that improve quality of life.

Dominican Republic highlights opportunities to strengthen international ties

H.E. Víctor Bisonó, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Dominican Republic, said hosting the Dialogue would strengthen international relations and reinforce the country ' s position as an investment destination and a strategic gateway linking Latin America and the Caribbean with other regions.

He said the Dialogue offered an opportunity to build on the Dominican Republic's international engagement, deepen bilateral ties and explore new avenues for investment and development in the country and the region. Partnerships and stronger frameworks for cooperation would support economic growth and open up new opportunities.

Dialogue explores global opportunities and the future of international cooperation

The Dialogue will open with remarks by H.E. Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic, followed by a main address on behalf of the UAE Government and remarks by Mohamed Yousef Al Sharhan, Managing Director of the World Governments Summit Organization.

A presidential dialogue titled "Governments and the New Geography of Opportunity" will bring together H.E. Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic, and H.E. José Raúl Mulino, President of the Republic of Panama. The discussion will examine how governments can use technology, trade and investment to shape new economic corridors, strengthen regional competitiveness and identify opportunities for growth and integration in the global economy.

The agenda includes a session titled "What Role Will Governments Play in Shaping the Next Tourism Destination?" Participants include the Hon. Dr. Natalio Wheatley, Premier of the British Virgin Islands, H.E. Harris Whitbeck, Director General of the Guatemalan Institute of Tourism (INGUAT), H.E. Shaikha Al Nuwais, Secretary General of UN Tourism, and Elena Martínez, Co-founder and CTO of SOS Biotech.

H.E. Albert Ramdin, Secretary General of the Organization of American States, will speak in "Threats to Peace: Ways to Mitigate and Resolve Them". The session will examine how diplomacy, preventive action and regional cooperation can help governments anticipate tensions and build lasting peace.

Artificial intelligence, investment and natural resources shape discussions on future economies

Sessions will examine the changes reshaping global economies, the opportunities created by technology, artificial intelligence, investment and innovation, and how countries can turn national assets and natural resources into lasting economic value.

"Global Insights: AI, Investment & New Economic Frontiers" will examine how AI, investment and connectivity are shaping the region's economy and the decisions facing its leaders. The session will feature the Hon. Philip Davis, Prime Minister of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas, H.E. José Ramón Icaza, Minister for Canal Affairs of the Republic of Panama, Senator the Hon. Jonathan W. D. Reid, Minister of Innovation, Industry, Science and Technology of Barbados, H.E. Noemí Espinoza Madrid, Secretary General of the Association of Caribbean States, and H.E. Mohammad Alhawi, Undersecretary at the UAE Ministry of Investment. They will be joined by Juan Sabater, Partner and Co-President of Valor Equity Partners, Alonso Aznar, Founder and CEO of Zaria Capital, and René Grullón Finet, Executive President of Grupo Popular.

World Governments Summit Luis Abinader with the participants of the dialogue in 2025 (archive)

Related sessions will explore how culture and local identity can become global exports, how technology can improve connectivity among islands and widen access to markets and services, and what lies ahead for aviation and logistics. They will also examine changes in capital flows and how governments can attract productive investment. "More Than an Island: A Conversation with Leaders of Small Island States" will bring together the Hon. Dr. Natalio Wheatley, Premier of the British Virgin Islands, and the Hon. Philip Davis, Prime Minister of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas, to discuss how small island states can strengthen their role in the global economy.

"New Energy, New Economies: Where Should Governments Invest?" will examine how investment can support emerging industries and strengthen energy security. The session will feature H.E. Félix Ulloa, Vice President of the Republic of El Salvador, and Enrique Riquelme, Founder and Chairman of Cox Energy.

"From Natural Wealth to National Wealth" will explore how governments can turn natural resources into diversified economies, higher-value industries and lasting prosperity across generations. Participants include H.E. Rodrigo Paz Pereira, President of the Plurinational State of Bolivia, and the Hon. Brigadier (Ret'd) Mark Phillips, Prime Minister of the Co-operative Republic of Guyana.

Anticipating change and improving public services

The agenda places particular emphasis on how governments can prepare for rapid change. Sessions will examine ten trends expected to reshape government leadership, service delivery and the ability to create opportunities over the coming decade.

"Before Disaster Strikes: Are Governments Ready?" will examine how foresight, technology and partnerships can help governments anticipate emerging risks, protect essential services and strengthen national preparedness. "The Next National Advantage: Learning Faster" will explore how skills development and lifelong learning can prepare people and institutions for rapidly changing economies.

H.E. Hesham Amiri, Deputy Chief of Government Services at the UAE Prime Minister's Office, will speak in "What Does a Zero-Bureaucracy Government Look Like?" The session will showcase the UAE's Zero Government Bureaucracy model and its experience in streamlining procedures and delivering faster, more flexible and more efficient services.

Other sessions will examine how artificial intelligence can widen economic participation and improve public services, and how effective communication between governments and communities can strengthen trust and public participation.

UN Tourism regional dialogue to address air connectivity and economic integration

UN Tourism will convene a high-level regional dialogue titled "Air Connectivity in the Americas: Key to Competitiveness and Regional Integration". Ministers, airport and aviation leaders, and development partners will share policy experience, successful practices and recommendations for improving air connectivity, supporting regional integration and unlocking the economic potential of tourism. Discussions will address tourism's contribution to growth, investment, jobs and local and regional development, as well as its role in national development agendas. Participants will also discuss charges, taxes, innovative incentives and competitiveness.

The Association of Caribbean States will hold a high-level meeting titled "One Sea, Multiple Destinations: Connecting Destinations, Experiences and Opportunities" to explore ways to strengthen links between destinations and deepen regional cooperation.

Five Emirati-inspired majlises to foster exchange and shape shared priorities

The second day will feature five majlises inspired by Emirati traditions of dialogue. The roundtables will bring together government leaders, experts and institutional representatives to share experience and develop common perspectives on strategic issues and the future of development.

The majlises will cover government innovation, global connectivity and economic competitiveness, talent, skills and the future workforce, national resources and future prosperity, and artificial intelligence and the opportunities it opens.

Participants will examine how lessons from other governments can improve public services and institutional readiness, and how transport, trade and digital connectivity can strengthen competitiveness. The discussions will also cover the skills needed by emerging industries, how strategic resources can support long-term prosperity, and how countries can build AI capabilities and encourage innovation grounded in trust and accountability.

The facilitators include Abeer Tahlak, Director of the Mohammed Bin Rashid Centre for Government Innovation at the UAE Prime Minister's Office, Tim Kingston, Chairman and Head of Investment Banking for Latin America at Goldman Sachs, Steven Bertoni, Assistant Managing Editor at Forbes, Dr. Carlos Díaz-Rosillo, Founding Director of the Adam Smith Center for Economic Freedom, and Jason Marczak, Vice President and Senior Director of the Atlantic Council's Adrienne Arsht Latin America Center.

International discussions on the future of societies and the Global South

The programme includes a Global Insights session on regional cooperation and the future of societies. It will explore how partnerships, innovation and human potential can shape the region's future, with H.E. Félix Ulloa, Vice President of the Republic of El Salvador, and the Hon. Everly Paul Chet Greene, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Immigration of Antigua and Barbuda, alongside leaders and representatives of international institutions and companies.

H.E. Víctor Bisonó, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Dominican Republic, will open the second day. The programme includes "META RD 2036: The Future of Government", featuring H.E. José Ignacio Paliza, Minister of the Presidency of the Dominican Republic, and Celso Juan Marranzini, President of the National Council of Private Enterprise (CONEP) and Coordinator of the META RD 2036 Transversal Committee.

Sessions will also examine the future of aviation, global investment trends, shifts in energy markets and how government partnerships with the private sector can help build more diversified and competitive economies.

H.E. Noura AlKaabi, Minister of State of the UAE, the Hon. Frederick Mitchell, MP, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Commonwealth of The Bahamas, H.E. Víctor Bisonó, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Dominican Republic, and the Hon. Everly Paul Chet Greene, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Immigration of Antigua and Barbuda, will take part in " New Bridges, New Influence: The Future of Next Global South? " The session will examine the outlook, challenges and opportunities for countries of the Global South and their role in shaping international relations and future partnerships.

A partnership advancing regional and international cooperation

The inaugural Dialogue, organised by the World Governments Summit Organization and hosted by the Dominican Republic last year, marked a step forward in regional and international cooperation. It brought together representatives of 22 countries, 29 speakers and 59 leading companies and institutions across 14 sessions and 10 strategic engagements covering the future of government, economic transformation, tourism, innovation and regional cooperation.

At the inaugural edition, the World Governments Summit and the Government of the Dominican Republic signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen cooperation, develop joint initiatives and establish a long-term platform for dialogue. The agreement supports closer partnerships between the UAE and Latin America and the Caribbean, and opens new opportunities for international cooperation and sustainable development.

World.title: South Africa: South Africa Must Close the Gaps in Corruption Referrals
World.content:
analysis

Thousands of referrals fall through the cracks of the country's many anti-corruption agencies. Better cooperation, tracking and follow-up are vital.

Between 2011 and August 2026, South Africa's Special Investigating Unit (SIU) made 5 944 criminal referrals to the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA). But only 570 registered police dockets, 91 court cases and 263 convictions in relation to these referrals were reported by the NPA to Parliament.

This does not mean thousands of referrals disappeared, as several may be consolidated into one docket; and not all provide sufficient evidence for prosecution. Parliament's concern was that the SIU, NPA and Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI, or Hawks) could not provide a consistent, reconciled account of how individual referrals had progressed through the criminal justice system.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

South Africa has numerous institutions with powers to investigate corruption, impose sanctions and pursue other forms of accountability. These include the SIU, NPA, Hawks, Financial Intelligence Centre, Auditor-General, Public Protector and financial regulators. Research from the Institute for Security Studies highlights that many depend on information or findings from other institutions to exercise their powers effectively.

The SIU's investigation into alleged corruption at the National Lotteries Commission (NLC) involving grants intended for community projects shows the difficulty in tracking a matter after it's referred. Between 2022 and 2024, 19 criminal referrals were made to the NPA. In May 2025, the SIU reported no recorded progress on 18 of these referrals. By March 2026, the NPA had consolidated the referrals into 16 matters, with two in court and 14 under investigation.

The NPA identified the Hawks' difficulties appointing forensic accountants as a major cause of delay. The Hawks later submitted dockets to prosecutors, but some were returned with requests for further investigation, as the Hawks explained in parliamentary proceedings.

Not every delay is avoidable. Evidence warranting an SIU referral may fall short of what is needed to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Complex financial investigations take time, and prosecutorial decisions must remain independent.

But the NLC case exposed shortcomings in accounting for matters as they moved between institutions. Their status was revealed only through parliamentary scrutiny, when routine reporting should have done so.

Similar difficulties can arise regarding referrals for disciplinary action. The SIU's investigation into procurement corruption at Tembisa Hospital produced 116 disciplinary referrals concerning 13 officials. By September 2025, 108 had been delivered to the Gauteng Department of Health. As of October 2026, the SIU had not received feedback on the progress of its recommendations.

While this does not establish that the department failed to act, it shows how referring institutions can remain unaware of next steps.

The Tembisa investigation also raises questions about how findings from one investigation inform subsequent action. The SIU identified repeated purchases just below competitive tender thresholds. Earlier SIU investigations in the Gauteng Health Department had identified procurement governance weaknesses, some of which persisted in the Tembisa case. This shows the importance of sharing lessons across facilities and checking whether corrective measures have been implemented.

Existing legislation offers examples of how institutions can be required to account for their handling of referrals. Under the Public Audit Act and Material Irregularity Regulations, public bodies receiving referrals from the Auditor-General to investigate suspected irregularities must promptly acknowledge receipt, report on progress at intervals specified by the Auditor-General, explain delays and communicate outcomes.

The Independent Police Investigative Directorate Act goes further. Police commissioners must initiate disciplinary proceedings within 30 days of receiving recommendations from the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID) and communicate outcomes. Failure to comply is a criminal offence.

Although their effectiveness is uncertain, these arrangements establish obligations to report on referrals without prescribing the final investigative or disciplinary outcome.

Similar reporting duties should be extended to other significant corruption referrals. Receiving institutions should be required to acknowledge referrals, explain decisions and report on progress, without compromising investigative or prosecutorial discretion.

Agreements alone have not resolved the problem. The SIU and NPA signed a memorandum of understanding in 2017, followed by another involving the Hawks and police in 2022. Yet the institutions still struggle to reconcile their figures.

Efforts to improve referral tracking are underway. The Presidency's SIU Referrals Coordination and Monitoring Mechanism monitors the implementation of SIU recommendations. Within this initiative, the Presidency, SIU and NPA worked with the State Information Technology Agency to develop a proof of concept for a Case Monitoring Mechanism to track SIU referrals to the NPA. In time, the system could also track disciplinary, administrative and regulatory recommendations.

While important, agreements and software systems are not sufficient to complete this work. Institutional leaders must ensure that staff record receipt, take responsibility for the next step, share relevant information, update case records and respond when deadlines are missed. Parliament should monitor whether the arrangements are implemented and whether overdue referrals receive attention.

The United Kingdom's counter-fraud standards offer useful guidance, recommending auditable records of referrals received, assessment decisions, reasons, milestones and outcomes. Such records would help institutions follow matters to their conclusion, even when several referrals are consolidated into one investigation or a case moves between institutions.

Close 

These improvements should also change how institutional performance is measured. Reporting should go beyond the number of investigations completed or referrals made to show how many referrals were acknowledged, assessed and concluded, how long this took and why matters remained outstanding.

South Africa's anti-corruption institutions have different mandates, and their independence must be respected. But this should not prevent them from accounting for how they handle matters referred by other bodies. Ultimately, accountability should not end where one institution's mandate stops.

Georgia Dorrington, Research Consultant, Justice and Violence Prevention, ISS

Martin Schönteich, ISS Consultant and former South African prosecutor

World.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia-Eritrea Border Clashes Raise Fears of Regional War
World.content:
As Ethiopian troops push Tigrayan forces toward the Eritrean border, fears of a new regional war are growing. With tensions rising between Ethiopia, Eritrea and Sudan, the Horn of Africa faces uncertain times ahead.

After a few weeks of relative stability, fresh clashes in the contested Ethiopia-Eritrea border areahave raised fears of a full-fledged war. Meanwhile, diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and Sudanhave hit new lows.

Fighters allied with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) launched their offensive on September 23. It was aimed at overthrowing the Ethiopian government as part of a larger rebel coalition. But the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF), backed by pro-government militia, have steadily pushed the TPLF out of Tigray, a region in northern Ethiopia.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

According to the conflict tracker of the monitoring organization ACLED, the ENDF have pushed further into Tigray, effectively driving the Tigrayan Defense Forces (TDF) towards the border with Eritrea. Skirmishes have been reported from several locations, while the ENDF have fired heavy artillery towards dwellings close to the Eritrean border town of Badme.

While no census data is publicly available, Badme appears to be a small rural town on satellite images. However, the locality is historically significant for both sides because it was the ground zero of the Eritrean-Ethiopian War from 1998 to 2000, sometimes dubbed the Badme War.

The war ended with theAlgiers Agreement, in which both countries agreed to honor the rulings of a newly formed Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission. The commission awarded Badme to Eritrea, a decision that Ethiopia challenged at times. Abdurahman Sayed, director of the London-based Horn of Africa Center for Regional Integration, told DW that Ethiopia might see an advantage in reclaiming Badme to resolve its current internal struggles.

"It seems now if the Eritreans withdrew and the Ethiopians came back, it could be to calm down the Tigrayans, especially those who are now supporting the party in power in Ethiopia", Sayed said.

He suggested that people like Getachew Reda, a former spokesman for the TPLF and current advisor to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, might be able to win the Tigrayan people over to side with the federal government through territorial gains for the Tigray region.

The ever-looming threat of a full-fledged war with Eritrea

"The coming of the forces to the Eritrean-Ethiopian border clearly indicates that the conflict can be triggered any time", Abdurahman Sayed said.

Eritrean and Ethiopian government troops allied against the Tigrayan forcesduring the 2020-22 Tigray conflict. Since then, Eritrea's allegiances have shifted towards the TPLF and away from Abiy Ahmed's central government. In October, the two neighbors cut diplomatic ties. At one point, Eritrean troops reportedly crossed the border into Tigray.

Magnus Taylor, a regional analyst with the International Crisis Group (ICG), believes that Addis Ababa's prime objective for the moment might rather be securing its northern border and destroying supply lines between Eritrea and Tigrayan forces.

"So what we might actually be seeing is a kind of a function of the attempts by the Ethiopian military to consolidate its control of Tigray, which includes pushing Tigray's borders with Eritrea", Taylor told DW.

However, securing control over Tigray could also involve direct conflict with Eritrea at one point, Taylor said: "If this happens, then it's quite likely that the Ethiopians would attempt to carry out all their objectives in Eritrea at one time."

Since Eritrea seceded from Ethiopia in 1993, Ethiopia has been the world's largest landlocked country by population. Prime Minister Abiy has repeatedly described the country's lack of sea access as an existential threat. While stating a preference for peaceful means to gain access, he said this could also mean capturing Eritrea's easternmost port, Assab, by force.

Ethiopia-Sudan relations at crossroads

At the same time, the diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and its northwestern neighbor, Sudan, have deteriorated even further.

Sudan and Egypt, both downstream the river Nile, have been on edge for years because of Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam (GERD). The massive GERD, built on the Blue Nile just kilometers from Ethiopia's border with Sudan, gives Addis Ababa significant leverage over the timing and regulation of water flows downstream, raising concerns in Sudan and Egypt over water security and dam operations. The Ethiopian government has rejected claims that the dam could be used as a means to pressure Sudan and Egypt.

Close 

Since 2023, Sudan has been embroiled in a civil war between two rival military forces: the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) , led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti . In mid-November, both sides accused the other of direct participation in each other's internal conflicts.

Two countries with severe internal conflicts and mirroring alliances: Could the situation deteriorate further into potential direct fights between the two armies? ICG's Magnus Taylor believes there is a risk, but at least not for now.

"The most likely scenario is we just get a continuation of this kind of proxy style of involvement with each other's opposition groups rather than formal direct involvement on the ground in the conflict," Taylor said.

Sayed also believes that, at the moment, there is no need for direct confrontation.

"The RSF can do the job that Ethiopia and any other country backing them wants them to do," Sayed said. "But if there is a need and the RSF are failing, the Ethiopian army could be pushed to get involved."

Edited by: Chrispin Mwakideu

World.title: Mozambique: Media Outlets Should Have Adopted Legal Measures to Defend Their Rights - Mondlane
World.content:
Maputo — Venâncio Mondlane, former presidential candidate and leader of the National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (Anamola), believes that media outlets should have adopted legal measures to defend their rights after the country's Supreme Court has limited the number of media companies authorized to cover his trial, which started this Tuesday.

"It was the national press's obligation to take concerted action to assert its own rights. The responsibility for the lack of a legal challenge should not be attributed to the court, but to the journalists themselves", Mondlane said, minutes after arriving at Supreme Court premises in Maputo.

Upon his arrival, Mondlane had a vehicle surrounded by journalists from both domestic and international media outlets, all eager to capture his statements, marking the first day of his trial.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Mondlane added that media outlets should not limit themselves to producing reports and opinion pieces, but should instead "adopt measures with legal standing to defend their rights."

The Supreme Court spokesperson, Pedro Nhatitima, had announced the availability of only 45 special seats for media companies, adding that "other national media outlets will have to compete for four rotating spots by registering via an electronic platform." However, Nhatitima did not reveal the criteria for the appointment of companies in question, most of which are state-owned.

Mozambique's Network of Human Rights Defenders (RMDDH) also condemned restrictions on press coverage of Mondlane's trial and advocated "for equal access for media outlets."

"The Supreme Court should review its criteria regarding the allocation of seats, ensuring equal access for the coverage of the trial. It should also provide transparent criteria for the accreditation and selection of journalists, and consider moving the trial to a larger venue to accommodate media coverage. Furthermore, the Court should adopt additional measures to guarantee public access to information about the progress of the trial. Security measures must respect the principles of legality and proportionality", reads the RMDDH statement.

Mondlane is accused of five criminal charges related to post-election mass demonstrations. The mass demonstration he called to protest against the alleged fraudulent results of the general elections held in October 2024 started peacefully but then degenerated into rioting.

He is accused of having committed the following crimes: public apology for a crime; incitement to collective disobedience; public instigation to crime; instigation and incitement to terrorism.

World.title: Recent service outages not state-sponsored attacks, DNI Jay Clayton testifies
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Recent service outages across U. S. systems stem from routine technical and maintenance issues – not a coordinated foreign cyberattack, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton testified Wednesday, even as he warned lawmakers that "superintelligence" is rapidly escalating the speed and sophistication of future cyber threats.

"Based on what we know today, after a great deal of digital diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes, " Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee's "Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years After 9/11" hearing. "They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack."

Clayton acknowledged public concern over the timing of the recent outages, telling the panel that the American people are right to ask questions, but intelligence reviews point away from foreign interference.

THE OUTAGES AMERICA HAS SUFFERED WEREN'T AN ATTACK, BUT THE NEXT FAILURE COULD BE

"We have no indication that these events are related," Clayton said in response to persistent questioning from Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y. "But let me answer something that the American people should know, which is the speed of compute and the level of capability of applications that use that compute is increasing substantially, which means legacy systems that were old six months ago or a year are a lot older."

The intelligence community remains on alert and continues to monitor for any malicious cyber activity targeting U.S. networks or law enforcement partners, Clayton said in his opening statement.

"After doing a great deal of due diligence inside the government with the private sector, with people in the private sector whose job is cybersecurity, we have no indication that these incidents are related, that they're coordinated," Clayton reiterated in the question and answer session of the hearing. "We also have no indication that they're a result of a state-sponsored malign actor."

TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS

Beyond the immediate outages, the intelligence chief warned lawmakers that rapid advancements in artificial intelligence – also referred to as "superintelligence" – are fundamentally altering the digital battlefield and raising the stakes for homeland defense.

"Let me note that superintelligence is reshaping the cybersecurity landscape, " Clayton said. "It is sharply increasing speed, scale, and sophistication of offensive and defensive cyber operations. And it's not just cyber. This goes to national security. It goes to the battlefield and it goes to commerce. Superintelligence is changing the way we do business, the way we fight wars and the way we combat terrorism every day."

GOVERNMENT INVESTIGATORS FIND AI PLATFORMS PRODUCE TERROR PLOT PLANS IN UNDERCOVER OP

During his opening remarks, Clayton outlined a broader heightened threat environment 25 years after the Sept. 11 attacks. While declining to discuss classified intelligence in an open setting, he noted that full briefings have been provided to the Gang of Eight and congressional intelligence committees.

Among the primary threats highlighted in his testimony:

Iranian plotting: Clayton said threats from Iran – both inside the United States and targeting Americans abroad – have "substantially increased," underscoring a commitment to detecting and deterring lethal plots.

Terrorism: While post-9/11 counterterrorism efforts have degraded the capabilities of major groups, Clayton warned of persistent threats from individuals inspired by ISIS and al-Qaeda, as well as networks exploited by adversarial nations.

Surveillance authorities: Clayton urged Congress not to let Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) expire, calling it the "single most indispensable tool" for early warnings on foreign threats to the homeland and U. S. troops.

"No other program can replicate the speed and effectiveness of FISA 702," Clayton said. "Letting it expire would simply be a mistake."

World.title: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

ABC News quietly suspended staffers involved in the botched story last month suggesting impropriety in the Trump sons' business dealings, Fox News Digital has confirmed.

The Disney-owned network stirred controversy with its report headlined, "Trump sons' investments have won billions in Pentagon contracts since his election," alleging that Anduril, the company investing in a new Baltimore shipyard, had ties to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump through 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm. The report claimed the firm had a "major stake" in Anduril, which was ultimately false.

ABC News raised eyebrows when it deleted the report without explanation after the story was called out on social media, then quietly republished a revised version of the report with an editor's note acknowledging the error.

GOP SENATOR CALLS FOR FCC PROBE OF ABC NEWS OVER TRUMP SONS-ANDURIL 'POLITICAL HIT JOB'

The ordeal resulted in an internal probe to determine what went wrong. While two staffers behind the botched story were reprimanded and rumors they will be terminated swirl, an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "No one's employment status has changed."

ABC News declined further comment.

The Wall Street Journal's Joe Flint first reported that the two staffers were on "paid leave."

ABC News' original story wrote, "1789 Capital — a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders — claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company."

"Since that investment, Anduril has been awarded 135 other contracts with the U.S. government and to date has received around $1.8 billion from those agreements, according to active defense contracts posted to SAM.gov, the official system for government contracting," the story continued. "The company is one of the largest manufacturers to receive an investment from Donald Trump Jr. and his brother Eric Trump, but they are not the only one."

ABC NEWS QUIETLY REPUBLISHES GUTTED VERSION OF STORY ON TRUMP SONS IT HAD DELETED WITHOUT EXPLANATION

Alexa Henning, a spokesperson for 1789 Capital and a former chief of staff to the director of national intelligence, took to social media, insisting the company does not have a "major stake" in Anduril and blasting the "biased hit piece."

"Here's a small lesson, that I also explained to ABC, the ‘reporter’ who is a complete idiot conflated raising funds with investment by 1789. Those are two separate actions," Henning reacted at the time.

"Meaning the ‘investments’ mentioned were actually the total number raised for a funding round, that MANY companies contribute to," Henning continued. "Another thing that the reporter buried the lead on was that many of these companies have gotten government contracts during Biden AND Trump, which completely negates the assertion by ABC that Don Jr and Eric Trump are doing anything wrong."

VENTURE CAPITAL FIRM TIED TO DONALD TRUMP JR WEIGHS LEGAL ACTION AGAINST ABC NEWS OVER BOTCHED REPORT

ABC News then sparked confusion among critics when it deleted the entire story, only to republish an overhauled version of the story days later with the new headline reading, "New shipyard announced amid earlier Democratic concerns about potential conflicts of interest" while stressing to readers that Trump Jr. "is not involved in investment decisions."

"CORRECTION: A version of this story published on Oct. 7 contained errors in the description of certain company investments, government contracts and event chronologies," the editor's note read at the top of the article. "After subsequent reporting, this version contains corrected information and additional context regarding some of those investments, contracts and events."

Henning has said that nobody from ABC News asked 1789 for comment prior to the initial story being published and that an ABC News journalist "vigorously defended" the report before it was suddenly deleted. She also previously said the company was considering legal action against the Disney-owned news organization.

"This should be a cautionary tale for any other reporters who continue to traffic in this false narrative," Henning told Fox News Digital on Wednesday when asked if a lawsuit is still being considered.
