"GTA VI" is a game of superlatives that's been crashing through records. The hype around it is unparalleled. No game in history has clocked so many pre-orders. It's thought that around 10 million people have already purchased it. There's no denying it: "GTA VI" is a global cultural phenomenon.

A few days before its release on November 19, fans can already start downloading the game. The file is so large that downloading it can take several days, depending on the internet connection. Providers have already registered a significant spike in data traffic.

As soon as the game is unlocked, players can start speeding through the fictional US metropolis of Vice City in a stylish sports car with criminal couple Jason and Lucia.

Miami gets cast as Vice City

To mark the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," its real-life inspiration — Miami — is getting a full-scale "Vice City" makeover. This promotional push includes the Miami Heat basketball team stepping onto the hardwood in custom "Vice City" jerseys for a home game, a local festival featuring artists from the game's official soundtrack, and roadside "Vice City" signage installed across the area.

Vice City is a fictionalized representation of the US metropolis of Miami Image: Rockstar Games

Expectations for "GTA VI" are sky-high. Nearly 5,000 people have been working on the game for more than 10 years. Development costs are estimated at around $1 billion (€900 million).

"Based on those figures alone — as well as the series' extremely successful and popular track record — this can certainly be described as a truly exceptional release," says Rudolf Thomas Inderst, cultural studies scholar and professor of Game Design and Game Studies at Germany's Neu-Ulm University of Applied Sciences.

When such an effort is put into a product, it's only natural for people to expect great things, he adds. Inderst is expecting "GTA VI" to showcase the absolute best of what modern gaming can do across gameplay, storytelling, visuals and tech.

Social satire and gameplay freedom

This video game series has been around for almost three decades, setting new standards through its different versions. A biting satire on US society and the American dream, "GTA" parodies politics, culture and the media.

The game is also renowned for its gameplay freedom and spectacularly staged chaos in a crazy world where players can do whatever they please. Shoot down helicopters with a bazooka, go to the hairdresser's, take a stroll on the beach, go to a nightclub, take part in car races and much more.

Pure escapism: In Vice City, there's shooting and dancing Image: Rockstar Games/dpa Picture Alliance

What makes it a standout among video games is how its NPCs — non-player characters, those not being controlled by a human player — are brought to life. They respond based on a player's interactions with them, displaying individualized behaviors and traits ranging from fear to hostility. "GTA VI" has an estimated 600,000 animations for the civilians in the fictional state of Leonida.

'Grand Theft Auto,' a long-running hit

"GTA VI" is essentially a huge adult playground, striking a chord across several generations. Millennials grew up with "Grand Theft Auto III," "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City," "Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas," and "Grand Theft Auto IV," while Gen Z grew up with "Grand Theft Auto V." Generation Alpha might still be too young for the latest edition, but will likely find ways to play it anyway.

In 'GTA VI,' Lucia and Jason play a gangster couple; the players' actions determine how close they become Image: Rockstar Games

Social media has certainly played a part in the series' ongoing success, particularly "GTA V" and its multiplayer spin-off, "GTA Online." Numerous content creators stream gameplay sessions on Twitch or YouTube, and particularly funny or crazy gameplay moments end up on TikTok.

At the same time, a dedicated role-play community has grown around the game. Players gather inside the world of "GTA" to act out specific characters, such as taxi drivers, judges or small-time criminals. They invent realistic backstories for their personas, and many even use accents to stay in character.

Perfectionism has its downsides

The hype surrounding "GTA VI" is not only good news for the game itself but could also boost the entire games industry by drawing more people back to their consoles. This is because the boom triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic was followed by studio closures and redundancies. Worldwide, it's estimated that 50,000 people in the games industry have lost their jobs since 2022.

But while publisher Rockstar Games is well-known for the meticulous polish of its titles and attention to detail, the perfectionism so prized by fans also has its drawbacks, especially for those working on the game. Rockstar, like many other game developers, has frequently faced major criticism regarding its labor practices.

'GTA' characters can relax at Leonida Keys, but game developers face high-pressure workloads in the lead-up to game releases Image: Rockstar Games

Former developers report extremely long working hours and a heavy workload that resulted in health issues. Trade unions accuse company managers of employee surveillance, resulting in a culture of workplace stress and low morale.

Coinciding with the launch of Rockstar's largest game to date, the developers behind it are pushing for trade union recognition. That move would give them a collective voice to address working hours, pay, pensions and parental leave. If successful, their campaign could set a major precedent for the wider video game industry, which continues to face challenges around fair labor practices.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: US House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker
World.content:
Jeffries is set to be the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives when Democrats take control of the chamber next year. He will be second in line to the presidency.

Democrats in the US House of Representatives on Wednesday nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker.

What do we know so far about Jeffries and the speakership?

Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, would be the first Black person to fill the role. He received 251 out of 265 ballots cast in a closed-door, secret vote.

"Thank you House Democrats. Together, we will deliver bold change," Jeffries posted on X after the vote. "And make a big difference for the American people!"

Some progressive Democrats voted against Jeffries' speakership, with the congressman considered by some to be in the moderate wing of the party.

The entire House will do a roll call vote on January 3, 2027, to elect a speaker when the new Congress convenes. As Democrats won control of the House of Representatives in the midterm elections, claiming at least 257 of 435 seats in the lower chamber of US Congress, the 56-year-old Jeffries is all but certain to get the position.

In a rebuke of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party, Democrats also won 56 seats and control of the Senate, the upper house of US Congress.

Jeffries will steer Democratic priorities in the House, such as possible legislation and investigations of the Trump administration. He will also be second in line to the presidency after Vice President JD Vance.

Progress or not? Democrats, Republicans pick new leaders in Congress To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Who are the other leaders in the next Congress?

Under Jeffries, Massachusetts Representative Katherine Clark will serve as female majority leader, and Pete Aguilar of California will serve as majority whip. Clark will be the first woman to serve in that position, with Aguilar the first Latino to fill his elected role in the House.

For the Republican House delegation in the new Congress, Jim Jordan, a representative of Ohio, will be the next House minority leader. Jordan is a staunch Trump supporter.

In the Senate, Chuck Schumer of New York is the frontrunner to lead Democrats in the upper chamber, with Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen also in the running.

Republican South Dakota Senator John Thune, who currently serves as Senate majority leader, is expected to be minority leader next year.

World.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
World.content:
Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.

"It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions."

Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.

Germans protest Rheinmetall's plans for Berlin arms factory To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”

Long held opposition

Many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

At the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, said Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination."

The 50+1 rule: Bayern Munich and Cologne case studies To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio

It has always been clear, said Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

"In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he said of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”

In the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer said he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case."

That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.

"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a new sponsorship, investment deals," he said.

Dortmund not the first to climbdown on sponsors

Indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

Fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

Both Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have rethought sponsorship deals of late Image: Alexandra Beier/AFP

Elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took issue with the factory farming practices of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

Union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a new shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate company, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.

German football's battle between commerce and 50+1

"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.

"We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy."

Striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.

"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he said.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal."

Additional reporting by: Emmie Eernisse

World.title: North Korea expanded uranium enrichment plant, says IAEA head
World.content:
IAEA chief Rafael Grossi has said the ongoing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment program remains "a cause for serious concern."

United Nations (UN) nuclear watchdog chief Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday North Korea has built an extension on its original uranium-enrichment plant at the Yongbyon nuclear complex.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has been unable to access North Korea since Pyongyang expelled its inspectors in 2009. It now relies primarily on satellite imagery to monitor the country's nuclear activity.

Grossi addressed the ongoing operation of enrichment facilities at Yongbyon and Kangson during a quarterly meeting of the IAEA's Board of Governors.

Kangson lies just southwest of Pyongyang, while the much larger Yongbyon facility is located farther north of the capital.

"Since ​mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original ​Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by ​late October 2026," Grossi said, with no further details.

He said the ongoing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment program remains "a cause for serious concern."

Enriched uranium is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and the nuclear reactors that run naval ships and submarines. It can also be used in nuclear weapons.

US President Donald Trump floated the possibility of a meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as he went to China to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Meanwhile, North Korean state media — which typically operates behind the global news cycle — has only released images of Kim visiting a ski resort and Mount Paektu, making no mention of possible Shenzhen travel plans.

Building a nuclear force

Kim has said he aims to arm the nation with an expansive nuclear force to counter the US and South Korea.

In March, soon after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, Kim accused Washington of "global terrorism and aggression."

The Iran war reinforced North Korea's long-standing view that it needs a nuclear arsenal to be able to defend itself against what it sees as its two largest enemies, South Korea and the US.

North Korean state media published pictures in June showing Kim inspecting a nuclear material production facility Image: KCNA/KNS/dpa/picture alliance

North Korea has been subject to various international sanctions over its nuclear weapons development and use of ballistic missile technology. But Pyongyang has repeatedly flouted the restrictions.

In September 2024, North Korea revealed its first covert uranium-enrichment plant. Kim delivered a speech then, including a call for "exponentially" expanding the country's nuclear arsenal.

In April, Grossi told reporters that his agency had confirmed "a rapid increase” in activities at nuclear facilities in North Korea.

In September, the IAEA passed resolutions at its annual conference regarding concerns about the North Korean nuclear program.

Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of Kim Jong Un, said in response that the country's nuclear-armed status was "absolute."

She called those expecting denuclearisation "idiots."

World.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: In an era of waning support, Europe remains committed to Ukraine
World.content:
The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

Once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

Extensive security measures have already been announced for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

The "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.

DW interview with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Led by Germany, France, and the United Kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within Ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London. Now they are gathering in Berlin.

But what can the coalition realistically achieve? Stefan Meister of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) is not overly optimistic. In an interview with DW, he said: "The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal. There is no plan outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises."

Merz: 'Germany has a seat at the table'

Nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine, and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.

Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.

Western allies boost Ukraine's defenses but clash over deep strikes To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

Unsurprisingly, this has sparked a debate among EU heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent Europe in such talks. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)? After the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, he said: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear."

Europe has yet to speak with one voice

But what exactly did that mean? That Germany alone would speak for all of Europe? Hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President António Costa, would also take part.

Stefan Meister of the DGAP believes the debate says a great deal about the pressures Europe itself is under: "Europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations. Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that."

German Deputy Government Spokesperson Sebastian Hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on Monday over a possible role for Friedrich Merz as chief negotiator. At the federal government's regular press briefing, he said: "This is not about discussing individuals. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place."

Can Germany make Europe pay more for Ukraine? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

German government spokesperson: Europe now needs stamina

US negotiator Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, struck a rather different tone last week. Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he said: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations."

Government spokesperson Hille responded on Monday: "Europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question." Hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance, and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

Declining support for Ukraine in German polls

European supporters of Ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the issue is shifting, including in Germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

According to the latest ARD DeutschlandTrend survey on the issue, conducted in September 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to Ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

A further study conducted for public broadcaster WDR in November 2026 found that support for Ukraine has become a more polarizing issue in Germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
World.content:
The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most important temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.

Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.

The Parthenon had a lasting influence on Western ideas of humanity and art. The sculptures adorning its pediments, created under the direction of the legendary sculptor Phidias, are considered unparalleled examples of proportion and grace. They have influenced artists from ancient Rome through Neoclassicism to the modern era.

'Very confident we've solved the mystery'

The east pediment above the temple entrance depicted the birth of the goddess Athena from the head of her father Zeus, surrounded by the Olympian gods. A total of 39 figures adorned the roughly 29-meter-long work of art. At its center stood a colossal Zeus figure, measuring 3.8 meters in height.

For centuries, scholars have puzzled over exactly what the arrangement looked like, as the pediment was destroyed during the Christianization of Greece.

But now there has been a breakthrough.

The results of the research are on show at the Frankfurt exhibition 'Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle' Image: Norbert Miguletz/Liebieghaus Skulpturensammlung

After decades of painstaking detective work and with the help of modern technology, archaeologist Vinzenz Brinkmann and his team have managed to piece together all the surviving fragments of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Brinkmann heads the Antiquities and Asia department at Frankfurt's Liebieghaus sculpture collection. "We're very, very confident that we've solved the mystery," he told DW.

The results are now on display in an exhibition at the Liebieghaus titled "Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle ."

Only around 20% of the original marble sculpture's volume is known to have survived. The fragments are scattered across various European museums, with most located in Athens. The British Museum also holds numerous pieces.

Brinkmann and his wife, Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, have spent more than 40 years working on this ancient puzzle, with so many of its pieces missing.

And they were far from the first to attempt it: "Already in the 19th century, many scholars studied the subject and developed well-founded theories based on their deep knowledge of ancient sources," Brinkmann explains.

In 1910, a study documenting the many fragments held by the British Museum was published. The research team was able to build on that earlier work, but progress remained slow for years.

Then, in 2014, a visit to the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg provided Brinkmann with a crucial clue. There, he encountered a Roman sarcophagus featuring a relief of Athena's birth. "That's when it suddenly clicked: They're all there!"

Nine such sarcophagi are known to exist, almost all of them in Rome. Each depicts a different section of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Brinkmann emphasizes that other scholars had already noticed this connection in the 19th century. "But we really seized on the idea and never let go."

The researchers are convinced that the Dioscuri — the sons of the king of the gods, Zeus — located in Rome’s Piazza del Quirinale are also copies of the group of figures from the eastern pediment Image: Zoonar/picture alliance

A handy tool: the iPhone

The researchers also benefited from 21st-century technology: 3D scanners and printers. Brinkmann and his team visited numerous destinations to examine around 60 original fragments at different locations — traveling light. An iPhone was all they needed to scan the pieces.

Digitally fitting the fragments together led to another important discovery. "We know these figures we're putting together!" Brinkmann recalls thinking at the time.

The Romans had repeatedly made individual copies of all the sculptures from the pediment. "These copies matched the fragments perfectly. Suddenly, we found ourselves surrounded by old acquaintances we had never suspected had come from the pediment." This finally enabled the researchers to reconstruct all the figures and their original arrangement.

Using a 3D printer, the team created a 4-meter-long model at a scale of 1:7.7. For the exhibition, they also produced life-size 3D prints of the most important fragments and mounted them on panels depicting the complete figures at their original size. An animation brings the reconstructed composition to life, digitally assembling the fragments to reveal how the east pediment once looked.

Alongside works from the Liebieghaus collection, the exhibition features loans from other institutions, including the Vatican Museums and the Louvre. Objects from the Acropolis Museum in Athens had originally been expected as well. But Greece withdrew its participation after learning that the British Museum was also planning to lend fragments to the Frankfurt exhibition. The Liebieghaus ultimately decided to forgo the British-owned fragments, too.

The dispute between Greece and Britain over the Parthenon sculptures

There is a reason for this controversy. Britain holds a substantial portion of the Parthenon frieze as well as fragments from both pediments.

Greek authorities have been campaigning for their return for decades.

The landmark of Athens: the Acropolis with the Parthenon Image: Fokke Baarssen/Zoonar/picture alliance

In Britain, the 56 sections of the frieze are known as the "Elgin Marbles," named after Lord Elgin, the British ambassador to the Ottoman Empire in Constantinople.

In the early 19th century, Elgin had sculptures removed from the exterior of the Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens. They were taken to Britain with the consent of the Ottoman Empire, which ruled Greece at the time.

Britain maintains that the sculptures were legally acquired.

Greece, however, considers them stolen.

For years, the dispute remained deadlocked. Since the Labour Party came to power in Britain, there has been some movement toward resolving it. But apparently not enough to persuade Greece to lend artworks to an exhibition in which the British Museum might also participate.

The exhibition "Athena, the Stage is Yours. The Parthenon Puzzle" runs through July 25, 2027, at the Liebieghaus in Frankfurt.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: India: Online censorship grows after 'Cockroach' protests
World.content:
Since anti-government Cockroach protests erupted, journalists and creators say their content is increasingly being restricted on social media in India.

A video showing a young girl crying as she spoke about alleged police brutality during the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in July. A video examining the Hindu nationalist Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's (RSS) contribution to the rise of India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). A satirical cartoon criticizing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

These are among the examples of content that have recently been restricted on social media in India.

A pattern of restrictions

Content creator CitySavitri describes herself as a "nobody" in the world of social media. She had started making videos just two months ago and had around 600 followers on Instagram.

Yet a video looking at the RSS's role in the BJP's 2014 election victory was restricted in India within an hour of being posted. It was the first of three videos she posted that faced restrictions.

The experience made her feel that "anti-government commentary" was being monitored and curtailed.

"It is very plain and simple to understand," the content creator told DW.

Independent journalist Sadhika Tiwari was covering the CJP protest in New Delhi on July 20, when police used batons and tear gas against demonstrators.

Tiwari's video of a frightened young girl crying and speaking about police brutality garnered around 10 million views within hours, she said, before it was restricted in India.

Political cartoonist Satish Acharya has also faced repeated restrictions, with Instagram blocking his profile twice recently.

'Suppressing independent journalism'

In May 2025, during the conflict between India and Pakistan, independent digital news outlet Maktoob Media's X account was withheld in India while it was reporting on the escalating crisis, its founder and editor Aslah Kayyalakkath told DW.

"We received no official notice or email from either the government or X. It was our readers who first alerted us to the blocking," he said.

Maktoob Media said it contacted Indian officials and X but received no response. Access to the account was restored a few days later, again without an explanation.

Kayyalakkath said Maktoob's content from the July protest also faced restrictions. "Suppressing independent journalism undermines transparency, accountability and democratic values," he said.

Several of the content creators and journalists interviewed by DW said they received no prior notification or explanation for the restrictions.

Some users were not sure if their content had been blocked at the government's request or proactively by the social media platforms.

When asked for comment, Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, pointed DW to a website statement noting users can appeal content and account restrictions.

How does the system work?

At the heart of the debate are India's IT Rules, 2021, amended in February 2026. Section 79 of India's IT Act protects social media platforms and other intermediaries from liability for content posted by third parties, provided they meet certain legal conditions.

One such requirement, introduced through the February 2026 amendments, is to remove or disable access to specified unlawful content within three hours of receiving a valid court order or a reasoned government notice. The previous deadline was 36 hours.

Failure to comply can result in intermediaries losing their liability protection.

Censorship in India: Muzzled by the government To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The government's Sahyog portal, which coordinates takedown requests between law enforcement, platforms and telecom providers, has faced criticism over the pace at which notices are issued.

Meta said it uses automated tools and technologies to detect and review content that may violate its community standards. It also automatically restricts access to certain types of content in India to comply with legal requirements under the IT rules.

Pranesh Prakash, a technology law and policy adviser, said the amended rules allow authorized police officials to notify intermediaries about content they consider unlawful without necessarily filing a formal complaint or initiating other legal proceedings.

"This has led to the worst period of social media censorship that India has ever seen, with digital news media accounts being blocked, cartoonists' accounts being blocked, and even mere discussions of an opposition leader's memoirs being blocked," he said. "Clearly, none of these disclosed any 'unlawful acts.'"

Prakash also raised concerns about the lack of public information on government requests to remove content, saying this made it difficult to assess the scale of restrictions.

A flaw in the system

The Software Freedom Law Center, India (SFLC.in), a digital rights organization, said the growing reliance on automated takedowns raised serious concerns about transparency, accountability and due process.

"There is little transparency about the processes through which content is identified, flagged and restricted, or whether there is any meaningful human oversight before a takedown is implemented," SFLC.in told DW.

The organization also tested X's verification process by submitting a takedown request against one of its own posts using a fake email address. X registered the request, raising questions about how it verified the identity and authority of those submitting requests.

After SFLC.in alerted the company, X introduced email verification codes for people submitting takedown requests.

"A channel that lets anyone pose as a law enforcement official can be misused to silence lawful speech," SFLC.in said.

X did not respond to DW's request for a comment.

Government says no censorship

The Indian government denies that it is censoring online content.

While the ministry did not respond to DW's latest request for a comment, in an email response to DW in August, Vinod Kumar, chief of media and communications at the Information Technology Ministry, said Instagram posts by students and protesters following the July CJP protests "are not being taken down as alleged."

"Media enjoys freedom in India. The Government does not censor online content," Kumar said, adding that the government only acts against "objectionable content."

Under the Indian IT rules, "unlawful content" generally refers to material which could threaten India's sovereignty and integrity, disturb public order, incite violence, or constitute defamation.

However, social media influencers such as university professor Madri Kakoti, alias Dr. Medusa, continue to report restrictions. Kakoti's Instagram account was restricted in India on November 16 without notice, she said, along with that of satirist Shamita Yadav.

Screenshot of the Instagram account 'the.ranting.gola' showing that the account is not available in India Image: Screenshot Instagram/the.ranting.gola

The price of free speech

Rights groups including Human Rights Watch have warned that expanding content restrictions could chill free expression and encourage self-censorship among journalists, creators and ordinary users.

Acharya, however, said he would continue his work.

"The Indian Constitution gives me the right to draw political cartoons," he said. "It's totally democratic to question and criticize the government in India."

For Tiwari, the issue goes beyond the reach of a single video. It is also about preserving a record of what happened, after the Delhi Police denied allegations of using excessive force during the July 20 protest in front of the Supreme Court.

"We have seen several other videos now, and it's well established why that girl was crying, and that the Delhi Police used force and lied about it," she said.

"Still, I want that video back up because it needs to stay for posterity. I think that's the larger idea: they want to take this stuff down so it fades from memory, allowing them to categorically deny it later when we have little left to show for what happened."

World.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar: What to know
World.content:
The ICJ is set to decide whether Myanmar's military operations in Rakhine State a decade ago were carried out with the intent to destroy the country's Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) will deliver on Thursday its long-awaited judgment in The Gambia's landmark genocide case against Myanmar, seven years after the case was lodged in The Hague.

The Gambia filed the case with the United Nations' top court in November 2019, formally accusing the Southeast Asian nation of breaking its obligations under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.

In documents and hearings, The Gambia has alleged that Myanmar waged a deliberate campaign of arson, rape and murder in Rakhine State from 2016 to 2017, intending to wipe out the area's ethnic Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.

A UN fact-finding mission later concluded that some 10,000 people likely died in the pogroms. Another 700,000 Rohingya fled the country to neighboring Bangladesh, where most of them still live today in the world's largest refugee settlement.

Even before 2016, the predominantly Muslim Rohingya had been subjected to decades of persecution by the Buddhist-majority country's government, with many forced into resettlement camps and most denied citizenship.

A number of cases over Myanmar's treatment of the Rohingya have been filed in courts around the world. The ICJ will be the first to issue a ruling.

"The Rohingya people have been waiting for justice for decades for the atrocities and crimes committed against [us]. There were no venues available in [Myanmar]… International venues were the only hope," said Aung Kyaw Moe, a prominent Rohingya activist whose family was forced to flee the country during the pogroms.

"We've come over many years to a situation where a judgment will be delivered, and the expectation from the Rohingya community is very high," he said.

Rohingya caught in the middle of Myanmar's civil war To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Journey to judgment day

A month after The Gambia lodged its case with the ICJ in 2019, Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, Myanmar's de facto civilian leader at the time, traveled to The Hague to contest the allegations, calling them "incomplete and incorrect."

The move tarnished her international reputation as a human rights icon. Many human rights advocates criticized her for defending the very military that had persecuted her for most of her life.

In 2020, ahead of a final judgment, the ICJ issued emergency "provisional measures" ordering Myanmar to take all steps "within its power" to prevent acts of genocide against the Rohingya, an order rights groups say it has blatantly ignored.

Myanmar's military went on to oust the country's democratically elected government the following year, placing Aung San Suu Kyi under arrest and setting off a bloody civil war that continues to rage.

Myanmar also challenged both the court's jurisdiction over the alleged crimes and The Gambia's right to lodge the case, both of which the ICJ rejected in 2022.

The ICJ then held 14 days of hearings this January for Myanmar and The Gambia to make their arguments before the panel. While Myanmar called one witness, The Gambia called three, as well as an expert.

A question of intent

As The Gambia has accused Myanmar of breaking several articles of the Genocide Convention, Thursday's judgment could be "fairly complicated," said Melanie O'Brien, a professor of international law at the University of Western Australia and past president of the International Association of Genocide Scholars.

The convention outlines that states have a duty to prevent and punish genocide and to establish effective penalties for those found responsible. The ICJ could rule in Myanmar's favor on some of these provisions and against it on others.

"So, there's quite a lot of layers here. They'll be looking at all of those issues, along with, of course, delving into the facts of the case and the individual crimes of genocide and whether or not Myanmar committed those individual crimes with the intent to destroy the Rohingya," O'Brien said.

Bangladesh: Could the UN help the Rohingya return home? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Proving Myanmar's intent behind the alleged atrocities is the key question the ICJ is grappling with.

Myanmar argues that its actions were strictly part of a legitimate counterinsurgency and counterterrorism operation, and that those actions could not at the same time be judged as acts of genocide.

Days before the Myanmar military launched its heaviest operations in Rakhine, in August 2017, the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, an armed group based in the state, staged a coordinated attack on more than 30 police posts, killing several officers.

Either-or, maybe both

The Gambia argues that Myanmar's actions can qualify as both counterinsurgency and genocide at the same time. It also argues that the sexual violence and killing of children that accompanied the operations are proof that genocide was part of the goal.

"It directly undermines Myanmar's argument that this was a legitimate counterterrorism operation," said Michael Becker, an associate professor of international human rights law at Trinity College Dublin and a former associate legal officer at the ICJ.

"Because evidence of those types of atrocities are very hard to square with the idea that this had some other purpose beyond terrorizing the Rohingya population and indeed taking actions to try to destroy them," he said.

O'Brien and Becker said The Gambia's case against Myanmar is a chance for the ICJ to clarify how it weighs such circumstantial or indirect evidence when judging whether genocide has taken place.

Because investigators were denied access to Rakhine State, they had to rely on interviews with victims and witnesses who had fled Myanmar and on reports by the UN and other groups.

"And how the court deals with that, whether the ICJ accepts or rejects The Gambia's view or Myanmar's view of genocidal intent and how you prove it, this will have major repercussions for other cases," said Becker.

Rohingya women in Bangladeshi camps lack toilets To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Justice denied vs. delayed

The ICJ is grappling with some of the same questions in cases between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, Ukraine and Russia, and South Africa and Israel.

"I'm sure that the parties in the other cases will pick up on what the court rules in this case and add it to their own cases," said O'Brien.

"And even though this case will only be binding on The Gambia and Myanmar, the court itself may also refer to its own law in their future cases," she added.

The ICJ's judgment may have some effect on not only other cases but other courts as well.

The International Criminal Court — which, unlike the ICJ, tries individuals and not states — is considering an arrest warrant request for Myanmar coup leader Min Aung Hlaing in a trial on alleged crimes against humanity committed against the Rohingya. Becker and O'Brien say a finding of genocide by the ICJ could bolster the case for granting the warrant.

What a finding of genocide would actually do for the Rohingya is another key question.

Enforcing any reparations or restitution the court may order would rest with the UN Security Council. But with China and Russia, both allies of Min Aung Hlaing's regime, holding veto power on the council, there are serious doubts about whether it would act on any court order on Myanmar.

Aung Kyaw Moe remains hopeful that the Rohingya will one day receive justice.

"Despite these challenges, there are a lot of hopes that we can [move] toward the betterment of the Rohingya people, including compensation, reparations, transitional justice in the domestic setting in the long term," he said.

World.title: Feijóo abre la puerta a una “derogación total” de la ley de la eutanasia
World.content:
El Partido Popular es contrario a la ley de la eutanasia aprobada por el Gobierno de coalición de PSOE y Podemos. El PP votó en contra en el Congreso de los Diputados durante su tramitación, cuyo debate final se celebró en marzo de 2021. Durante las últimas semanas, y ante las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre, Alberto Núñez Feijóo ya había adelantado que modificará la norma si es investido presidente del Gobierno tras las urnas. Finalmente, en una entrevista publicada este miércoles, el candidato popular a la Presidencia abre la puerta a que el cambio legislativo se lleve a cabo con una derogación total del texto.

“¿Nosotros estamos de acuerdo con la ley de la eutanasia? No. ¿Queremos modificar la ley de la eutanasia? Sí. ¿Esa modificación puede ser una derogación total o parcial? Por supuesto”, aclara el líder del PP en una entrevista ofrecida en el podcast El sentido de la birra, difundida este miércoles en YouTube y cuya grabación se produjo el viernes pasado, durante el primer día de campaña. El programa electoral del Partido Popular para el 29-N propone la aprobación de una “ley nacional de cuidados paliativos” para armonizar las normativas autonómicas sobre la materia, y “con el fin de que nadie se vea empujado a la aceleración de la muerte por falta de alternativas ni tenga que afrontarla en soledad”, explica el texto en su apartado 226. Sin embargo, el programa no menciona la vigente ley de eutanasia ni qué pasará con esa norma en caso de que el jefe de los populares llegue a La Moncloa.

En el El sentido de la birra, ante el youtuber Ricardo Moya, Feijóo clarifica que sí está sobre la mesa la posibilidad de que su futuro Gobierno derogue por completo la norma sancionada en 2021, que fue recurrida por el PP de Pablo Casado ante el Tribunal Constitucional en junio de aquel año y avalada por el órgano de garantías en marzo de 2023. “Nosotros, junto con la regulación de la muerte digna, tenemos que garantizar la vida digna y tenemos que garantizar todo un sistema de cuidados paliativos que en este momento en muchos sitios en España no están desplegados y tenemos que asesorar bien a una persona que aparentemente toma la decisión de poner fin a su vida”, añade el líder del Partido Popular, que vuelve a traer a coalición el mediático caso de la joven Noelia Castillo.

El PP también rechaza la ley trans, que Feijóo califica de “disparate” y cuya modificación también se incorpora en su programa electoral. “Revisaremos las normas que hayan generado inseguridad jurídica en nombre de la igualdad, como la Ley Trans, y eliminaremos la libre autodeterminación registral del sexo, para reforzar la seguridad jurídica y proteger a los menores. Garantizaremos que el sexo biológico sea el criterio para las categorías deportivas femeninas. y asegura que hay adolescentes que luego cambian de idea”, indica el apartado 115. Y en ello se reafirma Feijóo: “En el ámbito del deporte y en el ámbito de las federaciones deportivas, esto de que un señor pueda formar parte de una selección femenina...”.

Por otro lado, Feijóo insiste en que la receta del PP para aliviar el problema de la vivienda es construir más inmuebles. “El problema no se soluciona con decretos, se soluciona con ladrillo”, alega el líder del PP, que carga contra las medidas del Gobierno por considerarlas propias de una “legislación ideológica”. “Hay que construir un millón”, reitera, y apunta a que serán “las empresas, las coperativas” las que pongan en marcha los proyectos de edificación. Para favorecer esa construcción, su programa ofrece: ley antiokupación, que los Ayuntamientos otorgen licencias de construcción con máximo de 90 días y tanto rebajas como prorrateo de impuestos para quienes adquieran una casa. También pedirán flexibilidad a los bancos a la hora de otorgar créditos. Sobre la escasez de mano de obra en el sector, Feijóo sostiene que hay que “recuperar” a los albañiles que se marcharon por la caída de la construcción. Y además quiere a inmigrantes con contratos de obra en origen. “Todas las personas que entren con permiso de trabajo tienen que tener un permiso de residencia en nuestro país, aparecerá mano de obra, si viene un albañil peruan tendrá permiso de residencia. Es un círculo virtuoso”.

“Al PP se le ha juzgado judicialmente y políticamente”

Al margen de la entrevista, el líder del PP ha despejado el resto de su agenda de este miércoles y de este jueves para centrarse en la preparación del cara a cara con Pedro Sánchez de mañana. No tiene más actos ni comparecencias. “Feijóo está tranquilo, pero con ganas de poner al presidente del Gobierno frente al espejo de su incompetencia. Y combinará moderación y sentido de Estado con un examen exigente a la gestión de alguien que debería llevar fuera ya muchos años de la Presidencia del Gobierno”, señalan fuentes de su Gabinete en un comunicado. Génova también carga contra el candidato del PSOE por su entrevista en la revista Lecturas. “Pedro Sánchez lleva a la portada de Lecturas y al atril de sus mítines al elemento que más le alejaba de su masa electoral”, sentencian después de haber encargado, hace un año, una encuesta sobre la repercusión en el electorado de los procesos judiciales que rodean al secretario general de los socialistas.

En el podcast de El sentido de la birra, el líder del PP recuerda sus orígenes en Os Peares (Ourense), de niño, y su licenciatura en Derecho. También rememora que se planteó prepararse las oposiciones de judicatura, pero que lo descartó porque quería independizarse en menos tiempo y se decantó por otras a letrado de la Xunta. Se afilió al PP ya en el 2000. Feijóo recuerda también que votó al PSOE de Felipe González en las elecciones generales tras el golpe de Estado del 23-F. “Felipe era el cambio, la consolidación de la democracia, si gobernaba Felipe, si gobernaba el PSOE, el golpe de Estado no se iba a volver a producir”, cuenta el líder del PP sobre por qué se decantó por los socialistas.

Feijóo se ha defendido además de los casos de corrupción que afectaron a su partido y que fueron sentenciados. “Aquí, cada uno tiene su propia historia, ahora, de lo que ha pasado, cada uno tiene que aprender. Llevo cuatro años dirigiendo mi partido, a mí que se me juzgue. No acepto que nadie meta la mano en la caja. Al PP se le ha juzgado judicialmente y políticamente”, ha dicho en referencia a la Gürtel y a la moción de censura de 2018. “Los errores del pasado los asumimos”.

Por último, Feijóo no descarta del todo que Carlos Mazón siga en política tras las elecciones autonómicas de mayo del año que viene, cuando perderá su escaño como diputado valenciano. “El señor Mazón no es candidato a la presidencia de la Generalitat”, responde el líder del PP a Ricardo Moya en El podcast de la birra. “El señor Mazón es diputado en la Cámara. Ha cesado de sus responsabilidades de presidente de la Generalitat y, por tanto, en la siguiente legislatura veremos a ver lo que ocurre”, ha remachado el líder del PP. “Una dana no es una falta de mantenimiento y conservación, es un efecto meteorológico”, ha continuado Feijóo para cargar en su lugar contra el Gobierno central por los accidentes de trenes de Adamuz y Urda.

El jefe de la oposición compara además lo vivido en la Comunidad de Valenciana con lo sufrido en Letur (Castilla-La Mancha), para sostener que los efectos fueron similares, solo que el municipio albaceteño es más pequeño y por eso, ha dicho, el número de muertos —7— no fue tan elevado como en Valencia. “¿Qué censo tiene Letur? ¿Y cuántos muertos ha habido? Coge el porcentaje. Y el señor Page tenía la información que le daba la AEMET. No tenía más. Es que si no tienes más información y no tienes más competencias, tú ejecutas de acuerdo con tu información y competencias. Y el señor Mazón no tenía esa información y no tenía esas competencias”.

World.title: La industria audiovisual española celebra su papel protagonista
World.content:
El sector ha crecido en empresas, profesionales, espectadores y en presencia internacional, pero debe afrontar ahora el debate de ver cómo la inteligencia artificial va a cambiar el papel de los creadores

La bola negra, la aclamada película de Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi, se ha convertido en uno de los principales temas de conversación entre los amantes del cine. Y también entre los profesionales de esta industria. Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de DeAPlaneta Entertainment, una de las principales compañías españolas de distribución y producción cinematográfica, celebra la gran acogida que ha tenido en taquilla la cinta de Los Javis. Y así se lo reconoce a Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador de Filmin, la principal plataforma nacional de streaming, cuya compañía integra desde este verano a Elastica, distribuidora en España de La bola negra. Para Tous, sin embargo, el impacto de la película va más allá de las cifras y se refleja también en el interés que está despertando entre las nuevas generaciones: “Ves el público joven que se acerca, que descubre quién era Lorca, que descubre cosas sobre la Guerra Civil española, que le está retando a saber más”, apunta durante la conversación que ambos comparten en el nuevo capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell.

La película es el éxito más reciente de una industria que crece de manera sostenida tras el fuerte impacto de la pandemia, señala Segura. Un informe del Observatorio Nacional de Tecnología y Sociedad (ONTSI) cifra en 3.776 las empresas dedicadas a actividades cinematográficas, de vídeo y programas de televisión que existían en 2025, frente a las 2.901 de 2020, lo que supone un crecimiento del 30,2 %. A esta evolución se suma el progresivo regreso del público a las salas, cuya afluencia podría recuperar este año o el próximo los niveles previos a la pandemia, según Segura. Una recuperación que refuerza el buen momento de un sector que representa el 0,65 % del producto interior bruto (PIB) nacional y emplea a 63.000 personas.

“En 2007 se nos decía que el 'streaming' no funcionaría porque nadie pagaba por ver cine. Sabíamos que el futuro del cine sería la distribución por internet” Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador de Filmin, sobre los primeros pasos del negocio en España

Las fortalezas Un sector con escuelas de prestigio y vocación internacional

Distinguido por su talento creativo. España cuenta con una nutrida cantera de directores, guionistas, actores y profesionales técnicos altamente cualificados y experimentados, explica Juan Manuel Guimeráns, presidente de la Spain Film Commission, organización dedicada a atraer rodajes audiovisuales al país. Conforman una industria cinematográfica y televisiva consolidada que ha demostrado capacidad para abordar todos los géneros, del suspense a la ciencia ficción, pasando por la comedia y el drama histórico.

Con escuelas de prestigio. Dos centros educativos españoles figuran entre los 15 mejores de todo el mundo, de acuerdo con la revista estadounidenseThe Hollywood Reporter dedicada a las noticias sobre espectáculos. Sonla Escuela de Cinematografía y del Audiovisual de la Comunidad de Madrid (ECAM) y la Escola Superior de Cinema i Audiovisuals de Catalunya(ESCAC).

Con visibilidad en el extranjero. El sector impulsa la marca España de tres maneras.

La exportación de contenidos. Las producciones españolas han ganado relevancia en el extranjero gracias a directores como Alejandro Amenábar y Juan Antonio Bayona, series como La casa de papel y Élite, y empresas como El Ranchito, especializada en efectos visuales para Hollywood.

La coproducción internacional. Guimeráns señala que cada vez más países quieren coproducir con España sus proyectos.

La atracción de rodajes. “Este es un país seguro, que dispone de todo tipo de paisajes en muy pocos kilómetros cuadrados. Además, hay buenos incentivos fiscales y unas redes de logística y servicios complementarios, como catering o transporte, óptimas”, resalta el presidente de la Spain Film Commission.

Una potencia de la animación. España cuenta con profesionales altamente cualificados que desarrollan series y películas animadas que triunfan en todo el mundo, indica Guimeráns. El sector cuenta con los éxitos recientesde Robot Dreams (2023) y Buffalo Kids (2024), que recaudaron en el mundo el doble de lo que costaron.

“Estamos en un resurgir de las salas de cine, viendo cómo mucha gente joven acude porque así rompe con la rutina, sale de casa, deja el móvil, queda con sus amigos. Cuando hay una buena película mueve a la gente” Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador de Filmin, sobre la relación de los más jóvenes con el cine

Los desafíos Fomentar el empleo femenino y adaptarse a los cambios que ha traído la inteligencia artificial

El impacto de la inteligencia artificial. La irrupción de la IA no solo ha traído nuevas herramientas tecnológicas; está cambiado la manera de crear, producir y distribuir películas y ha abierto debates sobre el futuro de los profesionales y sus derechos. El reto en este sector, incide Guimeráns, va a ser gestionar la propiedad intelectual de todas las creaciones, de la imagen de las personas a los guiones y la música. Sin embargo, el presidente de la Spain Film Comission cree que la IA abre nuevas oportunidades para la creación y pone un ejemplo: “Una empresa española acaba de crear un gemelo digital de la biblioteca y el patio del Monasterio del Escorial. Muchos pueden pensar que eso hará que nadie quiera venir ya a rodar aquí, pero lo que va a permitir es dar posibilidad a todos los rodajes a los que Patrimonio tiene que decir que no por tener el calendario copado o porque suponen un riesgo para el estado del edificio”, explica.

Combatir la desigualdad. El desequilibrio entre hombres y mujeres es patente en casi todas las profesiones de esta industria, especialmente en los puestos de dirección y responsabilidad técnica. Según el informe anual de la Asociación de Mujeres Cineastas y de Medios Audiovisuales (CIMA), en 2024, las mujeres ocupaban el 38 % de los principales puestos de responsabilidad en los largometrajes españoles, frente al 62 % de los hombres.

Adaptarse a nuevos hábitos de consumo. El público está cada vez más disperso entre plataformas, salas, televisión y redes sociales. El consumo se desplaza hacia formatos más cortos y las audiencias se fragmentan en comunidades con intereses muy específicos. El reto de la industria está en saber cómo llevar a este público hacia el consumo tradicional o desarrollar contenidos y modelos de distribución adaptados a estas nuevas formas.

“Desde la pandemia, el público ha tardado en volver a las salas, tanto es así que este es el primer año en que se espera que la recaudación supere a la de 2019” Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de DeAPlaneta, sobre la paulatina recuperación del negocio de la exhibición de películas

World.title: “Amas da Terra son mujeres que protegen la tradición gallega y tejen las redes del futuro”
World.content:
El proyecto de la chef Lucía Freitas actúa como punto de encuentro para las artesanas, cocineras y otras profesionales gallegas que, con oficios tradicionales, constituyen la esencia vital de un territorio y ensalzan sus señas de identidad, como la gastronomía

La iniciativa de Amas da Terra surgió durante un viaje a Japón de la chef Lucía Freitas (Santiago de Compostela, 44 años). Allí conoció a las amas, las legendarias buceadoras dedicadas a la pesca a pulmón; y encontró en ellas un reflejo de muchas mujeres de su tierra. Inspirada por su ejemplo, impulsó un proyecto social para reunir, apoyar y poner en valor a las trabajadoras gallegas. “Amas da Terra son una inmensa minoría de mujeres que, con su trabajo, protegen la tradición, nuestra cultura y también tejen las redes del futuro”, explica la fundadora del restaurante A Tafona, que cuenta con una estrella Michelin y tres Soles Repsol, y de la barra gastronómica Lume, ambos en Santiago de Compostela.

Freitas ha promovido una comunidad de pequeñas productoras, artesanas y viticultoras; también de redeiras, que cosen, montan, reparan y unen las redes y los aparejos de pesca; muiñeiras, que trabajan en los molinos de agua; y cocineras profesionales que alimentan las zonas rurales. Tres de ellas regentan locales especialmente singulares en Lugo, que abren sus cocinas para dejar que los clientes se sienten a comer alrededor de la cocina de leña. Son oficios minoritarios y populares, que forman parte de la identidad del territorio y que, gracias a personas como ellas, siguen vigentes. Freitas considera que ellas son quienes mejor representan a cada comarca, pueblo o aldea de su región.

La vocación de Freitas comparte la misma esencia de Gastronomía para una Inmensa Minoría, la iniciativa de Cervezas 1906 que se creó para destacar a aquellos proyectos culinarios que parten de la tradición para innovar. Lo conduce la chef Verónica Gómez, quien pregunta a las integrantes de Amas da Terra sobre lo que sienten al defender ocupaciones tan únicas. El objetivo de Freitas es que esa particularidad sea compartida: crear un espacio de encuentro en el que puedan surgir sinergias. Quiere ayudar a mejorar sus ecosistemas laborales y que ellas se sientan acompañadas y valoradas.

World.title: Vivo en un piso de alquiler cuya dueña ha fallecido. ¿Me pueden echar sus sobrinos antes de que acabe el año de renovación?
World.content:
Pregunta. Vivo en un piso de alquiler en Sevilla. Firmé el contrato en 2018 y desde que vencieron los tres años que se recogía en el mismo he ido renovando año a año de manera tácita. Me acaban de comunicar que mi casera falleció en mayo, aunque sus herederos, que son sobrinos, no me habían dicho nada. Yo sigo pagando el alquiler a la cuenta a nombre de la fallecida. Me han dicho que quieren vender la vivienda en un futuro, pero que por ahora puedo permanecer en el piso. ¿Me pueden echar del piso antes de marzo, mes en el que acaba el año de renovación?, ¿si no me avisan con varios meses de antelación, se vuelve a renovar el contrato en marzo aunque la persona esté fallecida? María G.

Respuesta. Al haberse celebrado el contrato en el año 2018, resulta de aplicación la legislación vigente en ese momento. Así, de conformidad con el artículo 10 de la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos (LAU), una vez transcurridos los tres años de duración del contrato, este se prorrogará por anualidades, salvo que cualquiera de las partes comunique a la otra su voluntad de no renovarlo con una antelación mínima de treinta días respecto de la fecha de finalización de la prórroga.

Por otro lado, una vez fallecido el arrendador, sus herederos suceden al causante en la titularidad de sus bienes y derechos. En consecuencia, los herederos se subrogan en la posición del arrendador, manteniéndose vigentes las condiciones inicialmente pactadas en el contrato de arrendamiento.

No obstante, si los herederos transmiten la vivienda a un tercero ajeno a la relación arrendaticia que reúna los requisitos establecidos en el artículo 34 de la Ley Hipotecaria, este no quedará subrogado en la posición del arrendador, salvo que el contrato de arrendamiento se encuentre inscrito en el Registro de la Propiedad.

Por lo tanto, si la vivienda acaba siendo adjudicada o adquirida por uno de los herederos, se mantendrán íntegramente las condiciones del contrato de arrendamiento. Sin embargo, si la adquiere un tercero que reúna los requisitos legales anteriormente indicados, este podría solicitar de forma inmediata la posesión de la finca.

Asimismo, si la finca no estuviera inscrita en el Registro de la Propiedad, el adquirente también podría solicitar la extinción del arrendamiento, si bien los inquilinos tendrían derecho a exigir que se les permita continuar en la vivienda durante un plazo de tres meses.

En conclusión, si quien compra es un tercero del que podemos acreditar que tenía conocimiento de la existencia del contrato de arrendamiento, podremos exigirle el cumplimiento de este y, por tanto, mantener la relación arrendaticia en las condiciones pactadas hasta la finalización de la prórroga correspondiente.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Así se pensó, diseñó y construyó uno de los museos más sostenibles del mundo
World.content:
El antiguo edificio Pereda de Santander ha alcanzado la máxima calificación BREEAM obtenida por un museo gracias a una rehabilitación que combina soluciones arquitectónicas singulares, tecnologías pioneras y una gestión integral de la sostenibilidad. Este proyecto que preserva su patrimonio mirando al futuro recibirá este noviembre su certificado definitivo

Dos edificios decimonónicos anexos, sede histórica del Banco Santander en el paseo de Pereda y frente al mar, se han convertido en uno de los museos más excepcionales y sostenibles del mundo. Así lo refleja el 92,96% obtenido en la certificación BREEAM, uno de los sistemas de evaluación con mayor trayectoria y reconocimiento internacional, que analiza distintas categorías como la eficiencia ambiental, el confort o la salubridad.

Es la máxima nota recibida hasta hoy por una institución museística en todo el planeta en este sistema de medida, un logro —más destacado si cabe por tratarse de una rehabilitación y no de un inmueble de nueva planta— cuyo mérito se reparten el estudio de arquitectura del ganador del Pritzker David Chipperfield, la firma de servicios de ingeniería, consultoría y arquitectura IDOM y el mismo Banco Santander, impulsor de un diseño pensado para la excelencia, para durar. Contamos cómo se ideó y parió Faro Santander.

Los diez criterios BREEAM para medir un museo sostenible BREEAM es un sistema internacional de evaluación y certificación de la sostenibilidad de los edificios 01 Gestión Seguimiento de consumos y control de residuos durante la obra 02 Confort y bienestar Climatización TABS, aire filtrado y control de humedad y CO₂ 03 Energía Geotermia y aprovechamiento de la inercia térmica del hormigón 04 Transporte Aparcamientos para bicicletas y acceso en transporte público 05 Agua Recogida de lluvia para aseos y riego de jardines 06 Materiales Recuperación de suelos, madera y piedra del edificio original 07 Residuos El 98 % de los residuos fueron reutilizados o reciclados 08 Uso del suelo y ecología Terrazas ajardinadas, polinizadores y recuperación de arbolado 09 Contaminación Energía de origen 100% renovable y medidas contra la contaminación acústica 10 Innovación Combinación pionera de geotermia y climatización TABS en una rehabilitación

“El edificio de Pereda era fundamental para la ciudad y estaba cerrado. Fueron oficinas. Y había que hacer de él un edificio público, abierto a la gente: que desde dentro uno estuviera en contacto con Santander y desde fuera tuviera ganas de internarse”, recuerda Jose Azevedo, arquitecto portugués responsable de proyectos del estudio de Chipperfield.

Hallar una forma que respaldase esa concepción tan crucial para el tipo de museo naciente fue el primer y gran reto del encargo. Una singularidad que traía aparejada su recompensa: “Normalmente”, cuenta Azevedo, “cuando llevas a cabo la rehabilitación o construcción de un museo, te basas en la historia y principios de la institución, sus necesidades instruyen al arquitecto. Aquí estábamos entre todos dando a luz a la institución. De alguna manera, nos sentimos parte fundadora de ese carácter que va a definir a Faro Santander”. Un lugar de exhibición y creación, para el arte y la tecnología. Para la gente.

Gracias a la combinación de la geotermia y la termoactivación de los forjados (TABS), que aprovecha la masa térmica del hormigón mediante circuitos de agua integrados en la estructura, el propio edificio contribuye a proporcionar calefacción y refrigeración

Las fachadas del siglo XIX de piedra de Boñar debían mantenerse, se restauraron con caliza de la cantera leonesa original. La complejidad de que un edificio histórico no perdiera un ápice de su identidad y, a la vez, albergara en sus tripas una transformación tan profunda, era de tal magnitud que el equipo de arquitectos decidió no abordarlo como una única operación. Desarrolló distintas intervenciones —las galerías, la cubierta, el arco— bajo un mismo concepto arquitectónico, hasta conseguir a posteriori que todas funcionaran como conjunto. “No fue un ejercicio fácil. Tuvimos que trabajar y trabajar y trabajar... hasta que todo casó”, explica Azevedo.

El arco, uno de los elementos vehiculares de la rehabilitación, articula el edificio. Se trata de una estructura suspendida cuya construcción requirió una meticulosa labor de ensamblaje. Pero su valor va mucho más allá del ingenio técnico o lo estético. Para Azevedo, se trata de la materialización de la idea de conectar visual y espacialmente Faro con Santander: “Cuando estás ahí, de veras te hallas frente al mar, a la vez dentro y fuera”.

Uno de los elementos arquitectónicos más destacados de la rehabilitación es esta escalera helicoidal de hormigón pulido, que preside el vestíbulo, justo tras el arco central. Faro Santander

La sostenibilidad, en los cimientos de la rehabilitación

La sostenibilidad condicionó cada paso antes aún de que se trazase el primer boceto de un plano. “Poner el lazo cuando las cosas ya están hechas no funciona”, dice Sergio Arús, consultor de IDOM y asesor de la Fundación Santander y del equipo de arquitectura durante el proceso de acreditación BREEAM de Faro Santander. Cada avance de diseño se sometía al más estricto control de los criterios técnicos.

“La primera gran decisión, tomada tras mucha meditación, fue vaciar el interior del edificio, acometer la demolición y excavar”, cuenta Arús. Un proceso en el que se consiguieron hitos que van a suponer un ejemplo a imitar en cualquier obra: un 98% de los residuos que se generaron pudieron reutilizarse o reciclarse, solo un 2% de los cascotes y desechos acabaron en el vertedero.

“Se reaprovecharon, bien restaurados, suelos de madera o de piedra; incluso se fabricaron cajas de registro o mobiliario con madera procedente de los encofrados”, cuenta Arús, que explica cómo, por ejemplo, se desecaron in situ los lodos que generó la excavación, para que no contaminasen ni hubiera decenas de camiones incursionando hasta el centro de Santander para cargarlos y transportarlos, con la polución que eso hubiera ocasionado. Ningún detalle se dejó al azar. Y aquellos restos que no podían tener una nueva utilidad se clasificaron y enviaron a gestores autorizados, para su tratamiento y posterior reciclaje.

Una rehabilitación integral que no renuncia a su esencia Mantener las fachadas decimonónicas de la antigua sede central del Banco Santander, realizadas con piedra caliza de Boñar (León), supuso un gran reto técnico.



Foto: Juan Baraja Tras una deliberación minuciosa, se decidió vaciar el interior del edificio y levantar una nueva estructura.



Foto: Juan Baraja La complejidad de la rehabilitación era tal que diseñaron individualmente cada intervención y luego las armonizaron. Eso sí, teniendo en cuenta criterios de sostenibilidad en cada paso.



Plano: Estudio de arquitectura

de Chipperfield La excavación sirvió para instalar el innovador sistema de geotermia. Aunque se generaron lodos, se desecaron y reciclaron en la misma obra para evitar contaminación.



Foto: Juan Baraja Es la única rehabilitación de un museo que ha obtenido una calificación BREEAM de 92,96% en todo el mundo.



Foto: Juan Baraja Alzado del diseño de Faro Santander llevado a cabo por el estudio de arquitectura de David Chipperfield, galardonado en 2023 con el premio Pritzker

Pero si hay una innovación que permite comprender hasta qué punto Faro Santander es un edificio diferente hay que buscarla bajo los pies de los visitantes. Oculto en la propia estructura del edificio está uno de los ingenios para regular la temperatura de sus más de 10.000 metros cuadrados de salas de exposición y pasillos. Un sistema llamado TABS (Thermally Activated Building Structures) que, como explica Azevedo, “integra tuberías en los forjados de hormigón”. Por ellas circula agua, que aprovecha la inercia térmica de la propia estructura para calentar o enfriar los espacios. En invierno, basta que el agua alcance unos 23 grados para mantener un ambiente cálido; en verano, a unos 19 grados ya enfría. El hormigón funciona “como una gran batería térmica que mantiene las condiciones ambientales con oscilaciones mínimas”, describe Arús.

¿Y cómo se calienta o enfría el agua de esas tuberías? Gracias a la geotermia. “Es la primera vez que, en mi experiencia”, relata Azevedo, “conseguimos aunar ambas técnicas en un edificio”. Varias sondas geotérmicas enterradas en el subsuelo santanderino, que mantiene durante todo el año una temperatura suave y estable, se conectan a esas tuberías de los TABS conformando un circuito cerrado. El fluido procedente de las sondas del subsuelo, en invierno, llega a unas bombas que extraen el calor del terreno y lo elevan; en verano el ciclo se invierte, y las bombas lo que hacen es disipar el calor interno del edificio y derivarlo al subsuelo, que actúa “como una gran piscina”, dice Arús, que añade que “de esta manera se pueden alcanzar ahorros energéticos muy importantes frente a soluciones convencionales, y además se evita depender de los habituales equipos exteriores de climatización. Así fuimos capaces de liberar de buena parte de la maquinaria la cubierta”.

Además de una temperatura estable todo el año, se controlan las emisiones de dióxido de carbono y la humedad del ambiente, lo que garantiza una buena conservación para la pintura y el resto de obras de arte de la colección. Xoan Vázquez (Faro Santander)

La calidad del aire también está cuidadosamente controlada. El sistema de ventilación introduce aire exterior filtrado y recupera parte de la energía del aire extraído antes de expulsarlo. Así, en los días fríos, el aire que entra en las galerías puede llegar previamente atemperado. Con estas medidas más las que se encargan de la regulación de la humedad relativa y del CO₂ lo que se obtiene es un ambiente perfecto y salubre. “Es la manera idónea para preservar la gran colección de pintura y obras de arte de Faro Santander, ¡pero también de procurar un gran confort a los visitantes y trabajadores del museo!, aduce Arús.

La azotea y los jardines

La cubierta, con vistas espectaculares de la bahía, es un espacio amplio y perfectamente accesible. Una zona en la que apetece estar, con cafetería y jardines, y en la que se instalaron, como los denomina Arús, “hoteles de insectos”, que cumplen una misión: la de polinizar a todas las especies de plantas y árboles de esos jardines. “Las zonas verdes y la biodiversidad son también una prioridad en BREEAM”, explica Arús, que cuenta cómo se trasplantaron aquellos árboles que hubo que reubicar por las obras, y cómo luego se plantaron otros nuevos, aumentando netamente la masa forestal.

También destacan el arquitecto y el consultor otro aspecto: la gestión del agua. Un depósito recoge el agua de lluvia, que se reutiliza en el riego de las terrazas y en los inodoros. Grifos y duchas de vestuarios y baños son de bajo consumo, y los sistemas de riego son todos inteligentes.

Vistas desde la azotea de Faro Santander J.A.C.

La ubicación de Faro Santander, en el centro de la ciudad, favorece los desplazamientos a pie o el buen acceso en transporte público. Otro de los aspectos que mide BREEAM. Sin embargo, para ofrecer más alternativas, planearon y construyeron aparcamientos cerrados de bicicleta, pensados sobre todo para los trabajadores.

“Hemos demostrado que se puede construir pensando en la sostenibilidad y en las generaciones futuras sin hacer ningún sacrificio”, presume Azevedo. Una reflexión que se une a la metáfora de Arús, perfecto colofón de esa idea: “Si dentro de cien años el edificio deja de ser un museo, el hardware seguirá siendo valioso, y con una pequeña actualización de software podrá tener cualquier otro uso”.

World.title: Szczecin, un oasis urbano poco conocido entre Berlín y Varsovia
World.content:
