World.title: Insurers have settled majority of Pärnu flooding claims
World.content:
Insurance companies have settled three-quarters of the claims filed following September's flooding in Pärnu. The downpour caused €8.5 million in damage and repairs are still underway in several locations.

Those affected by the flooding in Pärnu in early September have filed 825 insurance claims totaling approximately €8.5 million.

"Home insurance accounts for the largest number of claims and in terms of value, around €5 million of the damage was to homes in Pärnu County. The main damage was caused by floodwater entering houses, apartments and other residential buildings and wreaking havoc inside," said Tuuli Pärenson, chair of the board of the Estonian Insurance Association.

The flooding also affected 99 businesses, which suffered a combined €745,000 in damage. The Rääma residential neighborhood was the hardest hit.

"Water backed up through my shower drain, causing around €7,000 in damage. Everyone on our street had their basements flooded, damaging their heating systems," said homeowner Tiina Meriküla.

Insurance company Ergo has received just under 100 claims, most of which have been approved for compensation.

"We also saw quite a few cases where utility rooms had been built on the lower floors of buildings. When heating equipment was submerged, the damage was quite extensive, reaching around €10,000 in some cases," said Taavi Kööts, head of Ergo's property claims department. "Our largest claim, including household belongings, is around €100,000."

Many Pärnu residents are still waiting for repairs to be completed.

"With larger claims, gathering the necessary information inevitably takes time and quite a few of the more severely damaged properties are actually still drying out," Kööts noted.

"I contacted my insurance company on the very first day and received a response a week and a half later. The insurer sent Vaskor Ehitus over just a few days after that," Meriküla said.

Workers from construction company Vaskor Ehitus have been dealing with flood damage every day for the past two months.

"We're about halfway through. Many houses have been opened up and are still drying out and restoration work hasn't started yet. I think it'll take us until Christmas to get the situation more or less under control," said Tamo Toodo, a project manager at Vaskor Ehitus.

So far, 75 percent of insurance claims have been approved, while the payout amounts or circumstances of the remaining cases are still under review. Approximately one in 10 claims was rejected.

"The saddest and, on a human level, most tragic reason is when the insurance coverage was insufficient. When taking out the policy, the person had chosen not to include flood coverage," Pärenson said.

"Another major category of cases in which insurers don't pay compensation is when people have failed to act reasonably or responsibly. I think the most striking examples were those that also made it onto television where people chose to drive their cars into water that was waist-deep, knee-deep or thigh-deep," she added.

Insurers received 44 vehicle insurance claims totaling €82,000, eight of which were rejected.

World.title: Estonian agency decides country needs signature scent, spends €13,327
World.content:
Estonia is looking to make a lasting impression on foreign dignitaries with specially developed fragrances capturing the scents of its coastline, forests and bogs.

The Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS) is inviting government agencies and other organizations to join a joint procurement of official gifts featuring signature fragrances inspired by Estonia's natural landscapes, Postimees writes.

According to Triin Joasaar, head of the e-Estonia Briefing Center, the initiative aims to offer high-level foreign visitors a memorable alternative to traditional souvenirs.

Developed in collaboration with perfumer Tom Olaf Urb, the two fragrances are called "Coast & Sea," a fresh scent inspired by Estonia's coastline and islands, and "Forest & Bog," an earthy, slightly smoky fragrance reflecting the country's autumn landscapes.

The gifts include signature perfume and rock-shaped room diffusers made from fungi and wood waste by Estonian company Myceen, while both fragrances are also available as soy wax candles.

A scented candle costs €15, while a perfume and diffuser set costs €50, excluding VAT.

Joasaar said the project has so far cost €13,327 excluding VAT, funded through the budgets of the e-Estonia Briefing Center and other EIS units involved in international relations.

EIS has ordered 100 scented candles, 10 liters of signature fragrance and 200 room diffusers, primarily intended for visiting foreign delegations and international partners.

One of the scented candles has also been included among gifts intended for the Finnish president.

EIS is currently assessing demand from other government agencies for a new order, which is expected to be similar in size to or smaller than the initial purchase, the paper reports.

World.title: Tallinn to begin major tram track repairs in spring, wrapping up in 2029
World.content:
Major work to the tramlines network in Tallinn starts in spring, though while they are set to last to 2029, should not disrupt traffic unduly, Tallinn City Government said.

Tallinna Linnatransport will next year repair tram tracks on Narva mnt and Maneeži tänav in the city center and the Majaka curve in Sikupilli. This will mean the temporary closure of service in the case of the Narva mnt section.

Three sections will be worked on concurrently; with Narva mnt the stretch from Poska tänav to Tallinn University will begin in late May to early June next year, Tallinn Deputy Mayor Joel Jesse (Center) told ERR, to be followed by the continuation to Maneeži tänav to the west.

"The aim is to renew and modernize the tracks, including all the necessary switches, new sleepers and the entire control system. There will definitely be less noise and vibration in the future," he said.

Work on the stretch between the university and Maneeži tänav will have to wait till 2029, however, to avoid disruption to the Laulupidu taking place in summer 2028. Tram service to Kadriorg, served by lines 3 and 4, will be suspended during the course of the repair work next summer.

The work may also disrupt other traffic, but it will still be able to pass in both directions, Jesse said.

Another major repair project taking place on Maneeži tänav, between Narva mnt and Gonsiori, where lines 4 and 6 run, is due to the need to replace worn tracks, Jesse went on. "

As part of the work, we plan to install a switch on Maneeži tänav toward Kadriorg so we have more options when there's a disruption. That will let us reroute trams as needed and keep them running on shorter sections when a line is disrupted," the deputy mayor said.

Tram service to the airport will continue during the repairs, Jesse went on. Trams will be routed via Laikmaa and Gonsiori streets.

The third project will take place at what is known as the Majaka curve, where the tracks have also reached the end of their service life, Jesse said. TLT is due to install track lubricators there and plans to install them at tram switches across the city later.

This should among other things reduce the squealing when trams pass over switches, Jesse said. Tram service will be able to continue through the Majaka stretch during the repairs.

World.title: Minister: I understand Narva's concerns, but Estonia's security is more important
World.content:
Minister of Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said he understands the concerns of Narva residents over the planned closure of the eastern border, but said the government must prioritize the safety of all Estonian residents.

On Saturday night, an attempt was made to set fire to the Threod drone factory in Viimsi. The Internal Security Service (KAPO) said the attack was ordered by Russia, and the government wants to respond by closing the border with Russia.

Although the saboteurs did not cross the Russian border, Taro said the necessary analysis has been carried out and shows that there are now grounds to close Estonia's land borders at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula from December 1.

"They did not cross the Russian border, they came across the Latvian border, but Russia ordered the operation. What has changed is that we have been subjected to two very specific attacks. That is the change," Taro said on Tuesday's "Esimene stuudio."

He said the attack on the Threod must not be treated as an isolated incident, as Russia wants to divide the whole of Europe.

Threod Systems. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

"They have said so themselves, they made their plans public quite some time ago, saying that all organizations and companies that support Ukraine to any extent are legitimate targets. We must look at the bigger picture and ensure that not only Estonia but the whole of Europe is an unfavorable operating environment for Russian intelligence services," Taro said.

However, the interior minister does not think it is necessary to close the border with Latvia, as the two countries cooperate well and law enforcement agencies are able to mitigate threats.

"As for the Russian border, an open border crossing point and traffic across the Estonian-Russian border always pose an additional risk. We have deployed an enormous amount of resources to border surveillance, customs checks and counterintelligence to mitigate these threats. You may have heard that our border controls are currently among the strictest in the world. The capacity of border crossing points is extremely low, everything is checked very thoroughly, and both vehicles and people go through X-ray screening. This requires enormous resources. If we see that we need to start dealing with a greater challenge, where Russia is targeting not only Estonia but Europe and NATO more generally, then we need to minimize these risks. The simplest and most effective way to minimize these risks across our border is to close traffic there," Taro explained.

However, many Narva residents are concerned, as many regularly cross the border to visit relatives.

The bridge over the River Narva, connecting Russia and Estonia. Source: Helen Wright /ERR

Taro said he understood their concerns but considers the safety of all Estonian residents more important.

"My task, however, is to stand up for the security and safety of everyone living in Estonia. This is where the decision must be weighed. The war that Russia has launched against Ukraine has caused suffering to very many people, not only in Ukraine but elsewhere as well. In our case, it brings inconvenience to certain people, but we must understand that the cause of this war and the entire situation is Russia's aggressive actions. That should not be forgotten," the minister stressed.

The recommendation to close the border came from one of Estonia's security agencies, he added.

"If we look at the broader picture, not just these incidents, from damage to our critical infrastructure to incidents at the border, we have always tried to respond very precisely, and that is what we have done. We have simply reached a situation where a security agency has also said that this is the right measure. It allows us to mitigate and reduce certain other risks and, among other things, sends Russia a very clear message that every action has a consequence and a price," Taro said.

The government will discuss closing the border indefinitely on Friday. Taro said time-limited restrictions have been tried before, but so far the other side has not taken such decisions seriously.

Luhamaa border crossing in southeastern Estonia. Source: Mirjam Mõttus/ERR

"We have imposed these three-month deadlines, but they have not borne fruit. We have had to extend them and introduce additional restrictions. The government can discuss this, and there are both pros and cons. I am inclined to think that if we look at the pattern Russia is pursuing, if it has already carried out kinetic attacks against our companies on two occasions... These are not some random border incidents like some of the previous ones we have had, where one might have asked whether someone had perhaps done something by accident. It is very difficult to foresee anything changing here in the near future, in three or six months. Rather, we are dealing with a long-term concern and challenge, and we probably cannot make a different decision until the circumstances we have discussed today no longer exist," the minister said.

The minister also confirmed that he informed the Latvian interior minister as soon as closing the border came onto the agenda.

"Of course, they were also informed about the joint operation. But as soon as the possibility of closing the Estonian-Russian border came onto the agenda, I passed that information on to him. For them, it is a matter for discussion whether they want to be the conduit or opening through which everything from Russia passes, both good and bad. Or whether they adopt a more unified approach and perhaps also impose restrictions or close everything altogether. That is their sovereign decision," Taro said.

The Estonian-Russian border runs through Lake Peipus. Border crossing points are highlighted on the map. Source: Helen Wright/ERR/OSM

World.title: More ambulance crews planned for Tallinn amid growing delays
World.content:
Tallinn Ambulance chief Raul Adlas says ambulance resources and hospital intake capacity have failed to keep pace with population growth in Tallinn and the surrounding region, contributing to delays in emergency care. The Health Board plans to add ambulance crews in the capital region in 2027 and 2028.

"The number of ambulance crews serving this area is relatively small. As a result, when call volumes increase, it becomes very difficult to respond quickly and some calls end up waiting in a queue," Adlas said.

He added the formation of queues is not directly linked to the number of ambulance calls but rather occurs when hospitals become overloaded.

"When that bottleneck begins to form, it spreads to ambulance services as well. If hospitals cannot immediately receive patients from ambulance crews, those crews end up waiting outside emergency departments. Calls then have to wait, ambulance teams from other counties are brought into Tallinn to help, queues begin forming there as well, and the snowball starts rolling. As a rule, this is caused by hospital intake capacity being too small," Adlas noted.

The highest number of calls in Tallinn typically occurs on Friday nights. On the busiest days, call volumes exceed 200 per 24-hour period. Workloads also increase during outbreaks of viral illnesses. Major public events in the city likewise generate additional emergency calls.

Raul Adlas Source: Kirke Ert/ERR

Roughly half of Estonia's population lives in Tallinn and Harju County. Outside Tallinn, however, there are no major hospitals in Harju County, making it necessary to transport patients to the capital. Adlas compared the situation to southern Estonia, where every county has a large hospital. The municipalities surrounding Tallinn have about as many residents as the counties of southern Estonia combined, yet places such as Viimsi Municipality do not have a major hospital.

As a solution, Adlas said the number of ambulance crews in northern Estonia should be increased. In addition, emergency departments need more staff and greater capacity to receive patients.

Taavet Reimers, deputy director general of the Health Board, said the agency's analysis confirms that there are indeed too few ambulance crews.

"By 2028, the plan is to increase the number of crews in northern Estonia by six," Reimers said. "In 2027, two additional ambulance crews will be added to the Tallinn area on top of the existing resources."

Reimers also agreed that emergency rooms should receive additional capacity. Current bed numbers were planned for a smaller population than now lives in Tallinn. Further analysis will determine how many additional places need to be created.

Ambulance. Photo is illustrative. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Ambulance network will be reorganized

On Wednesday, the Health Board also announced a reorganization of Estonia's ambulance network, dividing the country into four regions and allowing two-person ambulance crews to be deployed when necessary.

Nikita Panjuškin, head of the Healthcare Services Department at the Ministry of Social Affairs, said ambulance availability is currently uneven.

"There are regions where an ambulance arrives in an average of six minutes, but there are also places where the average wait exceeds 30 minutes," Panjuškin said.

Beginning in 2028, Estonia's current 10 ambulance service areas will be replaced by four regions: Northern, Eastern, Western and Southern Estonia.

According to Panjuškin, the plan is not to replace three-person ambulance crews on a large scale with two-person units. Instead, the smaller crews will complement existing three-person teams. "This will allow us to respond to more calls simultaneously and reduce the likelihood that all crews are occupied at the same time," he said.

Panjuškin said the number of physician-led ambulance crews will decrease, with some being replaced by nurse-led crews. The role of the remaining physician crews will also become more clearly defined.

"We believe a physician's primary role in emergency medical services should be to support nurse-led crews when they need consultation by phone or when a patient is in such an unstable condition that a physician is required. The vast majority of calls can be handled by specially trained nurses," he said.

Two new ambulance bases will be established in the Tallinn area, one in Hiiu or Pääsküla and another in Tabasalu or Muraste. They are intended to reduce the workload on Tallinn ambulance crews and make it easier to deploy crews across Tallinn and Harju County.

Additional ambulance bases will be established in Riisipere, Narva-Jõesuu, Sindi, Audru or Tõstamaa, and the Rõuge or Mõniste area. Where two alternative locations are listed, the final site will be selected by the winning service provider in the procurement process.

Until the end of 2027, ambulance services will continue under existing contracts. The changes will take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

This article was updated Wednesday with details of the ambulance network reorganization plan.

World.title: Flu vaccines run out already in some family medicine centers
World.content:
The flu vaccine arrived in Estonia later than usual this year, but some medical centers have already run out of doses. The vaccine should still be available at locations across the country.

According to the State Agency of Medicines, the first batch of flu vaccines arrived in Estonia in late October and the second in mid-November, with a third batch expected in January.

The vaccine is currently not available everywhere. For example, the Pirita Family Medicine Center announced Tuesday that its supply of vaccines for at-risk groups had lasted just seven days and that those who did not manage to get vaccinated in time would likely have to wait until January.

"Disappointment and frustration over how this has been organized should be directed at the Estonian Health Insurance Fund. Primary care providers cannot prevent illness if family medicine centers do not have access to preventive vaccines," the center said in a social media post expressing its frustration.

At West Tallinn Central Hospital's infectious diseases clinic, flu vaccinations using the standard injectable vaccine have been temporarily suspended for adults and children. However, vaccines remain available for people in at-risk groups, while children up to age 17 can also receive the vaccine in the form of a nasal spray.

A search for available flu vaccination appointments at pharmacies in various counties on the Apotheka website turned up no openings.

"We apologize, but the service is either unavailable at your selected pharmacy or all appointments have already been booked," the website states.

A search shows that vaccines are still available at Medicum, while Confido also confirmed to ERR that it has sufficient supplies. However, all appointments through the end of November have been booked for both free flu vaccinations for at-risk groups and paid vaccinations.

"We are continually opening new vaccination appointments, which will be added to our online booking system," said Confido Marketing Manager Eve Kaljusaar.

Vaccine availability differs by region

Evelin Kruusalu, chief public relations specialist at the Estonian Health Insurance Fund, said Estonia has not run out of flu vaccines nationwide.

"The free flu vaccines for at-risk groups that arrived in October and November have all been distributed from the Health Insurance Fund's central warehouse to our partners, but vaccines are still available at vaccination sites across Estonia," she confirmed.

Kruusalu acknowledged that vaccine availability varies by region and provider, which is why the Health Insurance Fund recommends checking whether vaccines are available at a particular location before going there to get vaccinated.

Estonia has ordered nearly 233,000 doses of flu vaccine for this season, including 140,000 doses ordered by the Health Insurance Fund for at-risk groups. Of those, approximately 103,000 doses have arrived in two shipments so far.

"This is slightly more than last flu season, when approximately 210,000 doses were brought into Estonia," Kruusalu said.

Nearly 103,000 vaccine doses have been delivered to vaccination sites and as of Wednesday, 57,000 doses had been administered to people in at-risk groups and other individuals seeking vaccination.

"The number of doses distributed and the number administered cannot therefore be compared directly, but the data shows that a significant proportion of the vaccines are currently at vaccination sites across Estonia," the Health Insurance Fund representative added.

Nasal spray vaccine not suitable for adults

The Health Insurance Fund's partners have ordered vaccines as expected this year and according to Kruusalu, a large proportion of the vaccines intended for at-risk groups are distributed from the fund's warehouse within the first two weeks.

The Fluenz nasal spray flu vaccine for children remains available at several locations where supplies of injectable vaccines have run out. However, Kruusalu said it cannot be used as a substitute for adults, even when injectable vaccines are in short supply.

"This is a live attenuated vaccine, which differs from injectable inactivated flu vaccines in both its composition and method of administration," Kruusalu explained, adding that it is intended for children and adolescents ages 2 to 17. "The suitability of the vaccine must also be assessed based on the child's health, as live vaccines are not suitable for all children."

More people are eligible for free flu vaccinations this season, as at-risk groups now also include adults ages 18 to 59 who are at increased risk of developing severe influenza due to an underlying health condition. This has expanded the population eligible for free vaccination.

According to Kruusalu, the available data does not yet allow for any definitive conclusions about whether demand for flu vaccinations is higher this year than in previous years.

"The pace of vaccine distribution has been as expected, but actual vaccination coverage and total demand for the season can only be assessed once more vaccination data has been entered into the health information system," she said.

New vaccine composition behind later deliveries

Kruusalu attributed the unusually late arrival of flu vaccines this year — the State Agency of Medicines previously announced that the third shipment would not arrive in Estonia until January — to a World Health Organization recommendation to update all three virus strains included in the flu vaccine at the same time.

"Although the composition of flu vaccines is updated every year, it is rare for all three components to be changed simultaneously. This has affected production, quality control and delivery schedules in several European countries, which is why vaccines are arriving in Estonia in stages," Kruusalu said.

She added that the Health Insurance Fund conducted its procurement as scheduled, but when production plans change, vaccine manufacturers' representatives determine how supplies are allocated among countries and which deliveries are prioritized. The manufacturer's forecast remains unchanged: the next shipment of vaccines for at-risk groups is expected to arrive in Estonia in January next year. Deliveries have been delayed across Europe.

"The Health Insurance Fund is working with its partners to explore ways to bring the next shipment to Estonia sooner, but this depends on the manufacturer's capacity," Kruusalu said, adding that the fund would immediately announce any changes to the delivery schedule.

During the 2025-2026 flu season, 197,161 people in Estonia were vaccinated against influenza.

World.title: Estonian-built warship launched at Saaremaa shipyard
World.content:
The 45-meter EUROGUARD warship, built at Baltic Workboats' shipyard in Nasva as part of a joint project involving 10 European countries and 27 companies, was christened by President Ülle Madise on Wednesday.

Following the launch, work will continue on outfitting the vessel, integrating technological systems and conducting trials to assess the performance of the developed solutions and their readiness for future maritime operations. The vessel and the systems developed aboard it are scheduled for further testing and demonstrations in 2027.

"Ships have been built in Estonia and sold abroad for centuries. Military vessels, however, have generally been ordered from abroad, relying on the experience of our allies," said Baltic Workboats CEO Margus Vanaselja. "Europe's first modular warship prototype of its kind at 45 meters in length, demonstrates that we are now capable of building military vessels ourselves. This project shows that even smaller allies can make a decisive contribution to strengthening Europe's collective defense capabilities."

The EUROGUARD vessel is being equipped with both autonomous navigation capabilities and the ability to be remotely operated from shore. Source: Pilleli Läets

The project's budget is approximately €95 million, of which €65 million is funded by the European Defense Fund.

The vessel is being equipped with both autonomous navigation capabilities and the ability to be remotely operated from shore. Its modular design allows the platform to be adapted for maritime surveillance, mine warfare, seabed and critical infrastructure protection, search-and-rescue operations, and the deployment and control of unmanned systems.

The vessel has a designed speed of at least 20 knots, a range of at least 2,000 nautical miles and an operational endurance of up to 10 days at sea.

President Ülle Madise at the launch event. Source: Pilleli Läets

World.title: Yemen law criminalizes Houthi activities, opens door to domestic and international prosecution
World.content:
ADEN: Yemen's government has moved beyond designating the Houthi group a terrorist organization to establishing a broad legal framework aimed at criminalizing its activities and prosecuting its leaders, financiers and affiliated entities.

The legislation brings the group's financing, recruitment and arms supply networks, as well as attacks on civilians and international shipping, within the scope of criminal accountability. It also gives authorities legal tools to trace assets and funds both inside Yemen and abroad.

On Wednesday, Rashad al-Alimi, Chairman of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, issued Law No. 1 of 2026 on the designation of the Houthi group as a terrorist organization and the criminalization of its activities and financing, following approval by the Cabinet and Parliament.

The legislation puts the terrorist designation into effect across the group's political, military, security and administrative structures, establishing a series of criminal, financial and administrative measures alongside mechanisms for international judicial cooperation.

The law goes beyond criminalizing direct military actions to encompass the organizational, economic and media structures operating on the group's behalf. It establishes individual and institutional responsibility according to the nature of their roles and proven connections, while introducing legal safeguards to prevent the designation from imposing collective liability on civilians or legitimate activities in Houthi-controlled areas.

Under Article 4, the law designates the Houthi group, which calls itself Ansar Allah, a terrorist organization in all its organizational structures and formations, including individuals and groups.

The designation extends to affiliated entities, including political, military, security and administrative leadership, as well as partisan, civil, cultural, social, media and economic organizations, where organizational links to the group have been established.

The legislation extends beyond the official names and front organizations the Houthis may use to conduct their activities or reorganize their structures.

An entity is considered affiliated with the group if evidence establishes that the Houthis created, manage or exercise direct or indirect organizational control over it, or that it operates in their name or on their behalf as part of their organizational structure.

However, the law places an important restriction on the scope of liability. It states that the designation does not constitute a conviction of any particular individual or eliminate the requirement to prove the elements of an alleged offense.

Nor does the designation automatically extend to individuals or entities merely because they maintain commercial or social relationships with the group or its members, or reside in areas under its control.

The law therefore distinguishes between proven organizational affiliation and legitimate civil and economic dealings. Decisions to list affiliated entities, along with measures taken against them, are subject to objections and appeals before the competent courts.

Severe Penalties

The legislation defines a broad range of acts as terrorist offenses, including using armed force to seize state authority or undermine constitutional institutions, besieging cities and villages, starving populations, targeting civilians, public facilities and private property, planting landmines, and attacking or disrupting international shipping.

Penalties for these offenses range from 20 to 30 years in prison to the death penalty. Under the law, the death penalty applies when offenses specified in Articles 5 through 10 result in death or permanent disability.

Criminal liability is not limited to actions carried out on the ground. The law also criminalizes membership in or joining the Houthi group, prescribing prison sentences of 10 to 15 years.

Those exercising effective leadership within the group face the death penalty, whether they hold a publicly declared leadership position or exercise significant authority over issuing orders, managing resources, supervising personnel or making organizational decisions.

The legislation also prohibits providing, collecting or making available funds and economic resources with knowledge that they will be used to finance the group. Violations are punishable by death or imprisonment for 15 to 25 years.

Criminalized activities also include supplying or smuggling weapons, military equipment and dual-use materials, facilitating access to such items, and providing logistical support or intelligence. These offenses can carry the death penalty.

In relation to recruitment, the law criminalizes recruiting, training, arming and enrolling individuals in Houthi military and security formations, prescribing the death penalty.

It provides for particularly severe treatment of cases involving child recruitment, coercion, threats or deception, as well as the exploitation of schools, educational and religious institutions, summer centers and care facilities for recruitment and military or security training.

The legislation includes specific protections for children, defining a child as anyone under the age of 18.

It provides safeguards against their recruitment, training, arming or use in military and security activities, while prioritizing the rehabilitation and reintegration of children who have been exploited and ensuring they are not held to the same standards of criminal responsibility as adults.

Cutting Off Funding and Reversing Confiscations

Disrupting the group's sources of financing is a central pillar of the legislation, which goes beyond criminalizing financial support to target entities established or reconstituted to represent the Houthis or provide legal, political, financial or media cover for the continuation of their organizational activities.

The law also criminalizes providing premises, facilities, equipment and services to the group and its affiliates.

It prohibits circumventing asset seizure and freezing orders by transferring, selling or concealing assets, changing their ownership or allowing third parties to benefit from them with the intention of obstructing enforcement.

To implement these measures, the legislation provides for the establishment of a permanent technical unit within the Office of the Prosecutor General to oversee the terrorist designation and related lists.

The unit will include representatives from the Public Prosecution, the ministries of Justice, Interior, Foreign Affairs, Finance, and Industry and Trade, the Central Bank of Yemen, the Central State Security Apparatus and the Financial Intelligence Unit.

Its responsibilities will include gathering information, verifying sources, examining organizational ties and command-and-control relationships, preparing files on individuals and entities proposed for terrorist listing, and submitting recommendations to the Prosecutor General.

The Prosecutor General will issue reasoned listing decisions after reviewing the files, while the relevant authorities will implement financial measures, including freezing funds and assets proven to be linked to designated individuals and entities.

These measures cover assets held directly or indirectly or controlled by the beneficial owner, while safeguarding the rights of third parties acting in good faith.

The legislation draws a clear distinction between freezing and confiscation. Permanent confiscation requires a final court ruling, and the inclusion of an individual or entity on a terrorist list does not, by itself, result in the confiscation of their assets.

At the same time, the law invalidates the legal, financial and administrative effects of rulings issued by the Houthis against state leaders, political parties, opposition figures, activists, journalists and human rights advocates, including the confiscation of their funds and property.

The provisions also cover amendments the group has introduced to laws, educational curricula and institutions, as well as confiscation orders issued under the authority of the so-called "judicial custodian."

The law requires the return of funds, property and rights to the state or their rightful owners where ownership is established, while allowing claims for compensation before the competent courts.

Protecting Trade and Humanitarian Aid

In a country where millions of people depend on the movement of goods and humanitarian assistance, the legislation dedicates a separate chapter to protecting economic activity and humanitarian operations.

It establishes restrictions on the application of measures that could harm civilians or disrupt access to essential supplies.

The law states that engaging in legitimate commercial, industrial, agricultural or service activities, including transporting food, medicine and fuel, does not in itself constitute a crime or evidence of financing or cooperating with the Houthis, even when such activities take place in areas under the group's control.

It requires the government, central bank and relevant authorities to take the necessary measures to ensure the continued flow of essential goods, facilitate humanitarian assistance and prevent legal measures from harming civilians or legitimate economic activities.

The legislation also exempts neutral humanitarian, medical and relief operations conducted by the United Nations and its agencies, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and licensed international and local organizations.

It emphasizes that providing food, medical treatment or humanitarian assistance to people in need does not constitute financing the group merely because the recipients reside in Houthi-controlled areas.

However, these exemptions do not provide immunity for activities used as a cover to finance the group or supply it with prohibited support. Criminal liability remains applicable where the elements of an offense are established.

International Prosecution

The legislation also expands the scope of cooperation with judicial, security and financial authorities outside Yemen.

It directs the Public Prosecution and relevant agencies, in coordination with the ministries of Foreign Affairs and Interior, to pursue legal action against suspects and convicted individuals residing abroad.

This includes requesting their arrest and extradition and seeking enforcement of relevant judicial rulings and orders.

International cooperation will encompass the exchange of information and evidence, requests for legal and judicial assistance, and coordination with the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol), foreign law enforcement agencies and judicial authorities.

It also provides for requests to trace, seize, freeze, confiscate or recover funds and assets located outside Yemen in accordance with applicable legal procedures.

The law further requires the government to activate the Arab Convention on the Suppression of Terrorism and relevant international treaties to cut off the group's sources of financing and prevent it from obtaining weapons.

On the political front, the legislation stipulates that no future political settlement may grant criminal immunity to Houthi leaders or members implicated in crimes and serious violations.

However, it explicitly excludes authorized official negotiations and communications conducted for the purposes of peace, ceasefires, prisoner exchanges and addressing humanitarian issues from criminalization.

World.title: Tunisia’s olive oil export revenues hit record 5.2 billion dinars
World.content:
TUNIS: Tunisia’s olive oil export revenues jumped 39 percent to a record 5.2 billion dinars ($1.71 billion) in the 2025-2026 season, from the year before, providing a much-needed boost to the ailing economy as Tunisia grapples with persistent financial pressures.

Olive oil export volumes rose also 47.5 percent to around 413,100 metric tons, the National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI) said on Wednesday.

Tunisia benefited from a record olive oil harvest of around 500,000 tons in the 2025-2026 season, making it the world’s second-largest olive oil producer after Spain.

The bumper crop helped drive export growth and strengthened the country’s position in global markets.

Olive oil is Tunisia’s leading agricultural export and a major source of foreign currency.

The European Union remains its biggest export destination, while North America has also emerged as an important market. Tunisian olive oil reached 85 countries during the first 11 months of the season, reflecting strong international demand, officials said.

Around 84.3 percent of Tunisia’s olive oil exports were shipped in bulk during the 2025-2026 season, while bottled and packaged oil accounted for just 15.7 percent of volumes, highlighting the country’s struggle to capture more value from its production and build stronger international brands.

The export windfall comes as Tunisia faces high public debt, weak economic growth and limited access to international financing.

World.title: Pochettino arrives in Manchester braced for relegation cauldron
World.content:
MANCHESTER: Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United on Wednesday morning, after an overnight flight took their new manager from his final match in charge of the US team into a relegation battle at a club desperately seeking a revival in fortunes.

Pochettino posted a photo of Manchester from the air on Instagram, signalling the end of his seven-hour journey from Cincinnati.

He's here. Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino! 🤝🇾🇪 https://t.co/MOhRCv79hq — Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 18, 2026

A private plane had whisked him away shortly after the US beat Haiti on Tuesday, and the 54-year-old Argentine was driven straight to United’s training center at Carrington.



Pochettino ⁠has precious little ⁠time to settle into his new surroundings, however, with an away Premier League game at arch-rivals Liverpool looming large on Sunday.

United announced Pochettino’s appointment on Friday, following Michael Carrick’s sacking, with the manager delaying his arrival to lead the US in their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

👀🔜 https://t.co/RdypQaktVN — Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 18, 2026

His focus must swiftly switch from international football to the daily grind of club management, ⁠where a harsh spotlight will follow his every move and a drastic change in form is needed, and quickly.

United have not won the league title since 2013, when long-serving manager Alex Ferguson retired, and the 20-times English champions have registered one win in 10 league games this season to lie 18th in the table, their lowest position at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87.

That was the season Ferguson took charge, and 40 years later Pochettino arrives in similar circumstances.



FERGIE TIME

Ferguson was given time at United, whose wait for another league title had reached almost two ⁠decades upon ⁠his arrival. Two days after taking charge, Ferguson’s side lost at Oxford United and dropped into the relegation zone.

Manchester United finished 11th that season, and had to wait until 1993 for Ferguson to deliver the title, although he did win a European Cup Winners’ Cup, FA Cup and League Cup along the way.

Day one 📍 Let's get going 👊 — Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 18, 2026

Pochettino, whose only league title as a manager came at Paris St. Germain, is unlikely to be afforded such patience.

US midfielder DaMarcus Beasley, who spent a season on-loan at Manchester City, joked with Pochettino in a post-game interview on TNT Sports on Tuesday that “Manchester will always be blue.”

“No way, you will see,” Pochettino replied.

“Give me time, give me time and that is going to start to change, for sure.”

World.title: Russia flight lands in Turkiye after bomb threat hoax: reports
World.content:
ANTALYA: A Russian passenger plane received a bomb threat while flying to southern Turkiye on Wednesday but landed there without incident with passengers and crew evacuated, Turkish news agencies reported.

The Sukhoi Superjet 100 operated by Azimuth Airlines was flying from Mineralnye Vody in southern Russia to Antalya where the COP31 UN climate summit is taking place.

A new bomb threat against an aeroplane – this time targeting an Azimuth Airlines flight from Russia to Antalya, in southern Turkey – has turned out to be a hoax. The Turkish authorities found no explosives after evacuating the 65 passengers. https://t.co/zlNZvCfFwu — 🇹🇷 🇬🇧 Turkey Türkiye (@hispanatoliaEN) November 18, 2026

After receiving the threat, the plane landed at Antalya airport, was taken to a secure area and all the 65 passengers and four crew were evacuated, DHA and IHA news agencies reported.

Nothing suspicious was found, IHA said.

Earlier this month, a spate of bogus bomb threats targeted dozens of commercial flights across Europe, prompting several countries to open investigations to the hoaxers. Ireland said it suspected a “co-ordinated campaign of disruption” though noone has yet been identified.

World.title: Saudi food security conference targets real-world projects within a year
World.content:
AL-AHSA: Turning food-security research into projects with measurable results within a year is among the ambitions of an international conference that brought researchers, policymakers and industry leaders to Al-Ahsa this week.

The third International Conference on Food Security and Environmental Sustainability was hosted by King Faisal University from Nov. 16-18 under the patronage of Eastern Province Gov. Prince Saud bin Naif.

The three-day event focused on artificial intelligence in food security, environmental sustainability and carbon capture, with discussions ranging from precision agriculture and robotics to smart supply chains, ethical data governance and investment in the Saudi date industry.

But Ahmed Saud Al-Saqufi, dean of the university’s College of Agricultural and Food Sciences and chairman of the conference’s scientific committee, said its real measure of success would come afterwards.

Ahmed Saud Al-Saqufi, dean of King Faisal University’s College of Agricultural and Food Sciences and chairman of the conference’s scientific committee. (Supplied)

“We expect the most important outcome of the conference to be the launch of a national applied initiative for food security and environmental sustainability, moving from research findings and scientific recommendations to projects that can be implemented and measured,” he told Arab News.

The conference included two opening sessions, 14 scientific sessions, eight workshops, a companion exhibition and a hackathon. It brought together 66 speakers and experts, including 14 international speakers, alongside 82 accepted scientific abstracts and 22 session moderators.

Contributors included the UN Food and Agriculture Organization, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology, France’s INRAE, the University of Roehampton and the University of Messina, as well as Saudi government bodies and national companies.

Artificial intelligence featured throughout the program, with applications ranging from climate-resilient agriculture and food processing to predictive logistics and environmental monitoring.

Al-Saqufi said precision agriculture and AI-based irrigation management were among the applications most ready for wider adoption in Saudi Arabia.

Speakers participate in an opening session on achieving a carbon-neutral, food-secure future at third International Conference on Food Security and Environmental Sustainability in Al-Ahsa. (AN photo by Waad Hussain)

“With limited water resources and rising production costs, there is a real need to move from traditional agricultural practices toward agriculture based on data and intelligent decision-making,” he said. “We do not need to wait for the technologies of the future. We need to use the technologies available today, adapt them to our climatic and agricultural conditions, and turn them into economic solutions that benefit Saudi farmers.”

“The real success of artificial intelligence in agriculture is not in the number of robots we use, but in the amount of water we save, the production we increase and the costs we reduce.”

Al-Saqufi said universities needed stronger links with government institutions and industry to put research into practice: “The real challenge is not producing knowledge or drafting recommendations, but having an institutional mechanism that ensures this knowledge moves from the university to the beneficiaries and is transformed into decisions and projects on the ground.”

He added that conference recommendations should be translated into defined initiatives rather than broad statements, with each linked to clear objectives, performance indicators and an implementation timeframe. Priority research should also be connected to funding programs and pilot projects so that solutions can be tested and their feasibility assessed before wider deployment.

That emphasis on application is particularly relevant in Al-Ahsa, which the conference presents as a potential national testing ground for sustainable agriculture. The oasis combines a long agricultural history with conditions that pose practical challenges for farming, including high temperatures, limited water resources, soil salinity and intensive agricultural production.

Delegates gather at King Faisal University for the third International Conference on Food Security and Environmental Sustainability, bringing together experts from Saudi Arabia and abroad. (AN photo by Waad Hussain)

“We believe Al-Ahsa has a major opportunity to become a national laboratory for sustainable agriculture,” Al-Saqufi said, adding that King Faisal University could help test agricultural solutions and train Saudi specialists to apply them.

“Our ambition is for Al-Ahsa to become a source of sustainable agricultural solutions, not only a food-producing region, and for its experience to be transferred to different parts of the Kingdom,” he said.

The program reflected the conference’s broad approach to technology and sustainability. Workshops also examined the use of AI in nutrition, food quality and public health, as well as digital sustainability and its integration with Vision 2030.

The conference's final day focused partly on investment opportunities in Saudi Arabia's date industry, with discussions covering global competition, manufacturing innovation, financing and supply-chain development.

For Al-Saqufi, linking research with investment, government institutions and the private sector will determine whether the work presented during the conference moves beyond the university.

“We want, after a year, to be able to point to a tangible result, not simply recommendations or scientific papers published after the conference,” he said.

“We want to say that ICFSES 2026 succeeded in turning scientific knowledge into three leading applied projects in food security and environmental sustainability that started in Al-Ahsa and began implementation through partnerships between King Faisal University, government entities and the private sector.”

World.title: Zelensky hopes for ‘swift’ EU approval of Ukraine loan
World.content: What President Ursula @vonderleyen and I discussed earlier could become a reality and GREATLY help Ukraine, our resilience, and our diplomacy. I thank her and the @EU_Commission for the proposal to establish the Instrument for Coordinated Support to Ukraine, under which the EU would provide up to €45 billion in financial assistance to Ukraine. This will complement the EU's existing commitments under the Ukraine Support Loan and will cover a significant part of the budget and defense needs for next year, 2027. We very much hope for the swift adoption of this decision by the European Parliament and the Council and count on the support of all EU member states. I also thank Ursula for her initiative to bring in assistance from our other partners through new mechanisms to facilitate and coordinate additional support. Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end.

World.title: Xi, Trump, Putin exchange greetings before historic China summit
World.content:
SHENZHEN, China: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.

The agenda for Thursday’s meeting between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin — which has raised fears of a carve-up into new “spheres of influence” — was unclear, however.

When Trump touched down in Shenzhen, Xi became the first Chinese paramount leader in decades to welcome a foreign leader as he arrived, mirroring the US president’s gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September.

Trump descended the stairs from his plane to be met by Xi, as well as renditions of both countries’ national anthems and fighter jets that flew overhead and left colorful vapor trails.

The pair strolled down a red carpet lined with people waving pom-poms, brandishing Chinese and US national flags, and shouting: “A warm welcome to you!“

A motorcade of dark limousines later carried Trump into the city, where the streets had been cleared of traffic, an AFP reporter observed.

Xi, Trump, Putin and other leaders attending the broader Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit then gathered for a welcome dinner, and the three briefly exchanged greetings before a group photo.

“I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations,” Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

Sanctions ‘failed’: Putin

Washington had signaled that the Ukraine war — something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem — was not expected to be addressed in the trilateral meeting, before Trump said that it would.

The summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

Earlier on Wednesday, Putin struck a defiant tone on his war in Ukraine, saying Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion had “failed.”

Addressing the APEC gathering, the Russian leader said he expected the trilateral summit to be “highly useful.”

“At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.

The Russian leader has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 offensive in Ukraine began, but has found an audience with Trump.

However, “full-scale” talks solely between Putin and Trump are unlikely to take place during their visits to China, Moscow said, according to Russian state media.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said sanctions would “continue to increase as long as this war goes on.”

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, said he hoped Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war.”

Kim incoming?

Putin and Xi met, their fifth tete-a-tete this year, including one by video link. The two men have long touted their strong personal friendship.

Xi urged yet closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties.”

Trump came to China from the Philippines, where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad — Australia, Japan and India — for the first time in his second term.

The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence.

Trump has also floated the possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un in China, saying the North Korean leader “would like” to meet, although there has been no confirmation from Pyongyang.

Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) where there were protests against a US supply chain initiative.

The specter of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large over his recent travels.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with ASEAN.

On Tuesday, a combative Trump doubled down, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earths production “within 10 months.”

World.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next US House speaker
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Democrats elected this month to the US House of Representatives nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to lead them in the next Congress, putting him on the precipice ‌of becoming the ‌nation’s first Black House speaker.

The ​incoming ‌House ⁠Democratic Caucus ​nominated Jeffries ⁠in a closed-door, secret-ballot vote.

Jeffries won 251 votes with 11 Democrats opposing him.

Many incoming progressives declined to say whether they would back Jeffries after the November 3 midterm elections, with several saying they wanted a leader who would support a bold agenda to pass populist policies ⁠that candidates campaigned on.

A group of seven ‌incoming House progressives said ‌in a joint statement that they voted ​against Jeffries because they’re ‌still working to secure commitments from the New York ‌Democrat.

“While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding ‌of leadership,” they said. “Those conversations are ongoing.”

Despite some opposition, Jeffries is expected to be elected speaker, ⁠a ⁠powerful position that puts him second in line to the presidency, when the new Congress convenes in early January. The speaker election requires 218 votes on the House floor. Democrats will have a majority of at least 257 seats. Several competitive races remain uncalled.

House Republicans last week nominated Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan to lead their conference in January. Jordan won the post over Majority Leader Steve Scalize after Speaker Mike Johnson said ​he would not seek ​to lead Republicans in the minority.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Iraq aims to raise non-oil revenues to 19% in 2027 budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s draft 2027 federal budget aims to raise non-oil revenues to at least 19 percent of total government revenues, marking the highest proportion in the country’s history.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi government, Haider al-Aboudi, announced the target on Tuesday, noting that non-oil income had never exceeded 11 percent before 2026.

According to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the government plans to achieve this increase and insulate the economy from oil shocks through several structural changes.

Authorities are automating customs procedures at border crossings, digitizing government operations, and strengthening tax collection.

The plan relies on tightening financial oversight to cut off sources of corruption and revenue leakage.

The bill introduces elements of program and performance-based budgeting, tying public spending to measurable goals rather than strictly to payroll and operational categories.

While the ministries of finance and planning have completed the draft, the bill has not yet been formally published or approved by the Iraqi cabinet.

The Iraqi government aims to spend 217 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $166 billion) in 2027, assuming an oil price of $58 per barrel, according to parliamentarians familiar with the draft budget.

The measures would result in a fiscal deficit of around 40 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $30.6 billion).

Members of the parliamentary finance committee told Reuters that the draft budget anticipates crude oil exports of around four million barrels per day, including shipments from Iraqi Kurdistan.

Oil exports generate the majority of the Iraqi government’s revenue, accounting for roughly 80 percent of the general budget’s resources.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

World.title: Baghdad Court sentences six more French ISIS members to life in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Al-Karkh Criminal Court in Baghdad sentenced six French nationals to life imprisonment on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, for membership in the Islamic State (ISIS) terrorist organization, raising the total number of French citizens convicted in the ongoing mass transfer case to 16.

According to a statement from the Supreme Judicial Council’s Media Center, the verdicts were pronounced in the presence of the defendants’ legal counsel and diplomatic representatives from the French Embassy in Baghdad.

The court issued the rulings under Article 4 (Paragraph 1)—read in conjunction with Article 2 (Paragraphs 1 and 3)—of Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law No.13 of 2005, applying discretionary sentence mitigation pursuant to Article 132 (Paragraph 1) of the Iraqi Penal Code to commute potential capital punishments to life sentences (equivalent to 20 years under Iraqi statutory law, subject to automatic Court of Cassation review).

The six convicts belong to a group of 47 French detainees transferred into Iraqi custody from detention facilities in northeastern Syria.

Initial inquiries were conducted by the First Al-Karkh Investigation Court with evidentiary and archival verification provided by the National Center for International Judicial Cooperation, before referring the suspects for trial.

Judicial proceedings for the group began on September 20, 2026, under tight security and without media access.

Today’s rulings mark the third wave of convictions handed down by the Al-Karkh Criminal Court in this case: on October 27, 2026, the court sentenced six French nationals to life imprisonment and a seventh defendant to 15 years in prison;two days later, on October 29, it issued life sentences to three additional French suspects, bringing the cumulative tally to 16 convicted individuals following Wednesday’s verdicts.

World.title: Fourth Arab SME Summit opens in Baghdad as CBI reveals 16.3 trillion dinar financing milestone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) The fourth edition of the Arab Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Summit kicked off at the Baghdad International Fairground on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, running through November 20 under the patronage of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi and co-organized by Iraq’s Ministry of Planning and the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA).

Participating as a strategic partner and sponsor, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) established a dedicated pavilion within the summit’s accompanying exhibition alongside commercial banks, corporations, and economic institutions.

Through informational publications and technical briefings, the CBI pavilion highlighted the banking sector’s role in executing national development financing initiatives and walked attendees through the application procedures for accessing SME loans—which carry a financing ceiling of 20 million Iraqi dinars per project through participating banks.

During the exhibition, the Central Bank unveiled updated cumulative figures detailing the scope of its developmental lending programs since their inception in 2015 through the end of October 2026.

Over that 11-year span, total CBI-backed financing reached 16.3 trillion Iraqi dinars, supporting the launch and expansion of more than 10,000 projects across Iraq’s private sector.

World.title: Iran-backed militia torture Iraqi environmentalist who refuses to abandon marshes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Jassim al-Asadi, an Iraqi environmentalist, has returned to safeguarding the country’s southern marshlands after being kidnaped and tortured by an Iran-backed militia in 2023, according to a November 18 article by NPR correspondent Jane Arraf.

Al-Asadi, 69, co-founded the environmental organization Nature Iraq in 2004 and has spent decades fighting to restore the marshes, which were mainly drained under Saddam Hussein and were designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2016.

Nature Iraq is an Iraqi-registered non-governmental organization accredited to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and also Iraq’s first and only affiliate of BirdLife International, an international conservation partnership.

Speaking with NPR, al-Asadi reported that armed men kidnapped him while he was traveling from Baghdad to his village of Chibayish in February 2023.

His captors accused him of spying for Israel and using his environmental expertise to aid foreign intelligence activities.

He said he was kept for two weeks, assaulted, shocked, and brutally suffocated during questioning.

When he was asked to confess or face death, he refused and instead composed a goodbye letter to his family.

According to NPR, al-Asadi was finally released due to pressure from his Bani Asad tribe, who mobilized hundreds of armed tribesmen to demand his liberation.

He denied an offer of refuge in Europe, preferring to stay in Iraq and continue his environmental efforts.

His homecoming comes as Iraq’s marshlands begin to recover after five years of severe drought.

Recent rains have boosted water levels, enabling some displaced buffalo herders to return, but pollution, water scarcity, and diminishing fish populations remain major concerns.

Despite threats against him, Al-Asadi continues to monitor water levels, help local people, and lobby for improved environmental protection.

The NPR investigation also highlighted the dangers confronting Iraqi environmental activists, especially those working with foreign organizations in regions where Iran-backed armed groups hold significant power.

Despite his suffering, al-Asadi remains determined to preserve the marshlands and its centuries-old way of life.

Nature Iraq organization focuses on conserving and rehabilitating Iraq’s ecosystems while safeguarding the cultural traditions and heritage connected to them.

World.title: CBI rules out dropping zeros from Iraqi dinar and favors banknote redesign
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) Spokesperson Mahmoud Dagher announced on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, that dropping zeros from the Iraqi dinar requires formal parliamentary legislation to overhaul financial transactions alongside large-scale currency printing, stating that under current economic conditions, the central bank views redesigning the physical appearance of banknotes as the most practical option.

Speaking during a televised interview with journalist Lana Al-Zahawi on Al-Nahrain TV, Dagher explained that redenominating the currency goes far beyond issuing replacement banknotes.

While passing enabling legislation through the Council of Representatives is legally feasible, he emphasized that re-indexing financial obligations, corporate shares, and market valuations introduces complex structural adjustments.

Citing the Iraq Stock Exchange as a practical example, Dagher questioned how shares currently priced at a nominal value of 1 dinar would be recalibrated without a comprehensive legal and accounting framework governing equity stakes and financial contracts.

Highlighting the industrial scale required for any currency overhaul, Dagher noted that replacing 10 million circulating banknotes requires printing an equal volume of new notes—a process contracted to premier international security printers such as “Theron,” which he ranked among the top four currency printing houses globally.

He underscored that banknote production is a specialized technical operation rather than a routine commodity order.

Instead of pursuing currency redenomination at this stage, the CBI favors updating the physical design and security features of existing denominations without altering their nominal face value or purchasing power.

According to Dagher, refreshing the banknote series delivers immediate economic and security advantages: it strengthens anti-counterfeiting protections, extends the physical lifespan of circulating notes, and incentivizes the return of hoarded cash back into the formal banking system.

World.title: Nvidia says no longer shipping ‘Hopper’ AI chips to China
World.content:
San Francisco – Scandal-hit Californian chip giant Nvidia said Tuesday it has stopped shipping artificial intelligence chips from its “Hopper” series to China, as scrutiny grows over Beijing’s access to powerful US semiconductors.

Advanced Nvidia chips are the world’s top hardware for training and running AI tools — making them highly sensitive equipment in the tech race between Washington and Beijing.

Lucrative sales of Nvidia chips — and allegations they are smuggled to China through third countries — are in the spotlight after former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman whom some US officials reportedly suspect of spying for Beijing.

In the third quarter, “sales of licensed Hopper data centre products to China was $2.4 billion,” interim CEO Colette Kress told an earnings call Tuesday.

But “our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China.”

Kress did not give a reason for the decision.

Dilin Wu, a research strategist at Pepperstone, told AFP “the timing says quite a lot.”

“We don’t know exactly what prompted the decision to stop shipments, but it certainly looks like Nvidia is trying to draw a clearer line around its China business and reassure regulators that compliance comes first.”

This year, the Trump administration began allowing limited sales of the flagship “H200” chip from Nvidia’s “Hopper” series to China.

But US conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also seen as reluctant to buy H200s as its homegrown chip industry gains momentum.

Washington still bans the export of Nvidia’s even more advanced “Blackwell” and “Rubin” GPUs to China, citing security concerns as advanced AI has military applications.

Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, a former director of a Singapore-based cloud computing company, has tanked Nvidia’s market value.

Alice Huang, no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International — a company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese tech firms obtain Nvidia chips in violation of US export controls.

As the scandal deepens, the United States moved Monday to close loopholes in those restrictions.

Its new rules aim to crack down on both chip smuggling to China and the large gray market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres full of high-end Nvidia chips in Southeast Asian countries.

Chandy Ye, a dual-qualified Hong Kong solicitor and mainland China lawyer, told AFP that the practical impact of Nvidia’s decision to stop Hopper shipments to China would be limited.

“Chinese authorities have already been actively steering the domestic tech sector away from procuring H200s since January 2026, meaning the local ecosystem has long been adjusting to this decoupling,” she said.

“The far more consequential development is the sweeping new interim rule from the US Commerce Department restricting remote access to advanced computing capabilities,” which closes a “massive loophole.”

World.title: UNICEF and IAP launch ‘Child Rights Pledge Platform’ to make pediatricians voice for wellbeing of children
World.content:
New Delhi: Putting child rights at the heart of wellness, Unicef and the Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) have joined hands to encourage pediatricians to champion the cause through the âChild Rights Pledge Platformâ launched on Tuesday on the official IAP website.

âThe initiative aims to support pediatricians across India to become champions for childrenâs rights by strengthening their understanding of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) and promoting the integration of child rights principles into everyday interactions with children and their families,â IAP and Unicef said in a statement.

The partnership aims to embed child rights into daily consultations by informing, educating, and engaging pediatricians on the Convention of the Rights of Child.



Dr Neelam Mohan, president of IAP said, âFor more than 50,000 pediatricians across India, this initiative is an opportunity to reaffirm our commitment not only to childrenâs health, but also to their rights and well-being holistically.â

âWe see children at every stage of their development and can recognise when their health, nutrition, development or well-being is compromised. We can identify and respond to abuse, neglect, exploitation, discrimination and other threats to childrenâs safety.





We are trusted by families and communities, and our voices can influence attitudes, practices and behaviours,â she added.

She asserted that given that pediatricians interact with children closely and can notice their challenges, it is crucial for them to be the voice of the children to safeguard their rights. âBy taking the pledge, we commit to promoting, protecting and advancing the rights of every child through our daily interactions with children, families and communities,â she added.

The platform allows the visitor to go through a simple guide on the rights of children enabling visitors to learn about not just rights focused on survival like life, health, nutrition, clean water and healthy environment but also on rights linked to development, protection, participation and non-discrimination, access and equity.
