World.title: Hindu population growth to fall behind other religions in India, globally: Pew Study
World.content:
Hindu population in India to rise by 176m by 2070, but share to decline

India's changing religious composition

Hindu population growth

across regions

Fertility, migration and religious switching to shape Hindu population

Islam projected to overtake Christianity as world's largest religion

Also check:

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

US projected to lose Christian majority by 2065

India's Hindu population is projected to increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, but Hindus are expected to account for a slightly smaller share of the country's population as Muslims continue to have higher fertility rates, according to new projections by the Pew Research Center.Despite the projected shift, Hindus are expected to continue making up more than three-quarters of India's population by 2070.The global Hindu population is also projected to grow by 199 million over the same period, reaching nearly 1.4 billion. However, as the rest of the world's population is expected to grow at a faster pace, Hindus' share of the global population is projected to decline from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070.The projections are part of a broader Pew Research Center study examining changes in the size and composition of major religious groups between 2020 and 2070. The estimates take into account differences in fertility rates, age profiles, religious switching and international migration.Pew said that although India's overall fertility rate has declined rapidly in recent decades, Muslim women continue to have more children on average than Hindu women.Combined with the younger age profile of India's Muslim population, this fertility gap is expected to increase the Muslim share of the country's population while reducing the Hindu share.India had 1.1 billion Hindus in 2020, accounting for around 95% of the global Hindu population. Nepal, with 24 million Hindus, Bangladesh with 13 million, Pakistan with 5 million and Indonesia with 4 million made up the other countries in the top five.The rankings are expected to change by 2070, with the United States projected to have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Australia is also expected to enter the top 10, ranking ninth with around 3 million Hindus, while the United Arab Emirates is projected to drop out of the list.Pakistan's Hindu population is expected to double to 10 million by 2070, although the country is projected to retain its fourth position in the global rankings.Outside India, much of the projected growth in the Hindu population is expected to come from Pakistan and the United States. Pakistan is likely to see an increase primarily through natural population growth, with births outnumbering deaths, while immigration is expected to be the main driver of growth in the US.The Asia-Pacific region, home to 99% of the world's Hindus, is projected to account for most of the community's growth over the next five decades. Its Hindu population is expected to increase by 191 million between 2020 and 2070.Hindus are projected to make up 28% of the region's population by 2070, compared with 26% in 2020.In North America, the Hindu population is expected to more than double from 4 million in 2020 to 9 million in 2070. Their share of the region's population is projected to increase from 1% to 2%.Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean are the only regions where the Hindu population is projected to decline in absolute numbers. If current trends continue, Hindus will account for less than 0.1% of the population in each of these regions by 2070.Pew's projections identify fertility, mortality, age structure, international migration and religious switching as the key factors determining changes in the size of religious groups.The global Hindu population is expected to gain more than 200 million people through natural increase between 2020 and 2070, with nearly all of this growth projected to take place in the Asia-Pacific region.Religious switching is expected to have little impact on the overall Hindu population. Pew said this is partly because Hindus have a high retention rate, with an estimated 99% of people raised Hindu continuing to identify with the religion as adults.The corresponding retention rates are 85% among Christians and 83% among Buddhists. Muslims have a retention rate of 99%, on a par with Hindus.Overall, religious switching is projected to reduce the global Hindu population by around 1 million people between 2020 and 2070, with most of the losses expected in the Asia-Pacific region.Migration, meanwhile, is expected to contribute significantly to Hindu population growth in North America, the Middle East-North Africa region and Europe. Together, these regions are projected to gain more than 8 million Hindus through migration by 2070.Asia and the Pacific is expected to record the largest migration-related losses. However, the region's gains through natural population growth are projected to far exceed the number of Hindus it loses through emigration.The Pew report also projects that Islam will overtake Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, as the Muslim population continues to grow at a faster pace.Both religions are expanding globally, but Pew attributed the faster growth of Islam largely to higher fertility rates among Muslims.âIt's the babies,â said Conrad Hackett, a senior demographer at Pew, explaining that fertility rates play a much greater role in religious population growth than conversion and other forms of religious switching.During 2020-2025, the fertility rate among Muslim women stood at 3.1 children per woman, compared with 2.5 among Christian women. The average for women belonging to all other religious groups was 1.6, below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman needed for each generation to replace itself.According to Pew's latest estimates, there were 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims worldwide in 2020. The new projections indicate that the Muslim population will reach 2.57 billion by 2035, overtaking the Christian population, which is expected to stand at 2.52 billion.If current trends continue, the number of Muslims worldwide will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the Christian population is projected to remain just below 3 billion.The projections also point to significant changes in the religious composition of North America.The United States, where Christians currently account for 62% of the population, is projected to lose its Christian majority by 2065. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to make up 41% of the US population.In neighbouring Canada, Christians are projected to account for less than half of the population by 2030. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to outnumber Christians in the country.The rise in the number of people identifying with no religion is a significant factor behind the projected decline in the Christian share of the population in both countries.

World.title: Gujarat farmers seek next-gen GM crops, call for science-led policy on farm technology
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Farmers on Wednesday sought access to the next generation of genetically modified crops and urged science-led decisions on farm technology during a media workshop organised by the National Farmers Empowerment Initiative in Ahmedabad.

Farmers said India could not continue relying on two-decade-old cotton technology as new pests, erratic weather and rising cultivation costs demanded improved crop traits.

"Bt cotton made a difference to cotton cultivation in India. Today, farmers face new pests, unpredictable weather and rising costs. We need access to improved technologies and better crop traits," said Prakash Punambhai Patel, a farmer from Simri village.



According to ministry of agriculture data, India's cotton yield increased from 186 kg per hectare in 2001-02 to 510 kg in 2013-14. However, Bt cotton remains India's only commercially approved GM crop, with Bollgard II, introduced in 2006, still the latest technology available to farmers.

Dr Vijay Kumar, former research scientist and head of cotton at Navsari Agricultural University, said agricultural technologies should be assessed responsibly and deployed to meet the needs of Indian farmers.





Participants also highlighted the potential of genome editing, alongside GM technology, to develop crops that are more productive, climate-resilient and nutritious. India released two genome-edited rice varieties in 2025.

"Farmers will adopt technologies that improve productivity and protect crops if they receive the right information and guidance. Agricultural policies must keep pace with science," said Mukesh Kantilal Patel, a farmer from Chanasma in Patan district.

World.title: Before the first bullet: Army rescued 27 from seminary, then hunted LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Security forces evacuated 27 people from Darul Uloom, an educational institution next to the mosque where top

Mohammad Lateef Bhat was holed up. The evacuation took place before security forces launched an encounter against Lateef in Zangalpora village of Jammu and Kashmirâs Kulgam district on Wednesday.

According to officials, an officer from the Army's 9 Rashtriya Rifles volunteered to enter the adjoining seminary along with his buddy and safely evacuate 25 girl students and two teachers.

Once the civilians were moved to a safe spot, troops of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles and the Special Operations Group of the Jammu and Kashmir Police launched the final assault and fired tear gas into the mosque to smoke out the terrorist.



Officials asserted that the troops maintained a tight cordon to prevent his escape and exercised maximum restraint to ensure that the religious structure suffered no damage.

Northern Army Commander Lt Gen Pratik Sharma, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, met troops in South Kashmir after the successful conclusion of the operation.

How security forces tracked down Lateef Bhat

According to officials, a search party accompanied by local civilians entered the mosque following specific intelligence inputs.





They found a room on the top floor locked from the inside.

When security personnel asked the occupant to come out, he opened fire, confirming that Bhat was inside. The Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist carried a cash reward of Rs 15 lakh on his head.

Senior Army officers in South Kashmir were determined not to let Bhat escape the cordon this time. He had earlier managed to flee during an encounter in Shopian on July 8, in which another terrorist, Zakir, was killed.

The operation followed a November 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam by Bhat and his associate Umar Nasir Dar, which left three personnel injured. Security forces subsequently launched extensive cordon and search operations across Kulgam and neighbouring Shopian and Anantnag districts.

Around 2,000 personnel from the Army, Special Operations Group (SOG) and CRPF were deployed for grid-based searches, backed by a Mobile Bunker Command Post (MBCP).

"Since November 11, cordon and search operations have been underway. In certain areas, it took us nearly three days to complete the searches due to high population density," a senior officer said.

He added that although the operations may have caused some inconvenience to residents, there had been no complaints of excesses by security personnel.

Bhat, who was in his early 20s, had passed school and previously worked as a carpenter.

He went missing in November 2025 before joining LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF).

According to security agencies, he was the prime suspect in several terror incidents in South Kashmir, including the killing of India Reserve Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi in Anantnag on July 22 and the targeted killing of two non-local labourers from Chhattisgarh in Kulgam on July 31.

Kulgam encounter: Lashkar commander Lateef Bhat killed, troops celebrate

Security forces killed Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohd Lateef Bhat in an encounter in Zangalpora village of Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district. Videos showed Army personnel celebrating the operation, with troops heard shouting "Lateef killed" as they returned from the encounter site.

Bhat was trapped inside a mosque and refused repeated appeals to surrender, but security forces ensured that the religious structure was not damaged during the operation.

The encounter followed an attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam that injured three personnel.

Trump reacts as Marcos sends Jollibee fried chicken as late-night snack in Manila

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr arranged a late-night delivery of fried chicken from homegrown fast-food chain Jollibee for US President Donald Trump and his delegation during their stay in Manila.

Describing it as a "taste of Manila", Marcos said he wanted Trump to sample one of the Philippines' most popular food brands. He also claimed that Jollibee had surpassed KFC in popularity in the US, prompting Trump to respond, "Oh wow, fantastic.

Bangladesh on alert as violence erupts ahead of Hasina's return

Bangladesh deployed hundreds of paramilitary personnel and tightened security across the country following a series of bomb blasts, arson attacks and clashes linked to protests over former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's proposed return from exile in December.

Police reported dozens of crude bomb explosions and vehicles being set on fire across at least 28 districts over the past 10 days. A petrol bomb attack killed a political activist in Hasina's hometown of Gopalganj, while a bus helper was burnt to death after two buses were set ablaze in Pirojpur.

Police also reported attacks on Grameen Bank branches and properties linked to the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party. Hasina, who has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024, has sought a new passport and identity card to facilitate her return. The interim government has accused Awami League leaders abroad of instigating violence and vowed action against those responsible.

World.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
World.content:
The body overseeing U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza ‌war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving ​the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse.

The 12-page Board ⁠of Peace report, seen by Reuters, is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the U.S.-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then.

The Board, established and headed by Mr. Trump, is expected ‌to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November.

"The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains ‌the principal risk to the process," the report said, warning that "a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be ‌sustained ⁠indefinitely."

Peace plan stalled

While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year.

Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected ​the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas ‌is dismantled.

Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops.

"Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said.

"Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not ‌been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble."

Senior Hamas ​official Basem Naim dismissed the report as "pure disinformation", accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to ⁠continue its aggression in Gaza.

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and a spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Israeli absence of decisions

Gaza's population of more than 2 million Palestinians lives confined to around a third of ‌the coastal territory, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings, under the control of Hamas fighters. Israel occupies two-thirds of Gaza that has been largely razed and depopulated.

The report criticised Israel's government for an "absence of decisions" on arrangements to train and deploy a civilian Palestinian police force to replace Hamas as Gaza's law enforcement authority. It said this was impeding the full implementation of the plan.

It said restrictions imposed by Israel on supplies and equipment, alongside funding shortfalls, had hindered the ability of Gazans to prepare for and respond to seasonal flooding. Heavy rain inundated displacement camps last week across Gaza and more ‌rain is expected later this month.

Hamas, for its part, was collecting taxes on goods entering Gaza that were impacting the availability of ​basic commodities, the report said.

The Board of Peace was established by Mr. Trump to oversee his ambitious plan to end the war that Israel launched in response to Hamas-led attacks from Gaza in October ⁠2023.

Around 1,200 people were killed in Israel in the 2023 Hamas attacks, while the Israeli assault on Gaza has since ⁠killed 74,000 Palestinians. More than 1,600 Palestinians, including many civilians, and five Israeli soldiers have been killed in Gaza since the U.S.-mediated ceasefire was struck in October 2025.

Mr. Trump's plan received strong international backing, though the Board itself ‌has been met with scepticism from many of Washington's Western allies.

Mr. Netanyahu's right-wing coalition government remains in power in Israel in a caretaker capacity despite losing its majority in an inconclusive election last month. On Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Defence Minister Israel ​Katz said Israel would not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas was dismantled and Gaza was demilitarised.

World.title: Pioneering musician and journalist Sakuntala Narasimhan passes away
World.content:
Sakuntala Narasimhan, a trailblazing musician, journalist, feminist and consumer rights activist, passed away on November 18. She was 86.

A multifaceted personality, she had the rare distinction of being a vocalist in both Carnatic and Hindustani traditions, apart from being a journalist with two PhDs in Women’s Studies and Musicology.

A setback to reinvention

When her first-born was only a year or two, she mysteriously lost her voice. She could barely speak, let alone sing. The doctors failed to identify the cause. For Sakuntala, an accomplished vocalist, being confined to home with a young child and unable to sing was deeply frustrating.

It was this setback that led her to take up writing, recalls her daughter, Shobhana Narasimhan, professor at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research.

“A women’s magazine held a short story competition, which she won. She then got to know the people at the magazine and gradually started writing more and more,” her daughter recollected. She was a longstanding columnist for multiple newspapers.

Two PhDs

“When she got married, she was pursuing a PhD in economics. However, she couldn’t complete it because I was born a year later. It always bothered her that she didn’t have a PhD,” says Ms. Shobhana, a physicist.

“When I got my PhD in 1991, I told her, “Amma, now it’s your turn.” She went ahead and got her first PhD in women’s studies and then another in musicology.”

A passionate musician

Renowned musician Archana Udupa, one of her students, remembers her as a genius who could do self jugalbandi, switching back and forth between Hindustani and Carnatic styles. She however, feels her teacher didn’t get the dues she deserved.

“She was the only A-top artist — A Top is more than A grade — in both All India Radio and Doordarshan, and both in Carnatic and Hindustani. I think our industry could have celebrated her even more. She got her State award when she was nearing 80. We need to celebrate such people at the right time and before it is too late.”

A public intellectual

Nupur Basu, journalist and documentary filmmaker, who had known Sakuntala for around four decades, said, “Her passion in life was music. But she cared about everything. Women columnists were rare those days. I would call her a public intellectual.”

“From a very young age, I was brought up to believe that there was nothing I couldn’t do simply because of my gender. She also taught me that if there is injustice, you must fight it and not keep quiet,” her daughter said.

Passionate about life, Sakuntala continued to write and sing until age began to catch up with her and take a toll on her health. She fell seriously ill in the last month and was diagnosed with cancer, which progressed rapidly.

World.title: Studies show trust in NDA government declining gradually, says Malcolm Adiseshiah awardee
World.content:
Recent economic studies in India point towards a gradual decline in trust on the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government, according to Raghav Gaiha, research affiliate, Population Aging Research Centre, University of Pennsylvania, and former professor of public policy, Delhi University.

Delivering the Malcolm Adiseshiah Memorial Lecture on the topic ‘Subjective Well-Being, Trust, and Democracy in India’ at the Asian College of Journalism (ACJ) on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Gaiha pointed out that erosion of public trust eroded the well-being of the people, threatening the very foundations of democracy. “Unless checked, continued erosion of trust, accumulated loss of well-being, and the brewing economic crisis together threaten to undermine the foundations of democracy,” he said.

Quoting political scientist P.K. Blind, he said trust in government represented confidence of citizens in the actions of a “government to do what was right and perceived fair”. Life evaluation, a measure of several components of well-being, including economic status, health, sense of security, family circumstances, and human and political rights, has perceptively deteriorated among people, he said quoting studies. Discrimination and violence against minorities, misleading claims of GDP growth in recent years, food price inflation and high unemployment, crackdown on the media, and denial of justice to certain sections have all contributed to the lowering of the subjective well-being, he added.

Delivering the Elizabeth Adiseshiah Memorial Lecture on the topic ‘Women and Work: The Missing Engine of India’s Development’, Kanika Mahajan, associate professor, Ashoka University, said India’s female labour force participation rate for women above 15 years stood at 32.8% in 2024 against a world average of 51% across 176 countries. “India sits among the lowest-ranked economies in the world on this measure, rivalled only by a few economies in West Asia and North Africa,” she added. While constraints at home, such as childcare, eldercare, safe transport, and availability of piped water, dictate women’s participation in economic activity, demand side constraints, such as quality of job creation for women, contribute to their participation as well, she said.

Mr. Gaiha was awarded the Malcolm Adiseshiah Award for his contribution to development studies and Ms. Mahajan was awarded the Elizabeth Adiseshiah Award.

C. Selvaraj, Chairman, Malcolm and Elizabeth Adiseshiah Trust, said the lectures pointed towards the multiplicity of quantifiable institutional factors that do not get into the reckoning of the quantitative economic reasoning, and those which economic models and quantitative measurements studiously avoid, he added.

Sashi Kumar, Chairman, ACJ, and A.R. Venkatachalapathy, professor, Madras Institute of Development Studies, also spoke.

World.title: EPFO tells trustees there’s no legal route to recover ₹1,800 crore from Reliance Capital
World.content:
The alleged siphoning of the remaining ₹1,800 crore of salaried workers’ money that Reliance Capital Ltd (RCL) has defaulted on paying to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is part of the agenda of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) meeting, scheduled to be held here on Thursday (November 19, 2026). According to the agenda note, seen by The Hindu, the EPFO may not be able to claim any more of the principal amount or interest under any legal route.

Among the issues to be discussed in the meeting are the status of the outstanding default on the retirement fund’s holdings and the annual performance of its portfolio managers. CBT members will also discuss the material shared by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on alleged fraudulent transactions, diversion of funds, irregular lending, and other alleged irregularities by the RCL.

The EPFO invested ₹2,500 crore of workers’ money with the RCL in 2013 and 2014, and the latter defaulted on it and is alleged to have impaired the security available to debenture holders, including the EPFO. The EPFO’s admitted claim from the RCL was ₹3,308.67 crore, out of which ₹2,500 crore was the principal amount invested. The investment was scheduled to mature in 2023 and 2024.

The custodian of the RCL, Standard Chartered Bank, has reported the receipt of ₹1,492.45 crore, i.e., 59.70% of the principal amount. “Total amount invested but not received as on 19.03.2025 is ₹1,007.55 crore, and the amount of interest admitted in Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) but not received is ₹808.67 crore,” the agenda note for Thursday’s meeting said.

The agenda note, citing the legal opinion of EPFO’s lawyer, added that no further legal remedy exists for additional recovery in view of binding Supreme Court judgments, the resolution plan approved by the National Company Law Tribunal, and the full-and-final settlement nature of distributions received. “The EPFO may not be able to claim further principal or interest under any legal route,” the agenda note adds.

A spokesperson for businessman Anil Ambani had earlier said that Mr. Ambani served as a non-executive director/chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 to November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the board of directors of the company and appointed an administrator. “Mr. Ambani has denied any wrongdoing whatsoever and reserves all rights available to him in law,” the spokesperson had said.

Further steps

The EPFO has told its trustees that the Central Bureau of Investigation has registered a case into the matter. The organisation has written to the ED on the issue and asked the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to refer the matter to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO).

“Considering the nature of the allegations and the financial loss suffered by EPFO, legal consultation was sought on the matter. Based on the legal opinion received, a reference was made to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for registration of FIR, investigation into the alleged fraudulent transactions, and for such appropriate action in accordance with the law,” says the agenda note circulated among members.

The meeting will also discuss the status of other defaulters, including the Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation (outstanding interest of about ₹85 crore), Richardson & Cruddas (a penal interest of about ₹5.36 crore), Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services Limited (a claim of ₹601.54 crore), and the Punjab State Industrial Development Corporation (₹1.10 crore interest in default).

The meeting will also review the performance of portfolio managers such as the UTI Asset Management Company Ltd, SBI Fund Management Ltd, and four asset management companies for Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) investments — UTI Asset Management Company Limited, SBI Funds Management Limited, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited, and Nippon India Life AMC. The evaluation report is prepared by M/s. CRISIL.

World.title: SSR special camps to be held at 660 polling station locations in Kanniyakumari
World.content:
Special camps for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls-2027 will be conducted for three days at 660 polling station locations across Kanniyakumari district.

The special camps will be held on Saturday (November 21), Sunday (November 22) and Sunday (November 29).

On the day of special camps, Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will be available at their polling stations from 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. to receive applications from eligible members of the public and provide necessary guidance. The applications received at the camps include Form 6, Form 6A, Form 7 and Form 8 and all these applications would be available at the respective polling booths.

Through this camp, youngsters attaining 18 years of age on January 1, 2027 and other eligible persons whose names have not yet been included in the electoral roll may apply using Form 6. Those who will attain 18 years of age on the dates April 1, 2027, July 1, 2027 and October 1, 2027 may also submit their applications in advance.

The district administration has said that at the above special camps members of the public may also verify whether their names are included in the electoral rolls and submit appropriate applications for inclusion, deletion, correction of particulars or shifting of residence.

Kanniyakumari Collector M. Prathap has appealed to all eligible members of the public to make use of the SSR camps, which would be held on November 21, 22 and 29 in the district.

World.title: SCoR plans 1,560 special train trips for Godavari Pushkarams
World.content:
RAJAMAHENDRAVARAM

The South Coast Railway (SCoR) authorities announced their action plan to transport the nearly 11 lakh devotees expected to travel by train for the Godavari Pushkarams-2027, with around nine lakh devotees likely to arrive at Rajamahendravaram railway station alone during the 12-day event.

As part of the transportation plan the railway authorities are preparing to operate 1,560 special train trips during the 12-day event.

The SCoR authorities have shared their action plan with Godavari Pushkarams-2027 special officer S. Suresh Kumar at a meeting on transportation facilities on Wednesday.

Inspection: Special Officer andSecretary to Municipal Administration and Urban Development S. Suresh Kumar on Wednesday advised the officials to finalise designated locations for pujas, and reviewed the action plans for security and transportation for the Godavari Puskharams-2027 in Rajamahendravaram city.

Mr. Suresh Kumar inspected the areas at Katheru, Jalaaripeta, which have been designated for vehicle parking, and enquired about connectivity to the ghats along the banks of the river Godavari.

In Rajamahendravaram city, he also inspected the proposed entry and exit points from the ghats, deployment of security personnel, swimmers and special centres to trace the missing devotees.

He was told that local swimmers and traditional boats would be deployed for rescue operations along the ghats. Mr. Suresh Kumar has directed Rajamahendravaram Municipal Corporation Commissioner Rahul Meena to finalise the spots where the devotees would be allowed to take a holy dip, both for VVIPs and other devotees.

Accompanied by Mr. Meena and Joint Collector Y. Megha Swaroop, Mr. Suresh Kumar inspected the ongoing works of Akhanda Godavari project works at Pushkar Ghat.

At the Godavari railway station adjacent to the Pushkar Ghat, which is the main ghat where the Godavari Pushkarams are declared open, Mr. Suresh Kumar asked officials to implement the transportation plan, to ensure better access to trains and bus services for devotees.

World.title: India imposes 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch imports amid UK trade pact dispute
World.content:
India is imposing an effective duty of 162.5% on bulk Scotch imports amid an ongoing dispute over the India-UK trade agreement, raising concerns among liquor companies as the levy exceeds the 150% charged before the agreement, according to eight sources and a government document.

The India-UK trade agreement, implemented in July, halved tariffs on Scotch to 75%. Businesses and the British government had hailed the move as a major win for companies such as Pernod Ricard and Diageo, which import Scotch in bulk and blend it to make popular products for India’s USD 65-billion liquor market.

However, in the first major dispute linked to the trade agreement, Indian investigators have argued that companies are using incorrect customs classifications for bulk Scotch concentrates, which are treated as raw materials used to make drinks such as blended whiskies.

Since May, such imports have been classified under a newly created customs category for “compound alcoholic preparations”, which attracts a 150% t tariff, according to Indian investigators. These imports are then subject to a consumption tax, taking the total duty to 162.5% , according to a government document reviewed by Reuters and eight sources, including industry executives and customs agents familiar with the matter.

As the dispute continues, thousands of litres of bulk Scotch in more than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod, Diageo and Bacardi remain stuck at ports, Reuters reported last week.

Under a provisional release arrangement pending investigation, 75% of the goods’ value must be paid upfront, with the remaining amount covered by bank guarantees, the sources said.

“Industry has already reduced prices of Scotch products in the market when the India-UK pact kicked in, and now they are faced with higher duties again,” said a source in the liquor importing business.

Pernod, which owns UK-based Chivas Brothers, Diageo and several other Indian companies believe that both bulk and bottled Scotch imports should be taxed at 75% under the trade agreement.

The British government has repeatedly said in statements that it is working with New Delhi to resolve the issue, while India has said the dispute will be settled soon.

Pernod and Diageo have moved to arrange bank guarantees and other funding to secure the release of their blocked containers and ensure business continuity. Bacardi is still deciding its next steps, three of the sources said.

Shares of Diageo in London and Pernod in France fell following the Reuters report, declining 1.5% and 1.25%, respectively. India is Pernod’s biggest global market by volume, and the company, along with Diageo, dominates the Indian spirits market.

Diageo declined to comment, while Pernod and Bacardi did not respond to queries. The Indian Finance Ministry and the tax authority also did not respond.

Businesses fear disruptions

Long-running tariff disputes have been a sore point for foreign investors and have affected companies such as Volkswagen and Samsung. Indian officials say they are only enforcing the law, but executives say they are often caught off guard by the way New Delhi classifies imports.

Mumbai-listed companies Radico Khaitan, Allied Blenders and Distillers, and Tilaknagar Industries also import bulk Scotch and are under scrutiny, along with Pernod and Diageo. Smaller companies could face greater pressure in arranging bank guarantees, as they may need to provide collateral. Such guarantees also have to be reported as contingent liabilities.

“We have no alternative at this stage,” said an Indian executive, referring to a possible disruption in the market due to a shortage of bulk Scotch. “Meeting the production requirements is extremely critical, even though bank guarantees stress working capital.”

About 80% of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk, and India is the largest market for Scotch by volume.

Most bulk Scotch imports are used to make Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) whisky by blending a small quantity of Scotch with other spirits. These mass-market products are considerably cheaper than wholly imported whiskies such as Chivas Regal and Johnnie Walker.

Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during the years of negotiations leading up to the trade agreement’s implementation on July 15. Britain has said that “iconic UK products”, including whiskies, would benefit from the pact.

The UK’s Scotch Whisky Association has forecast that the trade agreement could boost Scotch exports to India by USD 1.34 billion over five years.

A confidential memo from Indian investigators, reported by Reuters last week, said that any misclassification under the India-UK trade agreement needed to stop as it had “substantial revenue implications” for New Delhi.

Indian liquor industry sources said that while the classification issue was being debated, they had not anticipated the imposition of the additional local tax.

“The local tax addition is a googly,” one industry source said, using the cricket term for a deceptive delivery by a bowler.

World.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
World.content:
India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik.

Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said.

Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests.

Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12.

Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added.

“The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar.

“The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said.

Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.

World.title: ‘Have the courage to listen to the debate you started’: Bilawal sticks to his guns after speaking his ‘truth’
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Wednesday maintained that his recent remarks on the country’s political situation were the “truth”, urging government representatives to have the “courage” to listen to his point of view.

Speaking in an interview on Hum News programme ‘Faisla Aap Ka’, Bilawal reiterated his stance from his Tuesday’s speech, cautioning against new provinces and calling for a “political reset” so public issues could be addressed.

Bilawal emphasised that he spoke in the context of the US-Iran war, which has impacted economies around the world due to rising energy costs.

“Elites do not have the idea of what kind of difficulties Pakistanis are facing,” he said, highlighting the need for politicians to set aside their partisan political perspectives and think about how to “fix the system”.

The PPP chairman asserted it was his right to provide his perspective on what shape a “reset” should take if someone was suggesting that a reset was needed, indirectly referring to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s July remarks.

On the fact that his PPP was part of the ruling coalition, Bilawal contended that this was the exact reason to “listen” to him as he was a “major stakeholder”.

“These are not reasons to discount what I am saying […] I am telling you that this is the situation; these are my proposals to rectify it. You may disagree with my suggestions, but at least listen. You should have the courage to listen to the truth.”

The Bhutto scion added, “Because I am a stakeholder, I am saying: come to your senses.”

He further said, “Now let’s have the debate that you started. […] Have the courage to [continue] the debate that is now ongoing.”

Noting that the conversation had not been brought to the Parliament so far, Bilawal said, “You yourself decided to hold this debate in front of businessmen. It was decided on their own that this debate would be held through touts.”

The PPP chairman affirmed that Pakistan had not become so weak as a society that there would only be “one-sided debates”.

Replying to a question, he remarked that he “spoke too much yesterday, which was now hard to digest”.

Noting the ongoing “geopolitical atmosphere”, the former foreign minister wondered how many fronts the government wanted to fight on simultaneously, with India as an adversary, a near-war situation with Afghanistan and the fight against terrorism.

“The government has been deciding that we will fight the PTI; now the new decision is that they will also fight JUI, and it seems that after my truth, they have also decided they must fight me too,” Bilawal remarked.

“If you are going to fight everyone, and fight everyone internally as well, then who will lead Pakistan and its people out of this economic crisis?” he wondered.

The PPP chairman said the reactions from federal ministers to his remarks were “yet another proof that Pakistan’s politicians do not have the courage to hear the truth”.

“If you or they do not have enough courage or patience to listen to me, then what about the people of Pakistan who have no access to the prime minister, his ministers, or the National Assembly?”

Bilawal said he was unaware of “what was behind this debate because till today, despite being such a major stakeholder”, neither the prime minister nor a federal minister nor a political or any other stakeholder had discussed with him or the president that they wanted new provinces to be created.

“No attention” was being paid to the ongoing historic economic crisis, the ex-minister added.

Reiterating that he had not started the debate on governance, Bilawal quipped whether “only the PCB chairman had the right to tell how and why the system has collapsed”, referring to Naqvi, who also serves as the cricket board chief.

“If a reset has to happen, then has the PCB been given the responsibility that you have all powers to decide how the system will be reset, whether provinces should be divided? […] Should I go home quietly? This is not possible.”

Asked whether his remarks meant that PPP would take the path of resistance, Bilawal refrained from terming it that, adding that he provided his voters’ perspective and did not issue any protest call.

“I suggested to everyone that a political reset is needed, a democratic reset is needed, so that instead of politicians grabbing each other’s collars, fighting each other, we all join hands to pull the public out of this hardship,” he explained.

The PPP chairman termed the government’s reaction to criticism by Maulana Fazlur Rehman as “completely frivolous, irresponsible conduct”. “If he criticises, the reaction is to demolish the house, arrest his son and pressure his party workers,” he added.

Asked whether his warning regarding the division of Sindh was a threat, the Bhutto scion affirmed that his party was not one that engaged in violence.

He referred to Sindh’s history, particularly from 1980s onwards, adding, “Was what I said outside of a historical context or precedent? This wasn’t organic; it was orchestrated to create division in Sindh’s politics.”

He declared, “And this risk is still present today, which is why I was warning that if Sindh is divided forcefully, I would not do such things but there will be a reaction.”

Bilawal warned that while he would not want it, the law and order situation would worsen so much that it would be difficult to put out the “fire”.

More to follow

World.title: ICJ report sees 'judicial capture' in Pakistan after 26th, 27th Constitutional Amendments
World.content:
A report released by the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) on Wednesday said that the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments led to a “systemic judicial capture” in Pakistan.

The 26th Amendment , passed in October 2024, carved constitutional benches out of the Supreme Court, with their members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.

Barely a year later, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC). It also made significant changes to the judicial system, the military’s chain of command and granted immunities to government officials. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges resigned in protest the day it became law.

On Wednesday, the ICJ released a report — titled ‘Judicial Capture: Independence of the Judiciary in Pakistan after the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments’.

It said that after analysing the institutional framework governing higher courts following the two amendments, the judiciary in Pakistan no longer enjoyed institutional guarantees of independence required under international law and standards.

“The 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments were a decisive break from the model of judicial independence that Pakistan had built after the restoration of the judiciary in 2009,” the report noted.

However, it observed that the “erosion of judicial independence” was done through constitutional amendments, rather than the overt removal of judges.

The report said that while the government argued that amendments were made to “check judicial overreach, reduce the backlog of cases, end the perceived politicisation of the SC’s original jurisdiction and give Parliament a role in judicial appointments comparable to that of legislatures in other democracies”, the claims did not justify “changing the judicial structure in a manner that is glaringly inconsistent with Pakistan’s obligations under international law”.

It also acknowledged that the Supreme Court had “encroached into roles of Parliament and other institutions”. However, it also noted that with the 26th and 27th amendments, the Parliament failed to ensure these “deficiencies” were fixed in line with judicial independence.

“Instead, the 26th and 27th Amendments have led to systemic judicial capture by other branches of the state and the dismantling of the rule of law in the country,” the ICJ stated.

It was found that the ruling coalition had “exploited” the public’s grievances over the functioning of courts in a “self-serving manner” to control the judiciary.

“As a result, even the highest courts of the land in Pakistan no longer serve as a check on the executive or the Parliament and their function as avenues for redress of victims of human rights violations is seriously impaired,” the report stated.

Call for comprehensive review

In its recommendations, the report appealed to the government to begin a comprehensive review of the amendments and their implementation in “light of international law and standards”, particularly under the framework of Pakistan’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and by holding “transparent and broad” public consultation.

It suggested that the government engage in international cooperation, including seeking technical assistance from the UN special rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers and inviting them for a country visit.

In its recommendations to the JCP, the ICJ called on it to revise the criteria for judicial appointments in accordance with international law, standards and best practices.

It further suggested: “Ensure the published criteria are the sole basis for nomination of judges to the FCC, the SC, the high courts and constitutional benches of the high courts.”

It also called on the commission to establish a transparent procedure for appointments and publish reasons for each appointment that “demonstrate the published criteria are being implemented in practice”.

It also called on the JCP to refrain from transferring a high court judge without their consent.

In its recommendations to the Supreme Judicial Council, the ICJ said: “Define ‘inefficiency’ in a manner that is consistent with international standards to only mean serious incompetence that renders judges unfit to discharge their duties.”

For the Special Parliamentary Committee, which has the power to nominate the chief justice of Pakistan, the report called for it to adopt “clear and transparent criteria and procedures” for the appointment of the SC and FCC top judges and to publish the reasons for each selection.

Lastly, the report urged the FCC, the SC and the high courts to “interpret and apply the provisions of the 26th and 27th Amendments, to the greatest extent possible, in a manner consistent with the independence of the judiciary as guaranteed by Article 14 of the ICCPR”.

World.title: US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
World.content:
Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph.

The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media.

Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power.

His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration.

Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on Jan 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality.

Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics.

Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot — as some allies had hoped.

He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018.

The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous.

Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed.

The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs.

“Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday.

“We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.”

Brooklyn roots

Raised in Brooklyn’s working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012.

Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022.

He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020.

As speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and stand second in line to the presidency behind the vice president.

But he would face a formidable task in managing a Democratic coalition spanning centrists and an increasingly assertive left flank.

His party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their agenda against a president who retains veto power.

Jeffries’s nomination contrasts with a more competitive leadership contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran party chief Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.

Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, but acknowledges he is the underdog. Senate Democrats will elect their leader in early December.

Republicans chose their own congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune in the Senate.

World.title: PTA says submarine cable fault may cause internet connectivity issues
World.content:
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) said on Wednesday that a fault in one of the international submarine cable systems may result in users experiencing internet connectivity issues.

“One of the international submarine cable systems, the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5), has reported a fault at about 11km from Pakistan’s shore, which may cause some internet users to experience intermittent connectivity issues and a decline in service quality,” the authority said.

“Transworld Associates is coordinating with the SMW5 consortium to identify the root cause of the fault and determine the estimated time for restoration,” it added.

In the meantime, the authority said internet traffic was “being rerouted through alternative international links to minimise the impact and ensure service continuity to the greatest extent possible”.

It added that it was in close coordination with the concerned stakeholders and will “continue to monitor the situation to facilitate the earliest possible restoration of normal internet services across the country”.

On July 1, a fault in the SMW5 international submarine cable system caused widespread connectivity issues in Pakistan. The fault was resolved on July 3.

World.title: Asean secretary general to undertake working visit to Pakistan from Nov 18-20
World.content:
The secretary general of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), Dr Kao Kim Hourn, will undertake a working visit to Pakistan from Nov 18 to 20, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday.

In a statement, the FO said that Kao was visiting the country at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

“This will be the first high-level visit to Pakistan from the Asean Secretariat in over two decades. Pakistan has been an Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner since 1993 and a member of the Asean Regional Forum since 2004,” the statement said.

It said that during the visit, Kao would call on Pakistan’s leadership.

“The two sides will review the full range of Pakistan–Asean relations, explore avenues for enhanced cooperation and exchange views on regional and global developments of mutual interest,” it said.

“The visit underscores Pakistan and Asean’s shared commitment to deepening and diversifying cooperation,” the statement added.

Earlier this year, Dar attended the 33rd Ministerial Meeting of the Asean Regional Forum in Manila, where he drew attention to key challenges threatening peaceful coexistence and stability across the world, listing the Kashmir dispute and India’s threats to Pakistan’s share of water among them.

Last year, seven Asean member countries held a joint meeting with Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh to explore new avenues of investment and economic cooperation with Pakistan.

World.title: Pakistan conducts successful launch of Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile: ISPR
World.content:
The Pakistan Army on Wednesday successfully launched the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, according to the military’s media wing.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said, “The Pakistan Army successfully conducted the launch of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, marking another significant milestone in strengthening Pakistan’s national defence capabilities.

“The weapon system is equipped with advanced navigation and propulsion systems and is capable of engaging targets at long range with high precision and lethality at supersonic speed,” it said.

It added that the missile would “significantly enhance the operational flexibility and strike range of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command, further strengthening the country’s overall conventional deterrence and defence posture”.

According to the statement, the Army Rocket Force Command commander, senior officers from the armed forces, scientists and engineers witnessed the launch.

It added that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, and the services chiefs congratulated the team on the successful launch.

They appreciated the dedication and commitment of all personnel involved in achieving this significant milestone in Pakistan’s defence development, the statement concluded.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar termed the development a “testament to the relentless hard work, skill and innovation of our teams in strengthening Pakistan’s defence capabilities and national deterrence”.

“The entire nation takes immense pride in their unwavering commitment to keeping the country strong and secure,” he said.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful launch. According to the interior ministry, he said that the launch represented a “significant advancement in the defence sector”.

“The successful test of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile marks a major milestone in the country’s defence capabilities,” Naqvi said.

Earlier this month, the Pakistan Air Force performed a successful flight test of the country’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az.

ISPR said that the flight test marked “another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defence capabilities”.

World.title: Nawaz hails his govt’s ‘serious’ work on AJK development as PML-N charts 100-day plan
World.content:
The PML-N said its top leadership, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, discussed development and reconstruction in AJK with the region’s president and premier, both of whom belong to the PML-N.

Addressing the meeting, Nawaz hailed the efforts of his government in the development of AJK, particularly the formulation of a 100-day programme to develop the region.

“This is the first time, I think, that a party’s government and the party’s leadership are on the same page regarding participating in AJK’s development with such seriousness,” he said, adding, “I have never seen such enthusiasm before.”

He highlighted Amir Muqam, Rana Sanaullah, Chaudhry Tariq and Khawaja Saad Rafique’s efforts in particular.

He also expressed appreciation for the contributions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, who he said had provided green buses for Muzaffarabad and Mirpur as well as clinics on wheels and laptops. “This is a very good spirit and we should appreciate it,” he said.

In addition, he highlighted that PM Shehbaz had also agreed to allocate resources to the programme, calling it a “very good thing” that there was so much passion surrounding the decisions to contribute to the region’s development.

Nawaz regretted that there were previous governments in AJK that had “not cared” about it at all and forgotten its promises to the public. He highlighted the contrast between then and the current time.

He added that, now that Gillani had become the prime minister in the region, he felt that he himself had become prime minister.

“The zeal that is in my heart, I see that very same zeal inside his heart,” he said, adding that he would continue to visit AJK from time to time and hold meetings to discuss development.

Nawaz also said that while he had been premier, and Raja Farooq Haider had been AJK PM, “our sole focus used to be on development”. In particular, he noted that one project that they wanted to launch was for a motorway from Muzaffarabad to Mirpur.

“With this, your entire Azad Kashmir interior would have opened up […] If there ever was a finest project in the history of Azad Kashmir that was ever conceived, it was that project,” the PML-N leader said, requesting PM Shehbaz to now give that project “top priority”.

He also lamented that motorways linking major cities were unable to be completed during his premiership although they had reached the so-called “tender stage”, which if completed would have created motorway linkages all the way from Peshawar to Karachi. He expressed that he would ask for this to be completed as soon as possible.

He recalled other highlights of his premiership, including a highway built from Gwadar to Quetta in Balochistan and a Rs50 billion motorway built from Gilgit to Skardu in the Gilgit-Baltistan region. He also called attention to the Lowari Tunnel project in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which he said had been left incomplete for about 50 years before he ensured its completion during his time in government.

In contrast, he added, “for the last 15 years, a party’s government has continued to form inside KPK, and what did they achieve there?”

Regarding the country’s progress, he said, “Once our GDP rate was 7.5 per cent, and inflation was at a minimum. The electricity tariff used to be, I don’t know, one or two rupees.”

He also noted that during his tenure, the rupee had not broken 104 against the dollar, while the interest rate was 5.25pc and reserves had reached $24bn.

“It has risen from 24 to 27 (billion) today. But instead of 27, had this disruption not occurred, these would have been above 50 today […] way above 50,” he added, referring to the PTI government’s tenure during which they had returned to IMF loans and hiked the interest rate to about 22 or 23 per cent.

Highlighting that his government had also ended hours of loadshedding within three years, he also commended PM Shehbaz for having set up power plants with great speed.

Nawaz called for a “comparison” of major political parties in TV discussions when talking about performance, saying, “The PML-N’s performance is better than the performance of all parties in the country.”

He commended the work of PM Shehbaz, Punjab CM Maryam and DPM Dar for their “great work”, calling for all the party’s successful projects to be replicated in AJK. He added that this would benefit “the people of Azad Kashmir, its residents, the children, the elders, the poor, and all segments of society”.

During the meeting, the party’s leadership discussed public welfare, development projects and the implementation of election promises with the AJK leadership, according to a post by the party on X.

Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz also attended the meeting, along with federal and provincial ministers, including Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

The federal and Punjab governments reaffirmed their commitment to supporting AJK’s development and prosperity, the party’s statement added.

PM Shehbaz, AJK PM Gillani and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also addressed the meeting, with their remarks live-streamed on state media.

PM Shehbaz noted that the PML-N was provided a chance to serve the people of AJK in the July elections.

He assured Gillani that the federal government would provide “whatever financial assistance” is needed to fulfil the plans announced by the AJK PM.

“Whatever you need from the Centre regarding this, we are here,” he said, noting that Deputy PM Ishaq Dar, Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam and others had made great efforts for AJK’s progress.

The premier announced that a Daanish School will be inaugurated next month in Bhimber to provide good quality education to deserving children.

The prime minister paid tribute to the “martyrs of occupied Kashmir” and those who were currently in jail there.

“Their sacrifices will soon bear fruit,” he said, affirming that the government and the people of Pakistan will continue their political and moral support for India-occupied Kashmir.

In her remarks, CM Maryam noted it was “good to see” that her father had begun giving practical shape to his pledge to remain involved in AJK’s journey of development.

She said the Punjab government was ready to help in AJK’s development if needed.

Maryam expressed confidence that the AJK premier’s government would ensure the completion of various projects, including the Apna Ghar scheme, electric buses, Cath labs and Clinics on Wheels, ahead of their schedules.

“They have given timelines for when we are starting based on those timelines. I think they should also keep the timeline of when they will finish and deliver it in mind because that is more important,” she said.

The Punjab CM termed skill development a “low-hanging fruit”, adding that a model was ready to train and assist people so that a person can earn their own living after six months of training.

She highlighted her regular monitoring of projects through the Punjab Information Technology Board, stressing that 24/7 monitoring was extremely important.

“I think you should pay a lot of attention to law and order reforms, police reforms,” Maryam said.

She emphasised that the people of AJK should “feel that such a government has come into power that is not only doing work for their progress, for their development, but is also accessible to them”.

“This accessibility is very important; it changes everything. Secondly, you should speak outside with the public very often and give them confidence about what you are doing and what you want to do,” the Punjab CM advised the AJK PM.

In his address, Gillani highlighted planned development projects over the next 100 days, including the launch of Suthra Kashmir and ‘Apni Chhat Apna Ghar’ programmes in the region.

He said that the government guest houses would be revamped completely in the next six months to promote tourism, and that beautification projects for Muzaffarabad and divisional headquarters would be completed within three months.

He noted that Green Bus services had been launched in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad and would roll out across six cities for improved travel facilities. Additionally, he highlighted plans to launch two separate scholarships for those who could not afford higher education for their children: one for government universities and one for top private universities. He also highlighted the Daanish schools and university being built in the region, thanking the premier for his generosity in the initiative.

“The infrastructure of three cities where Green Buses will operate — Muzaffarabad, Bagh, and Mirpur — will be completed in 100 days,” he said. “These are all the things that will ensure the people’s trust in the government is restored.”

Later in the day, PM Shehbaz inaugurated the reconstructed Rathoa Haryam Bridge in AJK by unveiling the plaque, the PM Office said.

Nawaz, along with the AJK president and premier, was also present on the occasion.

On the occasion, the prime minister said the completion of the Rathoa Haryam bridge is a major milestone for development and prosperity in the region.

He noted that the bridge would ease commuting and transportation between Mirpur and its surrounding areas.

He further observed that the project would provide local residents with modern travel facilities and boost commercial and economic activities in the region.

The visit comes nearly three months after the PML-N came to power in AJK in August, following phased elections in which Nawaz played an active role in the campaign.

Speaking in Muzaffarabad during the election campaign in July, Nawaz had asserted that the city should be transformed into the most beautiful city of Pakistan. He said that whatever CM Maryam was doing in Lahore and other cities of Punjab should also be “copied” in Muzaffarabad and other cities of AJK.

He had also promised AJK residents that every development project would be implemented and that PML-N would resolve “all the issues” if it won the elections.

In his speech, he had also cautioned his party leadership in AJK that he would visit AJK every three months to see whether the party’s manifesto was being implemented.

After PM Gillani’s election, Nawaz handed him a comprehensive 100-day reform agenda, stressing that essential public services, including healthcare, education, sanitation and reliable roads, were basic rights of the people of AJK and should also reach remote areas rather than remain confined to major urban centres.

World.title: 15,000-tonne LPG cargo arrives from Abu Dhabi under new policy to ease shortages
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The government on Wednesday said it received the first cargo of 15,000 tonnes of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from Abu Dhabi after it introduced policy changes earlier this month to arrange imports through state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to ease supply constraints and contain rising prices in winter.

In a statement, the Petroleum Division said that SSGC LPG Limited (SSL) – a subsidiary of the state-run Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (SSGCL) – had imported a record 15,000 metric tonnes of LPG cargo, the largest of its kind that berthed at Engro Vopak Terminal Limited (EVTL).

The shipment marks the first “major” import under the new LPG guidelines aimed at ensuring the availability of LPG at affordable rates for the public, the statement said.

The SSL arranged the cargo through competitive bidding at a price yet to be disclosed by the company.

Petroleum Division officials said the company would publish details of the pricing components on its website in a couple of days, but claimed the SSL import had already dented market prices by Rs100 to Rs120 per kg.

Separately, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervez Malik informally told journalists that another shipment arranged by Pakistan State Oil (PSO) was on its way to Karachi and would reach over the next two days, followed by others.

He said LPG availability would address the pricing distortions in the market.

On November 3, the federal cabinet approved new LPG pricing guidelines to enable SOEs to play a leading role in securing LPG supplies.

Previously, formal sector companies had exited imports due to regulatory constraints that prevented them from recovering procurement costs.

Under the cabinet decision, the government also directed state-owned companies to lead LPG imports and strengthen the country’s supply chain, especially in winter.

The increased influx of LPG is expected to further improve market availability, ease supply constraints and help bring prices down through greater product availability.

It will also enhance supplies to hilly, remote and far-flung areas, particularly during peak winter season.

A welcome ceremony was held at Port Qasim to mark the arrival of the shipment, with Special Secretary Petroleum Mirza Nasir ud Din Mashood as the chief guest.

SLL Managing Director Jawad Ali Khan, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) Senior Executive Director (LPG) Sarmad Aslam, and other senior officials were present at the occasion, according to the statement.

Speaking at the ceremony, Petroleum Special Secretary Mirza Nasiruddin Mashood said that the prime minister and the petroleum minister had issued directives to take effective measures to ensure LPG availability to the public.

He said the arrival of the record shipment marked a new era for the LPG sector and would further strengthen the country’s supply chain. He congratulated SLL on this achievement.

The government said the LPG pricing change was meant to create competition in the market through procurement of LPG by four SOEs on government-to-government (G2G) and business-to-business (B2B) arrangements and flood the market.

LPG, often described as the poor man’s fuel, has been in short supply even before the onset of winter as western borders faced disruption. Resultantly, unscrupulous elements started taking advantage by selling the product to consumers at Rs700 to Rs800 per kilogramme against Rs295 per kg maximum price set by Ogra for November.

LPG pricing

The government is working with the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) to provide LPG to the “most deserving and vulnerable” at Rs300-350 per kg through a subsidy mechanism to be funded by a new account arising from the differential between LPG import parity price and auction of local LPG produced by refineries and exploration and production companies under a clawback mechanism.

The SOEs — PSO, Pakistan LNG Ltd, SSL and Parco-LPG — have been engaged with various suppliers from Saudi Arabia and Oman for LPG supply.

Apart from imports through SOEs, the cabinet has also decided to put an end to the existing quota system for domestic LPG enjoyed by influential groups, and local producers would auction their LPG in 5 to 10 tonnes through a competitive process under Ogra and the Petroleum Division’s supervision.

Under the new arrangement, these SOEs would announce the base price —freight-on-board (FOB) linked with the Saudi Aramco contract price (CP) — along with other costs including the premium, freight (CFR), insurance, incidental costs and import taxes actually incurred by PSO or any other SOE in the preceding month (monthly average landed cost) on their websites.

Ogra would stop issuance of price notification for local (or imported) LPG forthwith.

The local producers shall be entitled to this producer price only discovered through auction and the differential between the producer price (Saudi CP-linked FOB) and the base price of PSO shall be deposited in the fund account to subsidise poor consumers through BISP.

The private sector has been demanding an end to the Saudi-CP-linked price, considering that most of the imports originate from other countries, including Iran and Oman.

In case of no imports by SOEs in a month, the preceding month’s premium, incidentals and taxes shall apply with the current month’s CP on the pattern of diesel and petrol pricing.

There would be an increase in margins for LPG marketing and importing companies to Rs50,000 per tonne floor instead of the existing Rs35,000 per tonne as inflation adjustment since the 2016 LPG policy.

Ten per cent of the indigenous LPG produced by exploration and production (E&P) companies, refineries and other producers shall be allocated to state-owned marketers at producer price, to guarantee supply to the northern areas, Gilgit-Baltistan and other remote, hilly and hard-to-reach areas for supply through cylinders or already installed LPG air-mix plants.

The remaining 90pc will be allocated, through a transparent monthly auction with a floor price equal to 5pc of import-parity price of PSO, to prequalified bottlers to increase investment in infrastructure and storage, cylinders in circulation, geographical reach and operational capability, with safeguards against cartelisation.

Ogra would be required to convene product review meetings on the pattern of oil products to ascertain supply-chain position, including the import plan and winter stock planning, and instruct specific import volumes to SOEs to ensure demand and supply balance in the market, especially during the winter.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run.
